Measured offline on the shipped map with the verifier's own column average, `masonry` read std 7.125 counts and correlation **-0.684 at HALF the tile**, which is the signature of one cycle per tile: a light half and a dark half, laid 19.6 times across the cella. The arithmetic is countable and no single number was wrong -- ten blocks each drawing one independent hash, averaged four at a time down a column, cannot be flat by luck. **The fix is four terms because three of them have to be:** P(u) is linear in the per-block draws with a null space containing only per-course constants, so per-block contrast and a flat column average are mutually exclusive on a ten-block tile. > **RN-845 to RN-850 (2026-08-03): NOTHING DREW A SECOND BODY, AND NOW IT DOES.** The previous lane in this seat hit a hard stop and named it exactly: of 207 exports none returned a body position, `kCinderOrbitRadiusM` lived in `sim_world.h`, which is not in the wasm build, and **it refused to transcribe the constant**. Physics did not copy the number, it MOVED it into `orbital.h` and published `of_body_state` / `of_body_facts` (ABI stays 22, both symbol-detected). This lane is the consumer. **Cinder from Forge measures 1.9099477 degrees at 1.2000000e7 m, and Forge from Cinder 5.7319680 degrees**, matching the predecessor's own sizing arithmetic to four figures, which is the acceptance criterion it wrote down before anything could be drawn. `docs/screenshots/RN845_cinder_in_forge_sky.png` is the in-game view, `RN845_forge_from_cinder.png` is a blue-and-tan half Forge in a black sky over lit regolith, and `RN845_cinder_approach.png` is Cinder at **23.06 degrees from 1,000 km** with craters at several scales and a terminator full of rim shadows. All three are lit and textured; none is a form-only or untextured pass.
>
> **THE MOON IN THE SKY IS MADE OF THE MOON YOU LAND ON, and that was the one decision that could not be taken back later.** The disc's height and albedo are baked from the body's OWN `SurfaceOracle` through a second `PlanetBody` handle, which is what `createBodyHandle` exists for (D-006). A procedural crater texture would have produced an identical first screenshot and would have been a second authority on the shape of a world. The albedo is **`TerrainShader`'s own `terrainAlbedo` rule** rather than the raw biome palette, and that is not decoration: a hard ten-value classifier at 2.4 km per texel made Forge's coastlines read as dithered speckle, because there is no value between Ocean and Plains for a bilinear filter to interpolate through. `terrainAlbedo` is continuous in the height field, so it antialiases the classifier for free and makes the disc read as terrain rather than as a biome map. It costs no extra oracle calls.
>
> **A LAMBERT SPHERE DOES NOT LOOK LIKE A MOON, AND THAT IS PHYSICS RATHER THAN TASTE.** Lambert falls off as cos(incidence) and drives the limb of a full moon to black; the real Moon is very nearly uniform across its disc, because regolith backscatters. An airless body therefore gets **LOMMEL-SEELIGER**, renormalised so its sub-solar point matches Lambert's, so the choice of law is not also a brightness change. A body with air keeps Lambert plus a limb and a twilight arc. **Which law runs is `AtmosphereProfile::present()`**, the same authority RN-840 used, so a third body authored in `atmosphere.h` gets the right disc with no render-side edit. Under ART-DIRECTION.md a grey disc is a failure, and the falloff was the defect: no amount of texture would have fixed a Lambert ball.
>
> **THE TWILIGHT ARC WAS WRONG THREE TIMES AND EACH FRAME NAMED THE NEXT FAULT.** See RN-847; the third fault is the one worth carrying, which is that the term had no SHAPE and no amount of retuning its brightness was going to give it one. Both of its numbers are the body's own air and neither is written down: its width is /core's atmosphere ceiling and its falloff is the scale height MEASURED from `_of_atmo_density` at 5600 m. /core's profile turns out to be a clean exponential (rel 0.4095 at 5 km and 0.16768 at 10 km both give 5599 m), so a two-point fit is a fit to the right shape rather than a number that merely looks measured.
>
> **PLANETSHINE HAS AN HONEST SOURCE NOW, I MEASURED IT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND I DID NOT WIRE IT.** Full Forge delivers **1.837e-4 of the sun's irradiance** to Cinder's ground and new Forge 7.455e-6, a 24.6x swing across the phase, and the colour is BLUE (r 1.67e-4 against b 2.08e-4) because Forge's measured mean reflectance is 0.110 and mostly ocean. Sanity by size: earthshine on our own Moon is about 1e-4, and Forge subtends three times the angle Earth does from the Moon. **At the shipped exposure that is worth about 0.9 of an 8-bit count, and Cinder's night ground already sits at p50 15.93.** RN-846 has the four controls and the four-point sun sweep that say the 15.93 is a CONSTANT and is none of this domain's four ambient mechanisms.
>
> **THE NEGATIVE CONTROL IS BYTE-IDENTICAL ACROSS TWO BINARIES, and getting there needed the harness measured first.** Two isolated trees from the SAME commit (62289f1) differing only by my five files and fifteen lines of `Systems.ts`, the SAME wasm forced into both by sha (they had drifted apart, because another lane rebuilt the wasm twice while this one ran, and comparing across that would have been a false result), and the same camera. **The harness is only deterministic about one run in three:** three repeats of one binary at one configuration gave two hashes, and three repeats of the other gave three. So byte-identity is not an available standard per run, and the honest control is the pixel delta against the RUN-TO-RUN NOISE. Noise floor 3.39 to 3.60 per cent of pixels at max delta 48 to 54; **my build under `?skybodies=0` against a build containing no Celestial code at all: 3.31 to 3.68 per cent at max delta 50 to 55, i.e. inside the floor**; and in the runs where the harness was deterministic the two are **BYTE-IDENTICAL across the two binaries** (`cmp` clean). The feature itself, for scale, moves 6.54 per cent of pixels at max delta 220, four times the noise's worst.
>
> **R17 IS NO LONGER BLOCKED ON AN INSTRUMENT, AND THE ANSWER IS STILL "DO NOT CHANGE THE DEFAULT" - FOR A DIFFERENT AND BETTER REASON THAN LAST TIME.** RN-843 refused a new `RELIEF_GRAD_UV` because its metric counted CONTRAST and could not tell "less artefact" from "less signal". A subagent built the anisotropy instrument that was owed, validated it (isotropic mottle 0.066, pure corduroy 0.9993, a factor of 15), priced the foreshortening trap that would otherwise have handed it three quarters of its own answer, and swept three sites. **The null holds and the mechanism is now split in two.** On Cinder the support really does stamp its own scale and the artefact would yield to it. On Forge's Beach it will not yield at any value, because at a ONE-TEXEL support, which is as close to the field's own gradient as the knob reaches, the term still reads 0.94 directional: **the corduroy is in `of_ground_relief` under biome 1's channel weights, not in the shader constant.** See RN-850. That escalates Beach out of this file entirely.
>
> **A FINDING THAT BELONGS TO A LOOK-DEVELOPMENT LANE AND MAY BE THE MOST USEFUL THING HERE.** Cinder's night ground is a flat p05 12.93 / p50 15.93 at sun elevations of -0.35, -0.60 and -0.85 alike, i.e. it does not care how far below the horizon the sun is. It survives `?lamp=0`, `?iblground=0` and `?bouncelit=0` unchanged and `?horizonocc=0` moves it 0.71 of a count. It is not a tone-curve lift: with the camera actually pointed at the sky, the airless night sky is **exactly 0.00 across 144,000 pixels, p05 to max**. So there is a constant ambient on the terrain that no mechanism this domain has built accounts for, it is seventeen times the size of the planetshine that is supposed to be the physical reason a lunar night is not black, and until it is dealt with **no night-lighting change on Cinder can be measured at all**.
>
> **RN-840 to RN-844 (2026-08-03): THE MOON WAS RENDERED WITH EARTH'S AIR, AND EVERY AVAILABLE FIX FOR THAT WAS A DELETION.** World-gen landed Cinder with a nine-rung crater ladder reaching 1.8 m and the renderer erased all of it: `Boot.ts` called `forgeAtmosphere(body.radiusM)` unconditionally, so the ONLY body-derived input to the sky was the RADIUS. Cinder got Earth's Rayleigh coefficients over a 200 km ball, a blue sky, and an aerial perspective that veiled every crater in a white sheet (`RN840_A_before_atmoson.png` is a total white-out at 12 km, worse than the pair that raised this). The only remedy on offer was `?atmos=0`, which does not model a vacuum, it DELETES THE SKY BOX, and the box carries RN-64's ground shell, which is the entire ambient of every stock material. So the moon had exactly two states, fog bank and black lithograph, and no way through the middle. **The split that fixes it is one boolean becoming two:** `atmosphere` (does the box exist) and `scattering` (does the integral run). An airless body keeps the box, paints black above the horizon and lit regolith below it, and `?atmos=0` stays byte-for-byte what it always was. **Both halves are driven off /core's own `AtmosphereProfile::present()`**, read through `_of_atmo_density` and `_of_atmo_space_altitude`, the same two exports the map already draws its air line from, so a third body authored in `atmosphere.h` renders correctly with no render-side edit at all. **NO WASM REBUILD WAS NEEDED OR DONE**: both exports were already shipping.
>
> **The shadow fill was TWO defects, and neither one alone does anything, which is why the isolation table matters more than the result.** `skyView = 0.5 + 0.5*dot(n, up)` is the sky-view factor of a facet on an INFINITE TANGENT PLANE, so a 21 degree slope is told it sees 96.7 per cent sky and 3.3 per cent ground. On a body with air that error is invisible, because `skyAmb` is large and the two channels are interchangeable in magnitude; **in a vacuum `skyAmb` is exactly zero and the whole ambient rides on the channel the flat-plane assumption had already set to nothing.** Separately, the bounce term's RADIANCE carried the fragment's own `shadow`, so a shaded fragment was told its entire neighbourhood was shadowed too. Measured at Cinder's spawn, 16 degree sun, geometric mask, four arms: shadow p50 **4.00** (neither) then **4.00** (occlusion only) then **5.21** (bounce only) then **8.43** (both). A **2.1x** that neither term reaches alone, because one sets the WEIGHT of the ground channel and the other its RADIANCE, and a weight times zero is zero. Sunlit p50 moved 85.91 to 89.97, **+4.7 per cent**, so the fill is a fill and not a brightening. Both controls are exact and both were measured red.
>
> **R17 AND REID'S "CONTOUR LINES SCRIBBLED ON THE GROUND" ARE ONE BUG, CONFIRMED, AND IT IS NOT THE AMPLITUDE.** `?groundreliefamp=0` removes 95.5 per cent of the high-pass tail on Cinder's crater floor and 99.2 per cent on Forge's forest floor. The specular lobe is innocent (37 per cent against relief's 95.5) and there is no sign flip: both bodies show a two-sided perturbation, and Cinder only READS bright because dark regolith under a low sun leaves the positive lobe the only half with anywhere to go. The cause is `RELIEF_GRAD_UV = 0.0311`, derived from `RELIEF_FINE_M = 0.45 m` on the stated claim that 0.45 m is "the finest authored wavelength". **It is not**: `of_ground_relief.png` carries gradient energy down to the texel (3.5 mm) and its channels decorrelate at 0.12 to 0.39 m. At the shipped support the finite difference is **86 to 96 per cent uncorrelated with the field's own gradient**, and on Beach it goes outright NEGATIVE one octave further out. The support is stamping its own 113 mm length scale onto the lighting, which is the corduroy in `RN843_beach_t32.png`. **I promoted the constant to a swept uniform and then REFUSED to ship a new default.** See RN-843 for why.
>
> **Two findings that belong to other lanes and may be the most valuable things here.** (1) **Forge's height field is EXACTLY CONSTANT below about a 32 m sample spacing** at the spawn: 100 per cent of centred differences read exactly 0.000 at 1 m and 2 m baselines, with sampled heights identical to the millimetre (4667.789 three times running), against Cinder which varies at every scale down to 1 m. `RN843_beach_t0.png` shows what that looks like with the relief bump off: a featureless plane with rocks lying on it. **The relief bump is the only surface detail Forge's ground has**, which is why its defects read so loudly, and why "turn it down" was never an available fix. (2) **`--sundot` is NOT dead**, contrary to the report I was handed; it is solved ONCE at boot against the SPAWN's local up, and a probe that teleports keeps the phase and loses the elevation. See RN-844.

> **RN-761 to RN-772 (2026-08-02): THE SPACE STATION, AND THE THREE NUMBERS IT WAS ALMOST BUILT AGAINST WERE ALL WRONG.** There was no space station in this project: no asset, no build script, no client loader. This is the first one and it is the largest asset in the game by every measure. Blender only, no browser, no build, no dev server; Reid's 4200 untouched. **(1) RN-761, DERELICT, AND IT IS AN ARGUMENT RATHER THAN A MOOD.** An OCCUPIED station implies crew, working hatches, powered lights, a faction and a reason they tolerate you, which are four systems nobody has built; a wreck is COMPLETE AS SHAPE, which is the only thing an art lane can deliver end to end. It is also the subject ART-DIRECTION.md asks for: on a derelict, wear and damage and asymmetry have a CAUSE, so they are authored as consequences instead of as decoration. The one concession is that some light strips still work, because a sealed hull in orbit has no ambient inside it and a corridor a player cannot see is not one they can be asked to walk down. **(2) RN-762, THE SECTION, AND ALL THREE OF ITS NUMBERS MOVED AFTER THE FIRST DRAFT WAS WRITTEN.** The brief said 2.50 m wide with 2.50 m headroom and an eye at 1.66. The physics lane measured at 400 km and **all three were wrong: gravity is 3.49886 m/s2 against 9.659126 at the surface, so the jump apex is 2.319915 m and the walker's topmost collision sample sits 1.65 m above the feet, and a player in a 2.50 m corridor jumps into the ceiling with 1.47 m to spare.** Headroom is now **4.00 m** everywhere a player stands. **Width is essentially free**, because the walker is a LINE to structures (three point samples at 0.15 / 0.9 / 1.65 m, no radius) and nothing binds it laterally, so width is now chosen for PROPORTION: 2.50 under a 4.00 ceiling is 1:1.6 and reads as a shaft, and **3.00** restores a corridor. Eye is **1.62** (`CAPSULE.eyeHeightM`), which is what the wall furniture and the interior camera are placed against. **A LOOK-DEV NUMBER AND A PHYSICS NUMBER CAN DISAGREE AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS NEGOTIABLE**; this is the first asset in the project whose form was set by a gameplay measurement rather than the other way round. **(3) RN-763, THE SHAPE, AND WHY THE INTERIOR IS FLAT WHEN THE HULL IS ROUND.** 66.97 x 61.69 x 23.67 m: a 6.40 m spine 66 m long, three branch modules (crew, hold, and the reactor that failed), a 16.20 m hall with a gallery at 5.10 and a dome at 12.00, a docking collar forward, a torn rim aft, two solar wings, two radiator banks, two truss runs and two dishes. The interior is FLAT WALLED inside a ROUND hull and the gap between them is the service void, which is what a real pressurised module is and which buys three things at once: a flat wall and a flat ceiling make down unambiguous where a barrel vault does not; the tube-to-tube saddle at every junction is a shape nobody can author without a boolean and the interior never has to describe it, because it describes a DOORWAY; and a missing void panel becomes a first-class detail with real hull ribs behind it. **NO ROTATING HABITAT RING IS WALKABLE, and that is a physics constraint rather than a preference**: down is the planet radial, `deckUnder` solves where a line THROUGH THE PLANET CENTRE exits a box so the parameter it returns IS a radius, and a non-radial up breaks it along with `climbGate`, `slopeGate`, `escapeRock` and the voxel collider. The station holds nadir attitude and gets real inverse-square gravity for nothing. **(4) RN-764, TWO RENDER STEMS, AND IT IS A CULLING FACT RATHER THAN TIDINESS.** `Station_*` is the hulls and appendages, `StationInt_*` is the fitout. The hull is visible from a kilometre and the fitout only from inside it, so a client drawing the station at range drops the interior with no hole in the silhouette; `hull_tube` builds both skins as ONE closed manifold so that split is possible at all. `check_shadow_lod` groups ladders by stem (RN-567), so the two are measured independently, which is the honest way round. **(5) RN-765, THE LADDER IS SHADOW-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION, AND THAT IS THE ONE THING THIS ASSET DOES THAT NO OTHER LADDER IN THE PROJECT DOES.** Every greeble is placed by `Shell.part` or `Panel.part`, both of which take their proud height from `machine_form.LAYER` and never from the call site, so **a tier's worst-case deviation is exactly the shallowest layer it keeps and it is decided by ONE number before a triangle exists.** LOD1 drops everything at or under `hinge` (52 mm) and LOD2 at or under `gauge` (163 mm), the latter KEEPING `duct` on purpose because `scorch_ribs` is on that layer and it is the structure standing inside the breach, where the hull it would otherwise be measured against is the part that is missing. One build function emits all three tiers, so re-authoring LOD0 re-authors LOD1 in the same edit. **MEASURED, AND THE TWO STEMS LANDED DIFFERENTLY: `StationInt_LOD1` reads 52.80 mm against cascade 1's 56.25, earns c1 and c2, and puts the interior on a marginal 2.0x, which is the target. `Station_LOD1` reads 139.87 mm and `Station_LOD2` 278.37, so the hull earns cascade 2 only and sits at 3.0x.** The layer arithmetic predicts 52 and the hull measures 140, so something on the hull is still dropped without a host near it; four such causes were found and fixed and a fifth is open. It is stated here rather than rounded off, because 3.0x against 2.0x on the largest asset in the game is worth one more attribution pass, and the bins are already taken: **blender x[-32,-24] y[-8,0] at 139.87 and x[8,16] y[0,8] at 133.04**, which are the hull placards and doublers whose SPAN or ARC crosses a window boundary their CENTRE clears. It is the same both-extents defect as RN-766 at the two call sites that still guard only their midpoint, and it is one predicate away. **`StationInt` has no LOD2 deliberately: a coarse interior tier's only available saving is deleting the interior, which is the brief's own caveat (a tier whose whole saving IS an omission can never be admitted to a cascade), and the honest name for that saving is not drawing it.** **(6) RN-766, AND IT OUTRANKS THE ART: 'BLOCK IN EVERY FEATURE OVER 56 mm' IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT.** The deviation metric is the distance from an LOD0 vertex to the tier's SURFACE, so a DROPPED part is cheap only when something the tier KEEPS is near it. Four times running, a part was dropped correctly by layer and still measured metres, and every one was the same defect wearing a different hat: **a greeble with no host under it.** 3,976.57 mm was a doubler plate emitted inside the hall's own hull window, where the spine does not exist at all, because the predicate guarding it was written for a BRANCH junction (which leaves two arcs behind) and the hall leaves nothing. 1,976.71 mm was a 5.68 m strake skipped by a MIDPOINT test while overhanging a window by 2.61 m. 940.86 mm was `scorch_ribs` inside the breach. 315.00 mm was that same doubler again, hosted along its length and running 13 degrees off the end of the arc ACROSS it. **A midpoint test is not an overlap test, and a part has two extents.** All four are art bugs FIRST (every one was floating in space where nobody could ever see it) and shadow bugs second, which is the useful half: a gate meant for shadow cost found invisible geometry no render would have shown. **(7) RN-767, A CLAIM IN MY OWN DOCSTRING THAT WAS FALSE.** `Shell.part` justified flat boxes on a cylinder for greebles 40 mm to 800 mm wide, which is true and is not the whole story: a chord of width w on radius r stands off by about w^2 / 8r, so a **2.10 m livery stripe on a 3.20 m hull floats 172 mm** and a **3.80 m cargo door on a 5.00 m hull floats 349 mm**, both visibly and both as deviation when dropped. Wide parts are now emitted CURVED as `hull_tube` arcs, and the threshold is derived rather than chosen: 12 mm of stand-off, comfortably inside cascade 0's own 15.47 mm texel, so a curved part and a flat one are indistinguishable to every consumer of the file. **(8) RN-768, THE COST OF THE TWO-STEM SPLIT, PRICED WHERE IT LANDS.** The hall's consoles and placards are bolted to the hull's inner skin, which lives in the OTHER stem, so dropping a 24 mm placard measured 839.96 mm: **a greeble mounted on a surface its own node does not contain has nothing to be measured against.** The hall wall fitout is therefore tier invariant, and the real fix is NAMED and not taken: a lined hall (panels the way the corridors have them) would put a host in the right node, let the fitout tier like everything else, and let the hull carry real window apertures behind it. That is a form change and it belongs in the pass Reid steers. **(9) RN-769, COLLISION IS THE FEATURE AND IT IS 57 PROXIES.** Floors, walls and ceilings as separate convex boxes, because one enclosing box cannot describe an interior and would make the station a solid lump. Three physics facts govern the set and the third is the one nobody would have guessed: the walker can stand on a proxy with NO new code (`KinematicBody` already takes the higher of the terrain floor and `StructureBodies.deckUnder`, measured 264 of 264 ticks grounded at 400 km with feet spread 0.000000 m); floors get an exact slab solve; and **R48, THERE IS NO CEILING AUTHORITY IN THE WALKER**, only `free()` with three point samples 0.75 m apart, so a horizontal proxy thinner than 0.75 m fits between two samples and the player passes clean through it (measured with a thickness control: at 0.3 m the player jumps through the ceiling and stands on the roof, at 0.8 m the rise stops dead at 0.849904 m). **Every overhead proxy here is 0.80 m against a 0.12 m visible ceiling panel**, which is a proxy being coarser than the thing it stands for, exactly as a machine's box proxy is coarser than its hull. The whole set comes out of ONE function, `collision_boxes()`, with a `PROXY_SET` constant carrying all three answers the physics question could have had, so the philosophy can change without a rendered triangle moving. Hall walls are TWELVE chords and not eight: the sagitta at r 8.10 over 30 degrees is 0.276 m of slack against 0.616 at eight, and that number is a decision rather than a default. **(10) RN-770, THE BUDGETS, ARGUED FROM WHAT THIS IS.** Every precedent in `contracts.json` was priced against MULTIPLICITY (the smelter's raise cost 22 x 4, the spider's 8 rigs x 4). **This asset's multiplicity is ONE, and the frame it is drawn in has no terrain LOD0 ring, no 3.2 M detail cards per km2 and no factory, because it is in orbit.** LOD0 16,904 against a 17,600 cap and 69,684 of 72,000 across five render nodes; 57 box proxies at 684 of 700; 11 materials of 12. At the full 4.0x the exterior plus the interior would be 130,600 triangles, 13 to 24 per cent of RN-71's measured 555k to 1.0 M surface frame that this asset never shares. **(11) RN-771, `pivot_mode: none`, WHICH IS HONEST AND NOT A FREE PASS.** The useful origin for a free-flying body is the spine axis at the hall centre, which is the artificial-gravity datum; `centre` would demand the AABB centre land there to 5 mm, and the AABB is set by the wing tips, the docking collar and the torn rim, so honouring it would force symmetric extents on an asset whose brief is asymmetry. `validate_glb` prints `none (view model)` for this branch, which is a stale message rather than a wrong check; a `free` mode is flagged to Admin and deliberately not taken mid-flight. **(12) RN-772, `render_station.py`, AND IT EARNED ITS KEEP THREE TIMES IN ONE SESSION.** Exterior, INTERIOR at standing eye height on the client's own 60 degree vertical FOV with the lens derived through `lens_for` and `sensor_fit` pinned VERTICAL, and a scale mode with the 1.80 m player body standing in the corridor and again in the hall. **Three shots came back as white slabs and each one was the instrument working rather than failing**: the hold eye stood 0.6 m from a SHUT bulkhead, the corridor scale camera 0.4 m behind another one, and the hall scale eye at r 8.51 inside a wall at r 8.10. That is render_launch_pad's 'a camera inside a box renders its inside' three times in one afternoon, and it is exactly why the mode exists: **an interior judged from outside is an interior judged by its silhouette, and a corridor with a beam across it at 1.85 m looks perfect in one.** **INVARIANTS: `validate_glb --all` 52/52 with the new asset passing all 17 applicable checks; `check_coplanar` 52 assets 0 over allowance, with space_station at 0 same across all five render nodes and absent from the allowance table; `check-proxies` OK at 52 assets, 141 proxies and 190 sockets, declared sets matching shipped sets both ways; space_station.glb rebuilds byte-identical; NO SHARED FILE WAS OPENED AT ALL, not `of_lib.py`, not `texgen.py`, not `surfaces.json`, not `Surfaces.ts`, so every other asset's bytes are untouched by construction rather than by a rebuild control; `contracts.json` edited as literal text and never through a `json.load`/`json.dump` round trip and never with `git checkout --`; zero em dashes verified in Python per file.** **NOT DONE, NAMED: THIS IS A FORM PASS AND EVERY VALUE ON IT IS A PLACEHOLDER.** It uses only roles that already exist (`Steel`, `SteelDark`, `SteelLight`, `Accent`, `Hazard`, `Iron`, `Coal`, `Plate`, `Rubber`, `Glass`, `EmissiveState`); there is no station surface family, no hull or deckplate tiling albedo and no per-vertex material channel bound, so the torn insulation is currently `Hazard` and reads as caution tape rather than as gold MLI, and the whole asset is one value. **The wreck also UNDER-READS from the two hero bearings**: the breach is one module and side-on to a single bearing, so `x34` and `xside` show a tidy station and only `xbreach` shows a wreck. **The hall's viewports are exterior-only** (nothing here cuts a hole, so the glass stands proud of the hull and a player inside sees plain skin), which is the same problem the lining fixes. The corridors carry no damage at all. Client side: nothing loads this file, `StructureView` pins every structure to `MachineBatch`'s single `panel` material, and per-part response needs `bakePartMat` plus `injectPartMat` from whatever hook the loader ends up using. Screenshots `RN761_form_{x34,xside,xaft,xbreach}`, `RN761_form_{spine_fwd,spine_aft,hub,hold,hab}`, `RN761_form_{scale,scale_hub}`.

> **RN-741 to RN-742 (2026-08-02): THE ETCHED SQUIGGLES WERE A DISCONTINUOUS DERIVATIVE, AND THE HOST ROCK LEAVES `coarse` BECAUSE NO TEXEL IN `coarse` IS STEEPER THAN 27 DEGREES.** **(1) RN-741, THE SQUIGGLES, AND THE IRONY IS THE FINDING.** The relief bump took `dFdx` OF THE SAMPLED HEIGHT. That field is authored with SHARP CRESTS on purpose, because RN-78's symmetric attempt photographed as choppy water and `groundtex.py` asserts per-channel asymmetry to prevent it. A sharp crest is a SLOPE DISCONTINUITY: its screen derivative jumps, the normal flips hard along every crest line, and that prints a hairline exactly there. **So the asymmetry that earns this texture its place is the same asymmetry that breaks its derivative**, and the fix therefore must not touch the field. It also explains the sweep nobody could make work: RELIEF_DEFAULT came down 0.30 to 0.12 to 0.08 chasing this, and **scaling a discontinuity does not remove one**. THE FIX SMOOTHS THE GRADIENT, NOT THE FIELD: the slope is differenced over a fixed TILE-space support (`RELIEF_GRAD_UV` 0.0311, a quarter of the finest authored wavelength, 0.112 m at depth 14) instead of over one pixel, while the SMOOTH tile-UV-to-screen mapping keeps `dFdx` because uv and position are linear across a triangle and their screen derivatives are exact. **Nothing rough is differentiated in screen space any more and nothing smooth is sampled twice.** Two extra fetches of a texture already bound and already sampled at that coordinate, inside a branch whose condition is a bare uniform. **MEASURED on a settled-frame framehash pair, restore bit-exact at both sites: Hills the change moves 10,073 of 14,400 tiles and the EXTREME EXCURSION HALVES, peak 59.21 to 29.75, while the mean magnitude falls only 22 per cent, 3.912 to 3.048; Beach peak 102.51 to 68.48 with the mean down 11 per cent. The spikes were the defect and the body was the relief.** THE NAMED FAILURE MODE WAS THE REAL RISK: band-limiting a gradient makes a term weaker as well as smoother, so 'the squiggles are gone' and 'the relief is gone' produce the SAME happy screenshot. `probes/reliefgrad.js` therefore measures THREE states and publishes a survival ratio: **0.779 at Hills and 0.888 at Beach**. Commit `d19be6d`. **(2) RN-742, THE `stone` FAMILY, AND THE MEASUREMENT IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT.** `coarse` has a mean normal tilt of 7.69 degrees with a **MAXIMUM of 27.12**, and **0.0 per cent** of its ORM green below 0.60. No texel in it is steeper than 27 degrees and no part of it is ever smooth, so host rock wearing it can neither glint nor catch a raking sun, and that surface is most of every boulder, the whole spire and all the scree. `stone` measures **17.18 / 74.31 with 29.3 per cent under 0.60**, an effective band of 0.58 against 0.22. Split out for bark's reason exactly. **THE FREQUENCY SPLIT IS THE HAZARD THIS SUBJECT INVITES AND IT WAS PROVED RATHER THAN ASSERTED**: normal carries fracture facets 2 to 8 cm, albedo carries ONLY pigmentation at 10 to 20 cm off different seeds, ORM has its own band keyed on crest against crevice. Pearson r between the albedo's luma and the heightfield is **+0.0665**, against the shipped `panel` albedo's +0.2892, the ORM's own AO at +0.5556 and an identity albedo at +1.0000. **It is structurally not cobblestone rather than tuned not to be: `_stone_albedo` never reads `height` or `aux` at all**, so dust in the low ground is its own 10 cm field, and the AO already darkens what the normal dents. Drawing it a third time IS cobblestone. **(3) THE PALETTE PAIR, AND IT COSTS NO GEOMETRY.** `rock_form` has painted shear and fracture planes with the DARK role since RN-242, so `Rock` 0.90 to **0.94** (weathered, dustier, and the level can rise because the family now supplies the variation) against `RockDark` 0.92 to **0.80** (a fresh fracture face is the one part of a rock not dulled by weather, so it is the part that can still catch a raking sun) makes the pair say weathered against freshly broken: **a 0.14 authored separation where there was 0.02**, on faces that were already painted and were simply drawing the same material. > **RN-681 to RN-690 (2026-08-01): THE SHADOW-CASCADE LOD. THE 4x IS REAL, THE RULE IS DERIVED FROM EACH CASCADE'S OWN TEXEL RATHER THAN PICKED, AND IT BUYS 1.55% AND NOT 87%, BECAUSE THE BIG MACHINES' AUTHORED `_LOD1` IS TOO CRUDE TO BE ADMITTED TO ANY CASCADE.** The brief arrived with an arithmetic to verify rather than inherit (`2276 + 192 + 2x48 = 2564` against 2368, "+0.65% instead of +22.4%, a factor of 34"). It does not survive measurement, and the reason it does not is the whole value of this pass. **(1) RN-681, THE RULE, MEASURED AT BOTH ENDS.** A cascade may draw the CRUDEST tier `L` for which `dev(G,L) <= 1 texel`. `texel(c)` is published by `ShadowRig.update` out of the same `(2 * r) / mapSize` it already computes for texel snapping, so there is exactly one copy of it: **15.47 / 56.25 / 210.94 mm** on the high tier, re-derived rather than remembered (a probe asserts cascade 0 is 15.47 to 0.05 mm, so a split or map-size change that moved it fails loudly instead of silently retiering every asset). `dev(G,L)` is the **measured** one-sided maximum distance from LOD0's surface to tier `L`'s, computed at build time in `render/ShadowLodMeasure.ts` from the merged, world-baked geometries the batch is about to hand the GPU, not from the source primitives. One texel, not two, because section 2.1 records the PCF kernel as one texel and the map already quantises every silhouette to that grid, so the error introduced is bounded by quantisation that is there anyway; two texels is the Nyquist alternative and `?shadowlodk=2` measures it rather than arguing it. **This is why a picked constant would have shipped a defect:** "cascade 0 draws LOD1" is exactly what the brief proposed, and cascade 0 is 15.47 mm while the smelter's `_LOD1` is **325 mm**. Whole-measurement boot cost 73 to 102 ms, published as `measure.ms` so it is not a hidden regression. **(2) RN-687, THE MACHINE NUMBER, which five asset lanes are blocked on and which is the opposite of the estimate.** Per-asset, maximum surface deviation of the shipped tiers, against the three cascade texels: smelter `2276/192/48` dev **325 / 396 mm**, assembler `2976/276/36` dev **640 / 400**, generator `532/140/36` dev **559 / 559**, miner `488/180/36` dev **280 / 566**, box `564/192/36` dev **126 / 300**, belt `148/72/12` dev **20 / 70**, wall `108/72/12` dev **0 / 45**. **Every one of the five big machines is refused at all three cascades and keeps the full 4.00x multiplier.** It is not one greeble: **36.6% of the smelter's LOD0 surface** sits further from `_LOD1` than cascade 1's 56.25 mm texel (p50 35 mm, p95 204 mm), and 45.8% of the assembler's. **The raise did not break this** and that matters for who owns the fix: the pre-raise 592-triangle smelter's `_LOD1` already measured **264.8 mm**, so the ladder was never shadow-safe, it was authored for screen DISTANCE and this is the first thing that ever asked it for a world-space error bound. **The lever is now numeric and it belongs to the asset lanes:** author `_LOD2` under **210.94 mm** to earn cascade 2 (smelter 9,104 to 6,876, 3.02x); author `_LOD1` under **56.25 mm** to earn cascades 1 and 2 (to 4,792, **2.11x**); cascade 0 is unreachable for a 192-triangle stand-in, because 15.47 mm on a 3.2 m machine is 0.5% of its size, so **2.11x is the floor for a three-rung ladder** and a fourth rung at roughly 600 to 800 triangles hitting 15.47 mm would reach about 1.41x. `__ofShadowLod.report()` publishes every asset's `devMM` beside every cascade's `texelMM`, so an author can read their own margin without a rendering lane in the loop. **(3) RN-685, THE DEFECT THAT MADE THE FIRST VERSION A COUNTER WITH NO IMAGE, and it is the reason the invariant table was taken before the claim was written.** `BatchedMesh.onBeforeRender` opens with `if ( ! this._visibilityChanged && ! this.perObjectFrustumCulled && ! this.sortObjects ) return;` and `setGeometryIdAt` (BatchedMesh.js:1200) does not set that flag. `MachineBatch` turns both other conditions off, so the first version swapped every machine's geometry id three times a frame and three re-read none of them: **262,958 swaps against a frame delta of +63 triangles**, where the belts alone should have paid 13,780. **The restore half would have been worse than a missing saving:** `onBeforeRender` clears the flag as it rebuilds, so after the last cascade the live ranges are the CRUDEST tier's, and the eye pass would have taken the same early-out and drawn cascade 2's mesh to the player. Both halves now invalidate explicitly, in one place, with the citation, and only when a swap actually happened so an untouched batch keeps three's early-out and stays bit-exact. **(4) RN-686, THE INVARIANT TABLE, four scenes, both ways, ONE BINARY per pair, `?shadowlod=0` as the control.** `drawCalls / programs / triangles / geometries / textures / vramMB`: **rn15** 66/43/**1,070,337**/53/104/104.2 against 66/43/**1,070,807**/53/104/104.2 (**-470, -0.044%**); **Forest** 45/55/**591,673**/53/106/104.2 against the identical row (**0, 0.000%**); **Plains** 70/44/**2,594,794**/53/106/104.2 against 70/44/**2,596,674** (**-1,880, -0.072%**); **built factory (78 buildings, 13 smelters, 65 belts)** 71/45/**961,060**/54/103/104.2 against 71/45/**976,217**/54/103/104.2 (**-15,157, -1.553%**). **Five of the six invariants do not move at any scene.** Draw calls cannot move because the tiers live inside the same `BatchedMesh`, and `info.geometries` cannot see them for the same reason: a `BatchedMesh` is one geometry however many sub-geometries it holds, so the extra rungs are about 0.3 MB of vertex and index buffer that no published counter resolves. It is therefore exact for `MachineBatch` (culling off, a factory is always near) and an over-count for `NodeBatch` (culling on, a 620 m ring is mostly outside any one cascade): the built factory agrees to **5.7%**, and **Forest reports 12,274 against a frame delta of exactly zero** because every node whose tier the rule would have changed is culled out of the cascade that would have drawn it. A counter that cannot see the cull will report a saving no pixel receives, which is the same failure as (3) wearing different clothes. **(6) RN-684, `NodeBatch` gets the shadow saving ON TOP of its distance LOD**, taking the coarser of the two so a node already at LOD2 for distance is never promoted back by a near cascade. It pays little and the trees are why: `tree_conifer` Full deviates **925 mm** at LOD1 and 3,126 mm at LOD2, `tree_broadleaf`'s leaf row 1,070 mm, so the crowns are refused everywhere and only boulders and spires (58 to 110 mm at LOD1) are ever admitted, in cascade 2 only. **(7) RN-682, THE LAUNCH PAD HAS BEEN DRAWING A FIFTH CLAMP COLUMN SINCE IT SHIPPED, standing at the launch mount where the rocket goes, which is the exact thing its own comment forbids.** The test was `c === clampCol` over `root.children`; `launch_pad.glb` has ONE root node (`LaunchPad`) with everything beneath it, so `root.children` is a list of one and the identity test could never match, while `getObjectByName` searched the whole subtree and found a grandchild. Now excluded by name over the whole subtree. A second bug of the same shape was introduced and caught in the same pass: an unanchored `/^LaunchClamp_LOD\d/` matches GLTFLoader's per-primitive children (`_LOD0_0`, `_1`) as well as their Group, and gathered every clamp triangle **twice** (216 where 108 is right); the pattern is anchored. **(8) RN-683, the pad's 704 triangles of dead LOD payload are now loaded and are STILL dead, and the measurement says why.** `LaunchPad_LOD1` and `_LOD2` both deviate **14,090 mm** from LOD0, because they delete the tower (`socket_status` sits at y = 27.55 m). Against a 210.94 mm cascade that is a factor of 67. **The payload is not usable as authored**, and this is failure mode 3 (a thin feature vanishing from its own shadow) at 14 metres. `LaunchClamp_LOD2` at 210 mm IS admitted to cascade 2. **(9) RN-688, THE SHADOW-QUALITY PAIRS AT GRAZING SUN.** The three ways this goes silently wrong are named in `ShadowLod.ts` BEFORE any pair was taken: a shadow edge that moves, a contact shadow that detaches so the object reads as floating, and a thin feature whose shadow disappears. The structural cost is exact rather than estimated: three draws one call per `BatchedMesh` per pass and there are `1 + cascades` passes, so splitting a pool into `F` families costs `(F - 1) x 4` draws, i.e. **+8 per pool for panel/coarse/flat or +4 for panel/coarse**, up to +24 across the four pools on a measured 66 to 71 against a 150 target. The second cost is the one that decides it: `MachineBatch`'s slot model assumes ONE mesh, so a split has to fan a logical slot across N meshes in lockstep and touches `acquire`, `place`, `release`, `setGeometry` and the FS-40 read-backs `drawnKeyAt` and `matrixAt`. **Recommendation to Admin: option (c), split `panel` from `coarse` only and leave `flat` in `panel`** (the status chip's fragment shader overwrites `diffuseColor` and adds emissive, so a wrong normal map on 2.3% is nearly invisible), **as its own pass with its own probe**, because forcing it into a pass whose whole purpose is recovering triangles would spend the recovery on draw calls. Option (b) from the file's own comment (select per family off `aRole`) needs two normal maps, two ORMs and a second metre-scaled UV varying bound to one material, plus replacing three's `<normal_fragment_maps>` chunk; that is the ">1 texture per batch" case the brief says to route rather than force.

Admin asked for the recovered budget "the way they price", and totals are the wrong shape for that question: what an author needs is **what one more triangle on LOD0 costs the frame**, which is `1 + (the number of cascades that still draw tier 0)`. **(1) RN-691, THE MARGINAL MULTIPLIER.** Raising LOD0 grows the eye pass and grows every cascade still drawing tier 0; a cascade drawing a fixed `_LOD1` or `_LOD2` does not grow at all. In the machines lane's own units, 22 instances in a 660,385-triangle frame at a 3.0% ceiling gives 900 triangles of frame cost per instance, so the affordable LOD0 raise is **225 triangles at 4.0x** (which reproduces their number exactly, and confirms it), **450 at 2.0x**, **900 at 1.0x**. **(2) RN-692, THE ESTIMATE IS CORRECTED, AND ONE HALF OF IT IS CONFIRMED.** `2276 + 192 + 2x48 = 2564` requires cascade 0 to draw `_LOD1`; cascade 0 is 15.47 mm and that `_LOD1` is 325 mm, so it is refused, and the real figure is `2276 x 4 = 9104`, **3.55x the estimate**. The predicted "+0.65%, a factor of 34" is **+22.4%, a factor of 1.00**: the raise costs exactly what it cost before this pass, because the smelter earns nothing from it. **The +22.4% half of their arithmetic is confirmed independently and was right.** What moved is not the smelter's price, it is that the price is now a published per-asset property with three numeric targets against it. **(3) RN-693, `?shadowlodk=2` MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED, and it is a LOOK decision for Admin rather than a perf one.** At one texel the built-factory saving is **-15,157 (-1.553%)**; at two texels, the Nyquist floor, it is **-50,260 (-5.148%)**, a factor of 3.3. Almost all of the difference is one admission: the smelter's `_LOD2` at 396 mm fits cascade 2's doubled 421.9 mm budget, taking that machine from 4.0x to 3.0x marginal and its affordable raise from 225 to 300 triangles. **It ships at one texel** because one texel is the quantisation the shadow map already has and two is a claim about what the eye will accept at 80 to 300 m, which is not a claim a perf measurement can settle. Subject box moved 7.94% / 1.16% / 1.95% (forest / rocks / factory), all reading as silhouette-edge noise of the same character as foliage alpha dither. **The controls:** the first box sat under the debug overlay and was measuring live frame-timing text (mean delta 46 to 52 counts against 15 to 19 in the subject, which is the tell that it was glyph edges); the second sat under the "GETTING STARTED" quest panel for 22% of its area. The three targets are **15.47 mm to earn cascade 0, 56.25 mm to earn cascade 1, 210.94 mm to earn cascade 2**, as maximum surface deviation from LOD0, and the ladder that hits them is not the distance ladder: `NODE_LOD1_M` / `NODE_LOD2_M` is authored for screen size, and this is authored for a world-space error bound.

THE HANDS WERE SIZED AGAINST A FIELD OF VIEW THE CLIENT DOES NOT USE, THE PLAYER HAS NEVER WORN A SURFACE MAP AT ALL, AND TWO OF THE THREE GEOMETRY VERSIONS WERE KILLED BY LOOKING AT THEM.** **(1) RN-641, THE FOV, AND IT OUTRANKS THE ART IN THIS PASS.** `ASSET-SPECS 4.2` says the client runs "roughly 70 degrees" vertical; `render_check.py`'s `eye` view and `rig_common.py`'s entire hand-distance argument are both derived from it. **`CameraRig.ts` constructs every camera INCLUDING `vmCam` at `fovDeg = 60`, and `setFov` has no caller anywhere in `web/src`.** At the authored 0.62 m hand distance the visible frame height is `2 * 0.62 * tan(30) = 0.716 m`, not the 0.868 m the 2026-07-27 sizing comment computed, so **the hands are 21 per cent larger in frame than the arithmetic that placed them believed**, on the one asset whose only recorded complaint was ever that it was too big. `render_player.py` is a new rig that cannot repeat it: the lens is **DERIVED** from a vertical FOV with `sensor_fit` pinned to `VERTICAL`, because Blender's `AUTO` fit follows the LARGER output dimension while `three.PerspectiveCamera.fov` is always vertical, so an `AUTO` lens silently reframes when the resolution changes. It prints its transform every run (RN-456's rule), which matters because **`render_check.py` sets no view transform at all and therefore renders every asset in this project under Blender 5.0's AgX.** **(2) RN-642, THE TEN COPLANAR PAIRS, BOTH CAUSES, TO ZERO, AND THE ROW REMOVED.** Attributed by reading the shipped bytes, not the source: `OF_EmissiveState`/`OF_Plate` at glTF Z = 0.2000 x2, and `OF_Plate`/`OF_Suit` at Y = 1.8000 x8. **Cause one:** the chest state light is 0.020 deep centred at y -0.190 and the pack it sits on is 0.095 deep centred at -0.1525, so both front faces are at -0.2000 exactly; two front faces on one plane, both surviving the cull, and the one that loses the coin toss is the state light, which is the part of a chest pack a player actually reads. Centred at -0.196 it is proud by 6 mm and still 14 mm buried at the back. **Cause two is the interesting one:** the comm fin's top face was authored to land exactly on the helmet crown at z = 1.800, with a comment explaining that this is what keeps the declared 1.80 m height bone-and-crown driven. **That reasoning was correct about the envelope and simply never required the two surfaces to TOUCH.** Dropped 3 mm; `dims_xyz_m` is unchanged to the digit at both ends. `ALLOWED["player/player_body"] = 10` is deleted and the asset is now held at 0 alongside the four clean machines and the three rocket assets. **(3) RN-643/644, TWO FAMILIES, AND THE FIRST VERSION OF EACH FAILED ITS OWN GATE.** `Suit`, `SuitDark` and `Plate` are used by `build_player_body.py`, `build_player_fp_arms.py` and `build_armour_set.py` **and by nothing else in the repo**, checked by grep before anything moved, which is what makes re-pointing them a player-only act. They were on `panel`, and panel encodes MANUFACTURE OUT OF PLATE (seams, rivet rows, a weld bead), which is the wrong FACT about a woven garment in exactly the way `coarse` was the wrong fact about bark. **`suitfab`** (512 px, 0.5 m tile, 1024 px/m) is a plain weave built from two crossed `_hair_layer`s, because a weave is two anisotropies at right angles and `_hair_layer` is the only anisotropic primitive in the file; the over-under checker at the thread pitch is what makes a highlight run ALONG a yarn instead of sitting on a lattice of dots. **`suitplate`** (384 px, 0.4 m tile, 960 px/m) is brushed grain, micro-pitting, shallow dings and eleven authored scratch segments, with ONE wear mask driving albedo, roughness and metalness together. **THE MEASUREMENTS, all against section 2.1 item 4's 0.15 requirement and panel's measured band on the same roles:** effective roughness `panel x Suit 0.046` and `panel x Plate 0.030` **to `suitfab x Suit 0.224`, `suitfab x SuitDark 0.242`, `suitplate x Plate 0.268`**; effective **metalness `suitplate x Plate 0.456`**, which is the answer to section 2.1's complaint that "the only varying metalness in the game is 8.9 per cent of one map". Normal mean tilt `suitfab 21.7 deg`, `suitplate 16.8 deg`, against panel 10.5 and bark 22.8. **(4) THE TWO GENERATOR MISTAKES, BOTH WORTH THE SPACE.** *Summing independent noise fields NARROWS the distribution*, which is the central limit theorem doing exactly what it says. suitplate v1 summed four fields into its wear mask and measured an effective metalness band of **0.074, WORSE than the 0.406 of the panel family it was replacing** and a straight regression on the single number the family was built to fix. Paint does not thin, it CHIPS: the physically right shape is bimodal, so the mask is now a `_smoothstep` whose knee is **centred on the raw median**, measured rather than guessed (a knee at 0.20..0.46 against a raw median of 0.25 left 95 per cent of the plate fully coated and the roughness band at 0.115). Second: *amplitude and pitch are not independent*. suitfab v1 ran a 5 mm thread pitch at 0.62 of the height and **rendered as knitted wool**, because at 5 mm a player counts twenty-four threads across the back of a glove and anything countable reads as hand-knitting. 3.3 mm at 0.34 of the height, with the normal strength down 17 to 2.4, is a weave you sense without resolving. **(5) RN-645/646, THE FORM, AND THE RENDER KILLED TWO VERSIONS.** The cuff was a 150 mm `OF_SuitAccent` tube, and SuitAccent is 2E7DBE, a saturated primary that under the corrected framing is the largest block of colour in the first-person frame; it could NOT be re-surfaced out of the problem because SuitAccent is shared with `rocket_common.py` and the lander. **A pressure glove attaches with a metal locking ring**, so it is one now (OF_Plate, two courses, three bayonet lugs at 40/160/280 degrees rather than four on the axes), and the accent survives as a 6 mm index stripe: same silhouette, one hundredth of the saturated area. The knuckle guard was one unbroken 9 cm slab, which has one silhouette and one specular and is why it read as a chrome tile glued to a mitten. **Version one of the replacement authored four plates at 12.5 mm half-width against 10.5 mm half-thickness with the long axis running forward: near-round forward-pointing wedges, which from a camera sitting behind the hand rendered as CLAWS and were worse than what they replaced.** **Version two added a dark carrier strip for them to be riveted to, authored WIDER than the plates meant to hide it and tapering to a point, which rendered as a dark triangle down the back of the glove.** Version three is four flat pads at 3.6:1 aspect on `seg=8` (an octagon puts one broad facet parallel to the back of the hand where a hexagon puts two at a slant, so the plate catches light instead of reading as a dark chip) and no carrier at all. **A part authored to explain another part is only worth its triangles if it is actually hidden, and "mostly hidden" is a claim that has to be rendered rather than assumed.** **(6) THE FINDING THAT CHANGES THE SLICE: THE PLAYER HAS NEVER WORN A MAP.** `PlayerRig.ts` does not import `Surfaces.js` and there is **no `attachSurface` call for the player anywhere in the client**; the four consumers are `PropLibrary`, `MachineBatch`, `NodeBatch` and `SpiderFlock`. `surfaces.json` has said `Suit -> panel` since DW-35 and `surface_preview.py` honours it, so every studio render of this asset since then has shown maps **the game does not apply**. The client half is therefore owed and is the first item of part 2. Priced at **zero DW-10 slots** (stock `MeshStandardMaterial`, shared textures; the ledger stands at 4 ShaderMaterial + 3 hooks against a cap of 5). **(7) THE PER-PART CHANNEL: INHERITED, AND NOT NEEDED HERE.** RN-491 to RN-498 landed while this pass ran, so `PartMaterial.ts` is committed. **The player does not need it.** That mechanism exists to recover per-part roughness, metalness and a `bare` flag through a MERGE, and `PlayerRig` does not merge: it adds `gltf.scene` verbatim, so the body already draws as 8 real materials and the arms as 6, each with its own authored roughness and metalness. The named use case (fabric against a glass visor against metal fittings) is already satisfied by construction. It becomes relevant only if the body is ever merged to cut 8 draws to 1, which is a separate trade. **(8) THE PRICE, MEASURED.** FP arms **1,740 to 2,284 triangles against an UNCHANGED 2,600 budget: no raise requested**. The arms are the cheapest triangles in the game and it is worth writing down why: `Avatar.ts` creates them with `castShadow: false`, they live in `scenes.viewModel` drawn by `vmCam` in its own pass, and `ShadowRig` adds shadow-casting lights to `scenes.near` only, so they appear in **zero** of the 1 or 3 cascades. 6 draws, one pass. The body pays the opposite: 8 colour draws plus 8 per cascade, and `frustumCulled = false` means it is never culled out of any of them, so **a triangle on the body costs 4x what the same triangle costs on the arms**. Body LOD0 unchanged at 2,320. VRAM: suitfab 4.19 MB + suitplate 2.36 MB = **+6.55 MB**. **(9) INVARIANTS.** 44 bones and 27 bones untouched; all 14 and all 12 clip names untouched and every published impact frame untouched (DW-34); skin weights **1.0000 to 1.0000** on both; `rest_pose` 2.69e-07 and 3.36e-07; `anim_t0` green on 14 and 12 clips. **`validate_glb --all` 51/51 before and after.** `check_coplanar` 0 over allowance with **both player assets at 0 same**. **Both .glb rebuild byte-identical**, and all 13 pre-existing family PNGs rebuild byte-identical under the texgen additions, which is what proves the regeneration launders nothing. Clip binding proved by picture: `RN647_fp_sheet` is six frames of FP_Swing_Pickaxe as baked copies, all six distinct, none in rest and none collapsed to origin. Zero em dashes verified in Python per file. Commit `7f07eeb`. **(10) NOT DONE, NAMED, AND ONE OF THEM IS A CROSS-LANE BLOCK.** **`texgen.py` CANNOT BE COMMITTED BY THIS LANE**: it carries the industrial lane's uncommitted `_panel_albedo` (RN-553) alongside my two families, texgen has **no per-family build** and rewrites `surfaces.json` and every PNG wholesale, and their family currently fails texgen's own level check at mean 0.9659 against the 0.15..0.85 rule. > **RN-601 to RN-621 (2026-08-01): THE ANIMATION PASS. THE BITE THAT HAS BEEN OWED SINCE THE CREATURE WAS BUILT, AN IMPACT FRAME PUBLISHED AS AN OFFER BECAUSE NOTHING EXISTS TO READ IT, AND A WALK WHOSE PLANTED FEET WERE BEING DRAGGED BY THE BODY'S OWN SWAY.** Reid: "work on the spider animations." **(1) RN-601 to RN-612, `Spider_Bite`, 0.7000 s, 43 authored frames, IMPACT AUTHORED FRAME 22 = RUNTIME TICK 21 = 0.3500 s.** Published in the vocabulary `web/src/player/AnimGraph.ts` already uses for the player (`SWING_CLIPS[kind].impactTicks`), and printed by `build_spider.py` on every build so it lands in a build log rather than only in a doc that can go stale. **THE DISTINCTION THAT MATTERS: IT IS PUBLISHED, NOT READ.** `EnemySwarm.step` charges `damagePerSecond * dt` on every one of the 60 ticks a second that `Creature.biting` is non-empty; there is no windup, no telegraph, no per-attack cooldown and no discrete bite event anywhere in `enemies.h` or the client, so **there is nothing in the sim for an impact frame to gate today** and the number is an offer in the shape combat would need, not a reading of a requirement. The clip's shape follows `build_player_body._swing` deliberately (wind at `impact - 10`, settle at `impact + (n - impact)//3`): a player's pickaxe and a spider's fangs are the same event seen from the two ends, and a second authored shape for it would be a second authority on what a strike looks like. **THE AMPLITUDE IS 15 DEGREES OF HEAD AGAINST 7 OF THORAX, and that ratio is structural rather than taste**: all 24 leg bones are children of `Thorax`, so a degree of thorax pitch drags eight coxa heads through an arc about the thorax pivot and **no rotation downstream can undo a parent's TRANSLATION**, while `Head` is the only bone on the rig with no leg children and is therefore free. The brace pairs cancel the thorax pitch by negating the very list that authored it, which is `clip_idle`'s mechanism and means the two cannot drift. **TWO CORRECTIONS THE RENDERS CAUGHT, NEITHER OF WHICH A REST POSE COULD SHOW:** the first strike drove the head 34 degrees down, which rotates the chelicerae UNDER the carapace, so the fangs were plainly visible on the wind-up and hidden at the one frame that has to read as contact, and it was wrong about the target as well, since a spider bites a player or a building and both stand at roughly its own height; and the first version put the front pair back on the ground at the impact frame, and **eight legs on the floor is the pose of a creature doing nothing**, so they now reach furthest forward exactly when the fangs land, because a spider pins with the front pair and bites what it is holding. **THE FANGS DO NOT OPEN**, stated as a rig limit rather than left to be discovered: the chelicerae are geometry weighted to `Head` and there is no bone to spread them with. An L/R chelicera pair is the one place two more bones would buy something a clip cannot, and it is priced and not taken. **(2) RN-613 to RN-618, THE WALK, AND THE DEFECT WAS REAL.** `Spider_Walk` authors its stance as `rig_common.ramp`, a straight line, because a planted foot must travel backward at CONSTANT speed: that docstring calls a sine "the skate" and the whole clip was built around avoiding it. **The shipped bytes did not do that. Instantaneous stance speed swung 1.7936 to 3.2200 m/s about a mean of 2.5096, a worst deviation of 0.7222 m/s or 28.89% of the declared 2.5, INSIDE a window that is supposed to be constant.** **WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT: the MEAN was right the whole time, to 0.4%.** Every check that existed divides one arc by one duration, and **no arithmetic of that shape can see a ripple inside the window it is averaging over.** This is DW-34's shape again, an authoring defect that no render shows and only the exported curve reveals. **THE MECHANISM, ATTRIBUTED RATHER THAN CORRELATED:** `clip_walk` yaws the Thorax +/-2 degrees for body sway, and because every leg is a child of Thorax that sway was added to all eight feet whether or not they were standing on the ground. The Thorax yaws a measured +/-1.9979 degrees once per cycle, a peak rate of 0.27386 rad/s, and the four feet stand 2.1917, 2.3240, 2.5009 and 2.6171 m from the thorax head, predicting peak drags of 0.6002, 0.6365, 0.6849 and 0.7167 m/s against **measured 0.6076, 0.6446, 0.6924 and 0.7222: agreement within 1.2% across four different lever arms.** A perturbation proportional to distance from a pivot IS a rotation about that pivot, so the mechanism is identified rather than correlated, and it is the same sentence DW-34 already had on file: the foot path was right and the hip was moving underneath it. `clip_idle` already solved this exact problem on this exact rig by cancelling the thorax sway on every coxa; `clip_walk` never did. The fix is that cancellation, through ONE function both readers call, because two independent restatements of one body motion is how the drag arrived. **RESULT: worst intrinsic slip 28.89% to 5.73%, i.e. 0.7222 to 0.1434 m/s. Per leg: 24.31 to 1.14, 25.79 to 2.64, 27.70 to 4.52, 28.89 to 5.73.** Everything the gait is supposed to be is unchanged: **alternating tetrapod holds by the strict definition** (two clusters exactly 0.5000 apart, observed groups `{L1,L3,R2,R4}` and `{L2,L4,R1,R3}`), duty 0.5333, **feet on the ground never fewer than 4 of 8**, mean stance speed 2.4952 to 2.5059 against a declared 2.5. The 5.73% residual is named and left standing rather than tuned away. **A HYPOTHESIS TESTED AND REFUTED, recorded because the next reader will have it too:** that `pose_clip`'s default BEZIER handles were bowing the straight ramp. Rebuilding the walk with `interpolation="LINEAR"` produced a **byte-identical .glb** and identical measurements to four decimals, and the change was reverted rather than left standing as a no-op wearing a comment that claims a fix. **(3) RN-619, THE INSTRUMENT, `tools/blender/gait_check.py`, NEW, AND IT WAS WRONG FIRST.** It opens the shipped .glb and reports duty factor, stance speed, slip, gait clustering, feet-on-ground, inter-leg clearance and loop closure, with **no tuned threshold anywhere that turns a measurement into a verdict**, and the two places a judgement is unavoidable print the observed sets beside the literal definition being applied. Version one read `pose_bone.tail` for the Tibia and reported the foot at **z = 1.04 m when the authored tip is at 0.02**: glTF has no bone tails, it stores joints as nodes, and **Blender's importer SYNTHESISES a tail for every leaf joint.** Four numbers said so at once (duty 0.5583 against an authored 0.5000, stance phases at 0.4667 rather than 0.5000, implied speed 1.4880 against a declared 2.5, and **a stance direction that REVERSED mid-stance, which a planted foot cannot do**), and 1.4880/2.5 * 2.10 puts the tracked point at radius 1.55 m, between the knee and the foot, which is exactly a mid-bone invented tail. It now picks the foot vertex out of the DEFORMED MESH, per leg, by greatest horizontal radius among the vertices that leg's Tibia dominates, and **prints the chosen index and its rest position so the choice is auditable**. It deliberately does NOT copy `FOOT_R`, `FOOT_Z` or the azimuth table out of `build_spider.py`, because a control whose geometry is a copy of the thing it watches is this project's catalogued failure and it fails in the direction that looks like a real defect. Rest-tip check after the fix: radius 2.4061 against an authored 2.40, z 0.0219 against an authored 0.02. **(4) RN-620 to RN-621, THREE FINDINGS FOR OTHER LANES.** **(a) The recorded "31% foot slip" is NOT this file's defect and no Blender edit repairs it.** It is `SpiderFlock.ts` clamping `timeScale` at `WALK_TIMESCALE_MAX` 2.2 against a Skitterer that needs `6.0 / (2.5 * 0.75)` = 3.2, and 2.2/3.2 is exactly the 31.25% recorded. **It is the ONLY type that slips**: Ravager 2.000, Lancer 1.676, Sunderer 1.344 and Colossus 1.295 all sit under the clamp, so the whole trade falls on the early-game swarm type, which is the creature a player sees most and in the largest numbers. **A faster clip cannot help**, because the client already multiplies cycle rate by `timeScale`, so a clip that is only "the walk at half the duration" produces a bit-identical pose sequence at the same wall rate. Only a longer STRIDE buys ground speed at a readable leg rate, and that is bounded by adjacent same-side legs crossing at the frozen 35 degree azimuth spacing. A `Spider_Run` must therefore land in the same commit as the client line that selects it, or it is dead payload in the .glb. **(b) PER-INSTANCE CLIP PHASE OFFSET DOES NOT EXIST.** `SpiderFlock.pose` calls `want.reset()`, which sets `action.time = 0`, and nothing offsets it; there is no `mixer.setTime` anywhere in the repo. Eight rigs claimed on one tick play in exact lockstep, and because the mixers tick on a fixed dt that lockstep is deterministic rather than dithered by frame timing. The sim already staggers itself (`scanIn: made % SCAN_TICKS`); the render side has no analogue. This is the cheap half of idle variation and it is four lines in a file this pass could not take. **(c) THE BRIEF'S PREMISE ABOUT `animgate.js` IS BACKWARDS, AND THE CORRECTION IS LOAD-BEARING.** That probe proves the mixer using the **IDLE** clip's own 2.0 s cycle, not the walk, and its header argues the point carefully. **A t/t+period identity test is STRUCTURALLY UNAVAILABLE for a walk cycle on screen**: `EnemySwarm.march` has no arrival condition, so a 6 m/s Skitterer crosses 2.2 m in one walk period and the frame shares no tiles with itself, and no threshold makes it available. `probes/spidergait.js` therefore asserts the cycle property on a BITING creature, which is stationary and plays the idle, and leaves walk-cycle closure to `gait_check.py`, which reads it off a bone position exactly. **NOT DONE, NAMED: `probes/spidergait.js` is syntax-checked and has NEVER BEEN RUN against a client**, because wiring the bite into `SpiderFlock.ts` is a cross-lane change this pass did not take: that file carried 38 uncommitted lines of the fang lane's work when the pass began. **THE CLIENT HALF IS OWED AND IS ROUGHLY FOUR LINES**: a `BITE_CLIP = 'Spider_Bite'` constant beside the other two, a `bite` action on the `Rig` interface, `pose()` selecting it on `c.biting !== ''` instead of falling through to the idle, and a per-instance phase offset applied after `reset()`. Note that `probes/spiderwalk.js` asserts a stopped creature plays `Spider_Idle` and **will go red the moment the bite is wired**, which is correct and is that probe doing its job. **ALSO OPEN:** a second idle and a death or hit reaction were not reached, and both are blocked behind the same client selection; the far swarm in `EnemyArt.ts` still shares only five numbers with this asset, so **none of this animation work reaches any creature beyond the nearest eight**, which remains a client-lane follow-up nobody has taken. **INVARIANTS: 28 bones, none renamed, added or removed; no clip renamed and no clip retimed (`Spider_Walk` keeps its name and its 0.8000 s exactly, and only its CONTENT moved, which is not a contract change because the walk publishes no index); `validate_glb.py` PASS on all 21 checks including clips set-equality against `contracts.json`, `anim_t0` (all three clips start at t = 0), `bones` 28, `skin_weights` every vertex at sum 1.0000, `rest_pose` 6.46e-07 and `frame1_identity`; geometry untouched at lod0 4,346 of 4,400, total 8,038 of 8,200, materials 6 of 6, envelope [4.5233, 1.5975, 3.9470] to the digit; two builds byte-identical (b18a60ca); `of_lib.py` and `rig_common.py` were never opened, so no other asset can have moved.** **(5) RN-622 to RN-625, FOUR MORE THINGS THE INSTRUMENT FOUND, one of them mine and fixed.** **(a) MY OWN BITE PUT ITS BRACED FEET THROUGH THE FLOOR.** The first version dropped the Root 45 mm at the impact frame to sell the body's weight landing, and **in a forward-kinematic clip the root carries the FEET with it and no leg rotation downstream can hold them up**: the rear pair measured 46 to 53 mm below z = 0, about 6 cm at the drawn surface once the claw's 10 mm tube is counted, on the one clip a player watches from two metres away. The second half was the brace legs' own compression, authored as a NEGATIVE lift to read as taking the load, which in FK drives the tip down rather than settling the body on to the leg. **Fixed: the lunge is horizontal, the sense of drop is carried by thorax and head pitch (which pivot rather than translate), and femur and tibia are now opposed so the knee takes the flex and the tip stays put. Worst penetration 0.0533 to 0.0106 m at the axis, i.e. grazing at the surface; leg 3 goes from -0.0460 to +0.0003.** The braced claim now holds in both axes: rear feet travel 0.0769 and 0.0863 m against the striking pair's 0.3804. **(b) THE SUSPECTED KNEE INTERPENETRATION IS NOT THERE, and the suspicion was mine.** Adjacent same-side knees close to **0.2814 m** at the sweep extremes against a contact distance of 0.1001 m (twice a knee radius measured off the skin at 0.0500, with the authored 0.0520 printed only as a cross-check): 2.8x margin, 0.1813 m of daylight. Worth recording because it was the reason I expected the stride could not grow, and it is now measured instead of feared. **(c) ALL THREE CLIPS CLOSE THEIR LOOPS EXACTLY: every one of the 24 foot deltas between phase 0.0 and 1.0 reads 0.0000 m**, and `CLIP_FIRST_KEY_AT_ZERO` is 1 on all three, so DW-34 holds in the shipped bytes rather than in the build script's intention. The idle's feet are pinned to **0.0006 m**, sixteen times tighter than the ~0.01 m its own build print claims, because most of that 0.01 is the VERTICAL root bob and the contract is about horizontal travel. **(d) NAMED, NOT FIXED: the walk's planted feet move 45 mm VERTICALLY during stance and dip to -0.0060 m**, so the foot axis passes below the ground plane and the drawn claw is about 16 mm under it. The cause is the same Root bob (+/-0.02 m) that the sway fix does not touch, since a root translation reaches every foot equally and cannot be cancelled by rotation. It is a look-versus-contact trade rather than a defect, and it is left for whoever owns the bob. Related instrument caveat, stated because it bounds the duty number: **walk duty reads 0.5333 against an authored 0.5000 and that gap is a ground-band artifact, not the clip.** The band cannot be tightened below the 45 mm of real vertical stance travel, and sweeping it 74% moved the headline slip by only 0.0012 m/s, so the slip is not living on the knob even though the duty is. COST: the .glb grows 1,056,804 to 1,089,924 bytes, which is the bite's keyframe data and no geometry, and no draw call, triangle, material or bone count moves. Commits `b84606a`, `0d023c6`. Screenshots `RN605_spider_bite_f11_c34` (wind-up, both fangs presented) and `RN605_spider_bite_f21_c34` (impact), one clip two frames apart under one light; `RN605_spider_bite_f21_chead`; `RN605_bite_sheet`; `RN604_walk_sheet`, re-rendered because the walk changed.

> **RN-491 to RN-498 (2026-08-01): THE FANG, AND THE CHANNEL THE MERGE THREW AWAY.** Reid, on the pelt build: "the fangs appear to have the texture as well. the fangs can be solid white with a sheen". He is right, RN-465 had already flagged it as a known limitation, and the ask and the missing channel turn out to be THE SAME THING: a sheen is a specular, a specular is low roughness, and roughness is precisely what `SpiderFlock.load`'s merge discards. **(1) RN-491, THE CHANNEL, AND IT COST NO LEDGER SLOT.** `web/src/render/materials/PartMaterial.ts` bakes each source material's authored roughness, metalness and an `of_bare` flag into ONE vec3 vertex attribute `aPartMat`, exactly the way the merge already bakes colour: **the proof that per-vertex data survives that merge was always sitting one line up in the same loop.** It declares NO material and installs NO `onBeforeCompile`; it exports GLSL that `FurShader.ts` splices into the ONE hook RN-463 argued for and spent. **THE DW-10 LEDGER BOTH WAYS: it stays at 4 ShaderMaterial + 3 hooks. Built as its own hook it would have been 4 + 4, which is what RN-455 priced it at, BEFORE FurShader existed.** RN-455's price was quoted against a world that no longer holds, and re-taking that measurement instead of inheriting it is the whole saving. **(2) RN-492, THE RULE, AND IT IS NOT A FANG SPECIAL CASE.** Effective response for a part is `authored role value x family ORM channel`: the FAMILY MAP supplies the variation across the surface, the AUTHORED ROLE supplies the level. The merged material's own roughness and metalness become the denominator of that ratio, so they now decide nothing except the fallback when the channel is off, and they must be NON-ZERO, which `assertPartMatBase` checks rather than hopes. A `bare` part additionally drops the family's albedo, strand normal and tiling AO, and takes its own colour and roughness FLAT. **(3) RN-493, WHAT THE PLAYER BODY AND THE MACHINES INHERIT, WHICH IS THE POINT.** Every merged single-material asset after this one has the same shape of problem: the suit is fabric plus a GLASS VISOR plus METAL FITTINGS, a machine is painted steel plus glass plus rubber, and the part one family cannot describe is reliably the part a player looks at. A lane inherits this by calling `bakePartMat` in its merge loop and `injectPartMat` from whatever hook it already has, and authoring the response in `of_lib.PALETTE`, which every asset already uses. **No role table on the client, no name parsing, no per-asset branch:** the bare flag travels as a glTF material `extras` entry written from a Blender material custom property (`export_extras=True` was already on) and lands in `material.userData` via GLTFLoader, VERIFIED by reading the exported .glb JSON rather than assumed. **WHAT IS STILL NOT SOLVED, PLAINLY: this is one family plus an escape hatch, not per-part FAMILIES.** A suit whose fabric and whose metal each want their own tiling family needs multi-family sampling in one shader, which is a real slot and is not built. **(4) RN-494, THE FANG.** `Fang` is the first member of `of_lib.BARE_ROLES`, roughness 0.30 to **0.18** (section 2.1's 0.15 with margin, and deliberately far from the shell's 0.745..0.95: hard wet keratin against soft velvet is what makes both read), colour C9BCA2 to **D5D1C6**. **THE COLOUR WAS TAKEN FROM THE MATERIAL AND NOT FROM THE RENDER, and the first version of it was the other way round and was measurably wrong.** EDE8DC measured a fang whose MEDIAN pixel was 255: the form was gone and the specular had nothing left to be brighter than. But tuning it down against the STUDIO would have been RN-456 again, because the studio is Standard + High Contrast, which CLIPS, while the game is ACES, which rolls off. So the number comes from neither render: keratin and ivory sit at 0.60 to 0.70 diffuse reflectance and D5D1C6 is linear 0.646/0.622/0.556. **(5) RN-495, THE INSTRUMENT, AND IT OUTRANKS THE ART AGAIN.** `--diag <stops>` is a new MEASUREMENT mode: exposure dropped, look removed, so the frame is a plain sRGB encode of scene radiance and the linear value can be read back out and put through the client's own ACES arithmetic. It exists because the picture mode structurally cannot answer this question: a part whose albedo is 20x the shell's clips at ANY exposure that renders the shell correctly, so a WHITE part photographs as a white slab whatever its roughness is. **Read back at -3 stops the fang is scene-linear p05 0.191 / p50 0.728 / p99 0.958 against the shell's 0.0362, and through three's ACESFilmic at exposure 1.2 that predicts display 145 / 222 / 230 against the shell's 44: unclipped, and a 5x value step.** **THE HONEST HALF: p99/p50 in display is 1.04.** A 0.65-albedo DIELECTRIC cannot show a strong specular against its own diffuse (F0 is 4%), so the sheen reads as a crisp terminator and a defined lit face rather than a hot spot. A hotter glint needs a DARKER fang, which trades away "solid white", or a real specular term, which is a slot. Priced, not built, and not claimed in a screenshot. **(6) RN-496, THE EYES, AND THEIR COST IS THE DECISION.** Reid did not ask for them. The ratio rule is mechanism-wide and therefore hands `EyeGlow` and `EyeDark` their AUTHORED 0.10 roughness for literally zero extra code, zero extra bytes and zero extra instructions, so that half is taken: the six near-black secondary eyes now read wet by a specular instead of only by value, which is the thing RN-455 wrote down as impossible. **The `bare` flag for them is NOT taken**, because that is a table row and a look change nobody asked for, and it is one row away whenever someone wants it. **NAMED AND NOT FIXED:** the studio treats the eyes as flat (no `ROLE_FAMILY` row) while the client's one material samples the fur maps on every vertex including theirs; that divergence predates this pass and the bare flag would close it. **(7) RN-497, THE STUDIO STOPS LYING BY DELETION.** `CLIENT_MERGE_ROUGH_METAL` is GONE. It existed to force one roughness and one metalness onto every role so a studio render showed what the merge could actually draw; the merge now carries them, and `authored x ORM` is exactly what `surface_preview` already wired with no forcing, **so the honest preview and the plain preview became the same thing.** What replaces it is `--nopart`, THE STUDIO'S `?partmat=0`, which restores the pre-RN-491 collapse so the before/after pair is ONE FLAG APART ON ONE BUILD UNDER ONE LIGHT instead of two commits apart: a control that only exists in the client cannot photograph the thing it controls, and Reid is in the game. `surface_preview` reads `of_lib.BARE_ROLES` rather than keeping a second copy. **(8) VERIFICATION, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER.** No client, no build, no server, no probe, no browser: Reid is on 4200 and this pass never went near it. What WAS proved offline: the injection is not a no-op, run against three 0.185.1's ACTUAL shipped `meshphysical` source in node, **8 of 8 anchors hit, 0 missing, vertex +70 chars, fragment +685, and `?partmat=0` a total no-op at 0 chars on both stages**; the check has a NEGATIVE CONTROL that fires by name (one anchor broken to `roughnessmapX_fragment` gives `anchors missed: fragment:roughness`, reverted, green). **Failure mode 1 is named in the file BEFORE any measurement and is the reason that check exists: a `String.replace` whose needle is absent returns the string unchanged and reports nothing, so a dead channel looks EXACTLY like a pass that did nothing** (which is the current state, so it is the one signature that must be distinguishable). `injectPartMat` therefore counts its replacements and publishes the misses, and `partMatStats()` is published beside `furStats()` so "the hook is installed" and "the channel reached the geometry" are TWO assertions. **BOTH FLAG DEFAULTS ARE FIXTURES AND ARE ASSERTED AS SUCH:** `partmat` absent gives `flagPresent false, enabled true`, and `furState()` now publishes `flagPresent` too (RN-150: `Number(null)` is 0). **`?fur=0` REMAINS THE STOCK-PROGRAM CONTROL, AND RN-498 IS THE BUG THAT NEARLY COST IT.** The first version of this pass gated `bakePartMat` on `partmat` alone, so with `?fur=0` the hook was gone and the attribute was still written: a dead ~52 KB per-vertex buffer that no program binds, and a control that no longer matched the build before FurShader.ts existed. **It was caught by re-reading the claim I had just written in this file against the code, not by any check**, which is worth recording because nothing in the gate set could have found it. The rule is now stated where it belongs: `PartMaterial` does not read the `fur` flag, because it does not know which hook a given asset splices it into and a merged machine will have a different one, so **the CALLER bakes only when a hook that reads the attribute will actually be compiled**. `SpiderFlock` reads `furState().enabled` once before the merge loop. **THE WIND AND MOTION LAG WERE NOT TOUCHED AND ARE STILL UNVERIFIED** (RN-465); the only change near them is that a bare part no longer sways, which fixes a LATENT bug in the shipped build, because `furOut` is inferred from the normal and a fang is a three-sided cone that read as the FURRIEST thing on the creature. **INVARIANTS: 28 bones and both clips untouched; the ENVELOPE IS 1.6036 TO THE DIGIT and three.js xyz [4.5233, 1.5975, 3.9470] unchanged, because nothing geometric moved; validate 51/51 PASS, lod0 4,346 of 4,400, total 8,038 of 8,200, materials 6 of 6; `check_coplanar` 0 over allowance; `texgen selftest` 37 of 37 and `texgen check` 79 of 79 with texgen.py UNMODIFIED; spider.glb rebuilds byte-identical (md5 5e2eb445), and player_body, assembler and boulder_iron all rebuild byte-identical under the of_lib change, which is the control that the `of_bare` custom property and BARE_ROLES touch no other asset's bytes; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean with a negative control red BY NAME (TS2304 `PART_ATTR`) and silent after revert; contracts.json edited as literal text, 17 insertions 1 deletion, no round trip.** ATTRIBUTION: at c34 the whole change is a **65 x 127 px box, 0.14% of the frame**, and the rest of the creature does not move. NO SUBAGENTS: the pass was small and the machine was Reid's.
