> **RN-461 to RN-465 (2026-08-01): THE SHELL BECOMES A PELT, AND THE HALF REID ASKED FOR THAT BLENDER STRUCTURALLY CANNOT SHOW.** Reid: "make it more hairy. it looks like its made of shiny stone. it should look like it has almost like a fur. very short fur. the fur should react to movement and the wind too." **He is right and the brief was wrong, and the correction is worth more than the art:** a sharp specular highlight is the single strongest HARD SURFACE cue there is, and the WIDER the roughness band the harder a thing reads, so RN-455's measured 0.242 to 0.792 band was excellent machinery aimed at beetle carapace when the subject is a tarantula. **(1) RN-461, THE MAP, AND EVERY TERM INVERTS ONE ABOVE IT.** Family renamed `chitin` to `fur`. Roughness HIGH EVERYWHERE: effective **0.745 to 0.95**, still clearing section 2.1's 0.15 band but sitting at the TOP of the range instead of straddling the middle, so no part of the surface is near a specular. The punctate pits and bristle sockets are **GONE**: they were the right detail for a shell and were also the COARSEST thing on the map, which is backwards for a surface whose whole character is that it is finer than its neighbours. In their place `_hair_layer` lays **real, discrete, tapered STRANDS along a wobbling flow field**, two layers at 20 and 40 cells over a 0.30 m tile (15 mm and 7.5 mm apart), bucketed 3x3 the way `_worley` buckets its points so cost stays linear in texels. **Strands rather than filtered noise because every generator in that file is isotropic BY CONSTRUCTION** (worley is distance to a POINT, fbm is a lattice of scalars) **and no amount of tuning grows a direction on an isotropic field**; a highlight stretched along the flow is what fur has and felt does not. Albedo darkens at the ROOT and lifts at the TIP. **(2) RN-462, THE GEOMETRY.** 14 hand-typed 185 mm SPINES became **116 seeded 46 to 86 mm hairs** (46 abdomen, 22 carapace, 6 per leg), seated on the ring profile by arithmetic (`profile_at` / `surface_at`, roots pushed 25% inside) rather than checked by hand, which is the only way a hundred is possible: **RN-246's floating scree avoided by construction.** lod0 3,530 to 4,346 (budget 4,400), **+816 x MAX_RIGS 8 = +6,528 worst case, 0.7% to 1.2%** of RN-71's 555k to 1.0M frame; cumulative against v1, 1,060 to 4,346 is 2.6% to 4.7%. Draw calls STILL unchanged (the merge). **THE LEG HAIR RANGES SKIP THE KNEE AND THAT IS THE ADMIN CAP, NOT A PREFERENCE:** the knee apex is the highest point on the creature, the first version put a hair straight up off it and the asset measured **1.6710 against 1.6036, a 4% growth in DRAWN SIZE bought by decoration**; constrained to the femur and tibia below the knuckle, the envelope is unchanged to the digit. **(3) RN-463 to RN-465, THE MOTION, AND IT IS UNVERIFIED.** `web/src/render/materials/FurShader.ts` is **ONE new live `onBeforeCompile`** (DW-10: 4 ShaderMaterial + 2 hooks to **4 + 3** with the flora wind on), spent and argued in the RN-52 style. It carries three things a map cannot: **RIM SCATTER** (short fur reads almost entirely at the SILHOUETTE and at grazing angles, where the line of sight passes through many strands instead of off one, which is view-dependent and a texture by definition is not; added to OUTGOING radiance and not to diffuse, so it survives on the shadow side where a fuzzy edge is most visible); **WIND**, PropWind's ANALOGUE and deliberately not an extension (that hook is `#ifdef USE_BATCHING` and phases off `batchingMatrix[3]`, which does not exist on a SkinnedMesh, and its amplitude is linear in height above the prop base, which is right for a plant rooted in the ground and wrong for hair on a body) keeping its three rules: sim clock so pausing stops the breeze, phase from POSITION never spawn time, one shared hook object so the program cache key stays identical; and **MOTION LAG**, the cheap version, the flock's MEAN velocity differenced off the rig roots `SpiderFlock` already positions rather than adding a velocity to the sim for a rendering want, **with its limit written where it lives: eight creatures running different ways all stream their fur the same way, and per-rig lag needs a material clone per rig.** The displacement lands **after `<skinning_vertex>`, not after `<begin_vertex>`**: `transformed` is the BIND POSE until skinning has run, so displacing earlier makes the pelt swim against the animation. How far a vertex stands OFF the body has no attribute, so it is INFERRED from the normal, which varies slowly on the shell and points hard away on a three-sided hair. **`?fur=0` REMOVES THE HOOK ENTIRELY** rather than zeroing an amplitude, so the material keeps its stock program and the build is bit-exact to the one before this file existed: that is both the negative control and the perf isolator, and a zeroed uniform would be neither. **(4) WHAT IS NOT DONE, PLAINLY.** The static fur look IS verified in Blender and the pair is committed. **THE WIND AND THE MOTION LAG ARE UNVERIFIED**: both are functions of a clock and a velocity that exist only in the running game, Reid is playing, and no build-and-look loop was run. `furStats()` is published so the hook and the `?fur=0` BOOT DEFAULT can each be asserted in their own right (RN-150: an unexercised default ships off silently). Failure modes are named in the file header BEFORE anyone measures: fur swimming while the creature stands still is the clock off a wall timer; a pop on claim is a phase off spawn time; an even cartoon outline is the rim noise dead; a creature going black when the sun passes behind it is the rim added to diffuse. **ALSO OPEN:** the fangs wear the fur map, visible in the head close-up and unavoidable while the merge gives the creature one material, priced at RN-455 and unchanged. **INVARIANTS: 28 bones and both clips untouched; validate PASS, lod0 4,346 of 4,400, total 8,038 of 8,200, materials 6 of 6; `check_coplanar` 0 by absence; `texgen check` 79 of 79; spider.glb and all three fur PNGs rebuild byte-identical; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean with a negative control red BY NAME in both files and silent after revert.** Commit `28402f9`. The look-dev values freeze is lifted for THIS ASSET ONLY (Admin, 2026-08-01) and stands everywhere else. **(1) RN-453, THE FAMILY, AND ITS SHAPE IS THE GENERAL THING, NOT THE SPIDER.** `chitin` is **normal + orm + a TILING ALBEDO** at metre UVs, 0.30 m tile, 384 px, opaque, mean-neutral. Pushing the relief fine enough to stop that ALSO deleted every feature it had at 7 m and it went **rock to dusty clay without passing through chitin**. The split that works: **ALBEDO carries pigmentation at 10 to 20 cm plus crease darkening; NORMAL carries relief below a centimetre (punctate pits and bristle sockets, an annulus with a hole in it off ONE worley field so the two stay concentric); ORM carries an effective roughness band 0.242 to 0.792** against section 2.1's 0.15 requirement and `panel`'s measured 0.032. Under AgX the chitin reads as dusty terracotta, **which is a statement about the view transform and not about the map**, and three renders were spent tuning against it. `render_creatures.setup_view_transform` now PRINTS its transform, look and exposure on every run (Standard, +0.26 stops, High Contrast: not ACES, and the docstring says so, but wrong in the same DIRECTION as the game rather than the opposite one), the world is a dim sky, the sun is 2 degrees so a shell's specular stays TIGHT, and the floor is substrate-coloured at section 2.1's own reference luma. The other half is `surface_preview.apply_all(force=...)` and `--merged`, which **force the CLIENT's single roughness and metalness onto every role so a studio pair previews what the game can draw**, because a render giving the fangs 0.30 flatters in the direction nobody double-checks. **(5) RN-457, THE MERGE.** `SpiderFlock` DELETED `uv` in the merge; a map bound to that material would have sampled 0,0 on every vertex and drawn one flat texel with every "is a map bound" check reading true. UVs now go through `Surfaces.copyUv`, which copies unconditionally (a mixed attribute set makes `mergeGeometries` return null and the `?? list[0]` swallows it, reducing the creature to its first primitive) and COUNTS. **(6) RN-458, THE PALETTE.** The creature roles moved out of `build_spider`'s runtime `PALETTE.update()` into `of_lib.PALETTE`, because texgen's own "no stale roles" gate refuses a family row for a role of_lib has never heard of: **a role that wears a surface is a first-class palette role.** `Chitin` came UP from 2B2126 to 4A3B36, and that is the single biggest value decision here: section 2.1 puts groundNear at luma 35 to 55 and **a creature at luma 36 has no separation from the ground it stands on at any sun angle.** **(7) RN-459, IN GAME: BOUND, PROVED; LOOKS RIGHT, NOT PROVED.** `probes/spiderskin.js` against a frozen build of `1b6b5b4`, one port of my own, killed immediately, Reid's 4200 untouched. **smoke PASS, 88 draw calls of 150, 8 rigs claimed. `uv.byConsumer.spider = 6`, synthesised 0, countMismatch 0: the UVs survive the merge.** The material is on `chitin` with all five slots bound, mapSize **384 not 1x1**, repeat **3.3333 = 1/0.30**, normal and orm in NoColorSpace, alphaTest 0, roughness 0.800, metalness 0.040. **Two-sided: unbinding every map moves 200 of 1296 tiles at peak 16.27 counts and changes the hash; rebinding is BIT-EXACT at 0 tiles moved.** **THE GAP, NAMED: `setMaps` unbinds EVERY family at once, so those 200 tiles are terrain, foliage, machines and creature together and cannot be attributed to chitin. Attribution needs a per-family unbind the API does not have.** **AND THE PICTURE FAILED TWICE, FOR TWO REASONS, NEITHER FIXABLE IN BLENDER: (a)** the aiming sweep is spiderwalk's "twelve headings, keep the one that moves most", which was true at RN-124 and is FALSE now because the flora lane's wind landed in between and **11,465 foliage instances move in every heading**: INSTRUMENTS.md's dominant failure, and the thing that moved was another lane's feature; The tergite banding is two rings 18 to 20 mm apart with a radius drop, i.e. **rock_form's bedding ledge (RN-241) wrapped round a body**: an annular lip, watertight, and cheaper than separate scute plates. **(2) RN-451, THE FINDING, AND IT OUTRANKS THE ART.** The brief and this asset's own contract both say the far swarm shares the authored shape, so silhouette work reaches every creature on screen while skinning cost falls only on the nearest eight. **IT DOES NOT.** `EnemyView` draws `EnemyArt.creatureGeometry()`, five boxes and sixteen limb boxes built in TypeScript, and the two representations share exactly **HIP_Y 0.62, KNEE_Y 1.55, KNEE_R 1.05, FOOT_R 2.4 and AZ 35/70/110/145**. The claim boundary swaps animation and not shape only to the extent of those five numbers; they are frozen here and are the reason the knee had to be a pinch rather than a knuckle, and everything else on the creature was free. **Re-authoring the far stand-in against this form is a client-lane follow-up and no Blender edit can do it.** **(3) THE PRICE, STATED.** lod0 1,060 to 3,450 (budget 3,600), total 1,960 to 6,380 (6,700). `SpiderFlock.MAX_RIGS` caps the skinned pool at 8, so worst case is **+19,120 triangles in a fight against the 555k to 1.0M per frame RN-71 measured, 1.9% to 3.4%**, beside the rock lane's accepted 1.7% to 3.0%. **DRAW CALLS UNCHANGED AND `max_materials` STAYS 4, AND THE REASON IS A SECOND FINDING**: `SpiderFlock.load` merges every `_LOD0` primitive into ONE geometry and bakes material colour into a vertex-colour attribute, then draws with one material per enemy TYPE, so **this file's material count never reaches the draw-call count**. > **RN-371 to RN-378 (2026-08-01): THE MACHINE FORM PASS, PART 1. A ROCK IS DETAILED BY FRACTURE AND A MACHINE IS DETAILED BY ASSEMBLY, SO IT NEEDS ITS OWN VOCABULARY, AND THE COPLANAR GATE HAS TO SURVIVE IT STRUCTURALLY RATHER THAN CAREFULLY.** Blender only, no browser, no build, no dev server: other lanes are live in the client. **(1) RN-371, THE INSTRUMENT, `tools/blender/render_machines.py`.** `render_check.py`'s machine views were computed for a 4.4 m frame width and crop an 8 m assembler, it has no floor, no view at the height a player stands, and no way to draw more than one copy of anything. **A FACTORY IS NOT LOOKED AT ONE MACHINE AT A TIME**, so this tool's `line:` shot places the machines on the client's OWN 1 m site grid (even footprints on integer centres, belt tiles on half integers) with real belt tiles between them, both curve handednesses, and the player body in frame as the only honest scale reference for a 3 m to 8 m object. `studio:` is two bearings on a neutral floor, `face:` is the standing-eye view at the port side which is the frame the game actually shows, and `det:` is 1.3 m of the front-lower CORNER including the ground contact, because a bolt head is 0.03 m and is four pixels in a whole-machine frame. **Both framing bugs RN-306 found in `render_flora.py` are fixed at birth rather than inherited**: `hide_render` is set BOTH ways so a second shot in one invocation is not an empty frame, and every view frames by whichever of height and footprint is LARGER. A third was found here and is written down: resolution is PER SHOT, because every distance in the file is solved from the sensor fit and Blender fits the 36 mm sensor to the larger pixel dimension, so the first `face:` put an 8 x 4 machine across 43 percent of a 720 x 640 frame. **(2) RN-372, THE VOCABULARY, `tools/blender/machine_form.py`, NEW and new for `rock_form.py`'s reason**: `of_lib.py` is read by every lane and all 51 assets, and industrial assembly detail has no business being visible to a tree. Eighteen greeble types over a `Face` abstraction with in-plane (u, v) coordinates, so one description of a detail band serves +Y, -Y, +X, -X and the roof. **THE COPLANAR GATE IS HELD BY TWO PROPERTIES, NOT BY CARE, and this is the part worth keeping.** The four clean machines are at ZERO by their ABSENCE from `check_coplanar`'s allowance table, and greebles are precisely how coplanar pairs get made; the catalogued root cause is two parts dimensioned off one landmark where the landmark is a width COPIED rather than DERIVED. So (a) nothing is ever placed ON a face: `Face.part` puts a part's front at `plane + proud` and its BACK at `plane - proud * 0.55`, and there is no call in the module that can land a part flush; and (b) **the proud height is a property of the greeble TYPE and not of the call site**, so two parts can only meet on a plane if they are the same type, and a type has one role, and a same-material overlap is invisible by construction and deliberately uncounted. **A caller cannot re-create the defect by passing a number, because the number is not a parameter.** Measured: assembler same-facing 0 before, 0 after, across 2,292 added triangles. **(3) TWO THINGS THE FIRST DRAFT GOT WRONG, BOTH NOW STRUCTURAL.** Nothing in this project CUTS geometry: there is no boolean anywhere, so the first module had a `sink()` that put a box inside a solid body, which would have authored four maintenance hatches nobody could see. A machine gets a recess the way `build_assembler._mouth` already got one, by standing a COAMING proud of the surface. And winding is not a rule an author can follow: the in-plane basis is (Y, Z) on an X face and (X, Z) on a Y face and those have opposite handedness against their own normals, so six axis-and-sign cases are six chances to ship an invisible backfaced panel on one side of one machine. `machine_form.oriented` tests the SIGNED VOLUME of the closed solid instead, which is one test that cannot be wrong. **(4) RN-373 to RN-377, THE ASSEMBLER, 684 to 2,976 triangles at LOD0.** Sixteen plate seams for ninety-six triangles, because a strap that spans the body shows on the face it enters AND the face it leaves (`build_smelter`'s rib trick, named and pointed at plating). **FOUR FACES THAT NOW DIFFER**, which is what gives the machine a front: instruments, a cable run, a canopy over the outlet and an eave with five gussets on the front; a feed hood leaning the OPPOSITE way on the rear intake, so the two intakes and the one outlet are distinguishable by shape from across the base; a ladder, a step and a bracketed landing on the side intake; a louvre coaming and a hinged, latched, bolted hatch on the service side. Sixteen anchor pads bolting the machine to its own plinth, which is what closed the one frame in the pass that showed nothing: the player-eye detail view was a picture of an empty yellow band and an empty dark slab. Kick plates at the foot of all four faces, **TWO OF THEM DENTED, and that is this lane's whole answer to wear**: look development owns every albedo and roughness value in the game, so a scuff cannot be authored here, but a dent can, and a dent is the cause a scuff is the effect of, for the same twelve triangles the box it replaces cost. A four-sided railing with posts, rails and toe boards in place of four boxes, because a parapet is SOLID and a railing lets the sky through at the exact height a player sees a roofline against it. **THE LADDER IS THE BEST TRIANGLES IN THE PASS AND THE REASON IS SCALE, NOT DETAIL: it is the only greeble whose size a player already knows.** It stops at 2.42 and arrives at a bracketed landing, and that is arithmetic rather than taste: the collar is 0.20 proud from 2.90 to 3.20 and a stringer stands 0.139 proud, so a ladder taken higher DISAPPEARS inside the collar for 30 cm and reappears as a stub. **(5) RN-378, THE BUDGET RAISE, ARGUED AND PRICED IN THE ROW.** lod0 1100 to 3050 (actual 2976), total 1800 to 3500 (actual 3428). `MachineBatch.ts:195` selects `_LOD0` ONLY and never switches by distance, and `MachineBatch.ts:211` sets `castShadow` against three CSM cascades (`Quality.ts:23`), so **every machine triangle is drawn FOUR times a frame and the whole raise is paid on every assembler on screen**: +2,292 each, +9,168 over four, **+1.4% of the 660,385 triangle frame `probes/portcost.js` measured over a 79-building base** and 0.34% of the 2.7M `StatsProbe` alert. Assemblers are the rarest machine in a base; portcost's own reference base is 22 smelters and 57 belts and no assembler at all. **RECORDED AND NOT ACTED ON: LOD1 and LOD2 are DEAD PAYLOAD on EVERY machine, exactly as RN-243 found the harvest nodes' are, because nothing selects them.** Kept because `lod_nodes` lists them; flagged to the client lane. **(6) INVARIANTS.** All 18 machine and structure assets rebuilt BYTE-IDENTICAL before any edit, which is what makes "before" a measurement rather than a file date; `validate_glb --all` 50/51 after (the one failure is the sibling rocket lane's in-flight `rocket_parts`, not this lane's); `check_coplanar` 0 over allowance on all 51 with the assembler at 0 same; the 8 x 4 x 8 declared box now asserted BY THE BUILD (`machine_form.assert_inside`, axis named and overshoot in metres) rather than found afterwards in the shipped bytes; sockets and the collision proxy untouched and verified 6/6; **`contracts.json` is shared and the rocket lane held uncommitted edits in it, so the commit staged a FILTERED blob whose only difference from HEAD is the assembler row**; real index verified empty before and refreshed to HEAD after; zero em dashes verified in Python per file. **ALL MATERIAL VALUES UNTOUCHED AND OWED TO LOOK DEVELOPMENT.** Commit `5182a3a`. Screenshots `RN371_before_*` against `RN372_after_*` (`_a`, `_b`, `_face`, `_det`) plus `RN371_before_line` / `RN372_after_line`. **NOT DONE: the smelter, miner, box, belts, generator, power pole, inserter, structures set, survival smelter and primitive furnace.**

> **RN-331 to RN-352 (2026-08-01): THE LOOK-DEVELOPMENT PASS. THE CLIENT ALREADY HAD ACES, SO THE PASTEL WAS SOMEWHERE ELSE, AND THE PLACE IT WAS IS THAT THE GROUND UNDER A FOREST WAS PAINTED THE COLOUR OF THE FOREST.** First pass under `docs/web/ART-DIRECTION.md` that owns colour, and the deliverable meant to outlive it is section 2.1, THE CALIBRATED TARGET. **(1) RN-331, THE FINDINGS, STATED BEFORE ANY CHANGE, BECAUSE THE BRIEF'S OWN HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG AND IT IS WORTH RECORDING THAT IT WAS.** The brief predicted that "pastel is very often an unmapped or naive curve plus a lifted black point". Measured: **the curve was never the problem.** `CompositeGlsl` has carried the ACES RRT+ODT fit, matrices and all, copied character for character out of three's `tonemapping_pars_fragment`, since RN-10; `Renderer.ts` has set `ACESFilmicToneMapping` and `outputColorSpace = SRGBColorSpace` since W0. Output is sRGB-correct and is NOT double-encoded: the composite writes its own `srgbEncode` and its fragment source contains no `<colorspace_fragment>` or `<tonemapping_fragment>` include, so three's `WebGLProgram` has nothing to substitute and cannot add a second one. The grade runs in DISPLAY space after the encode (RN-10 fixed that once already) at contrast 1.06, saturation 1.08, **lift +0.012, which is a lifted black point and is the one half of the brief's prediction that was true**, and vignette 0.16. **The half that was badly wrong is exposure.** It sat at three's default 1.0 and had never been calibrated against anything: measured across three sites at local noon, `hiFrac`, the share of the frame above luma 200, read **0.00 per cent at Hills, 0.00 at Plains and 0.86 at Forest**. At every site and every daylight elevation the top fifth of the display range was EMPTY while the black point was lifted off zero. That is a frame with no highlights and no blacks, which is what "pastel" is as a number, and it is an exposure fault rather than a curve fault. **(2) RN-332, THE ABANDONED LANE'S WORK: ADOPTED, EXTENDED, AND ONE OF ITS CLAIMS OVERTURNED.** A stopped lane left uncommitted `curveMix` (a slope-matched S that rolls the toe and shoulder so the ends stop clipping), the URL grade flags, `PostDefaults.ts` and `probes/lookdev.js`. I re-derived its numbers on my own build rather than trusting them and **they hold**: at Hills noon, world-band iqr 87 to 108 and mean saturation 0.533 to 0.458, both past a measured instrument floor of 0. The work is kept because its reasoning is sound and its negative control is exact (the restore is bit-identical at eleven rungs of twelve, and `?curve=0` reaches the pre-RN-207 straight line without a rebuild). **Its last unfinished check is overturned in section 5.** **(3) RN-333, THE SHIPPED RESPONSE CURVE.** exposure 1.0 to **1.2**, contrast 1.06 to **1.45** on the S rather than the straight line, saturation 1.08 to **0.92**, lift 0.012 to **0**. The saturation cut is what makes the contrast rise a VALUE change rather than a chroma change: a per-channel contrast raises chroma on its own, and at 1.45 with the old saturation 1.08 Hills noon measured saturation 0.527 to 0.578, i.e. the opposite of what the art direction asks for. At 0.92 the same frame reads chroma 56.8 against 57.7 while value contrast rises 29 per cent. **(4) RN-334, THE FOURTH SITE CONTRADICTED THE OTHER THREE, WHICH IS RN-64's LESSON ARRIVING ON SCHEDULE.** The abandoned lane measured Hills, Plains and Forest, all green biomes. I added **Beach, the site world-gen's own survey calls "the one to show Reid first"**, and two checks went red there and nowhere else: the pivoted contrast moved tiles 13,866 up against 383 down (a desert at noon lies almost entirely ABOVE the 0.5 pivot, so a contrast increase can only brighten it) and the masked night ground FELL, p50 31 to 28 and mean 27.2 to 24.9. An exposure sweep inside one page settled it: 1.20 / 1.08 / 0.98 gave Forest midnight masked-ground p50 2 / 1 / 1 and mean 4.82 / 4.22 / 3.76 against 4.06 before, so **1.20 is the only candidate that does not spend RN-152's starlight floor**, while Beach noon reads p50 172 / 163 / 155 against 150. The trade is published rather than hidden: **1.2 is kept and the price is that Beach noon reads brighter.** The root cause is stated and not fixed: one global exposure serves biome albedos spanning 0.03 (Forest, linear) to 0.58 (Beach red, linear), a 20x range, and no single value can be right for both ends of it. **(5) RN-335 / RN-336, THE GROUND-SKY MASK, AND THE NIGHT ANSWER IS NOT THE ONE THE PREVIOUS LANE GUESSED.** Its last words were that "night terrain got brighter but the night sky lost 1 to 2 counts, and my check conflated them". The conflation was real; the diagnosis was not. `lookdev.js` now builds a sky mask ONCE at noon, per column, as the maximal contiguous run from the top that is blue and bright, and reuses it at every rung: the geometry does not move between rungs, so a noon mask is the same partition at midnight, when no rule could find one, and it is the same partition before and after the grade, so a grade cannot move a pixel between populations and fake a difference. **Measured at Hills, elevation -23.8 degrees, over 461,209 masked sky pixels: the night sky reads mean 0.06 counts before and 0.07 after, with p50 and p95 both exactly 0 and 99.94 per cent of it under luma 24. It is black to the digit and had nothing to lose.** Both movements were the GROUND's, one at its median (7 to 9, up) and one at its own upper tail (37 to 35, down), and a percentile over the union of two disjoint populations cannot say which is which. The check now asserts the ground's MEAN and MEDIAN, which is what RN-152 actually bought, and publishes p95 and the sky beside it. The tail loss is a property of a contrast pivoted at 0.5 rather than a regression: at night every ground pixel lies below the pivot, so no global contrast can raise the median without pulling the tail toward it. **(6) RN-337, THE MASK'S OWN BAR MOVED, AND FOR A LEGITIMATE REASON.** The first bar was "the top row is 95 per cent sky", true at Hills (1.0000) and FALSE at Forest (0.8394), because a canopy hangs into the top of the frame and the 16 per cent that is not sky is leaves. Widened to 0.60 with the measurement recorded, because this is INSTRUMENTS.md's opening failure in miniature: a control that was right when it was written, against a world that then grew trees. **(7) RN-345 to RN-347, THE FOLIAGE AND THE FLOOR, AND THE PICTURE FOUND WHAT NO STATISTIC HAD.** Admin redirected mid-pass on Reid's verdict of the flora work: *"Forest floor looks the same before and after. Still plato-y smooth pastel."* Standing eye at the Forest site pitched 26 degrees down, `docs/screenshots/RN347_forestfloor_before.png` answers it in one look: **the forest floor is a large, smooth, saturated emerald SHEET with sparse tufts standing on it.** The tufts are the understorey, which two lanes had just re-authored for silhouette. The sheet is `BiomePalette.HEX`, it is most of the pixels, and nobody had touched it since W1. **The error is categorical rather than a matter of degree. `biomeAt` classifies CLIMATE, the table was filled in by naming the classes (forest is green, plains is green), and the terrain material draws the GROUND. The ground under a forest is litter, humus, root and soil; the green belongs to the 3.2 million detail cards per square kilometre standing ON it. Painting both the same green leaves the layer that exists to read as vegetation with nothing to read against, which is exactly why two passes of silhouette work changed nothing Reid could see: the silhouettes were correct and they were invisible.** Beach `c8b48a` to `b3a184`, Plains `5f7d38` to `6d6a47`, Forest `2f5230` to `41392b`, Hills `6f7346` to `6b6650`; every one moves down in saturation and toward the substrate, and **Mountains, Polar, Regolith, MoonHighland and CraterFloor are deliberately untouched and are the control, so any measured move at those sites is a bug in this change.** Measured on the money shot, world band: mean saturation **0.590 to 0.439** and mean chroma **25.8 to 13.0**. Beside it, two smaller terms with one owner each so a later change stays attributable. **RN-345**, a family-level `FOLIAGE_TONE` in a new `render/instancing/FoliageTone.ts` (saturation and value about the colour's own luma, leaf 0.62 / 0.86 and grass 0.70 / 0.94, `?foliagetone=0` the exact negative control, boot default 1 through an explicit `null`-safe parse per RN-150). **RN-346**, `ScatterLook.tintFor` widened: value band 0.80..1.18 to 0.66..1.26, the dry drift un-squared (the median instance sat at t = 0.19, i.e. 81 per cent of the way back to the one green) and a second independent CHROMA axis added, because dry is a WARM drift and a field varied only along it is a LINE through colour space where a real understorey is an area. The extra hash draw is re-SEEDED rather than given a new index, since `k * 8 + 12` would alias exactly onto instance `k + 1`'s `+4`. **THE FOLIAGE FINDING THAT MATTERS MOST TO THE NEXT LANE: the two albedo cards carry NO HUE AT ALL.** Decoded from the shipped bytes, `of_grass_a.png` opaque means are R 188.1 / G 187.1 / B 186.2 and `of_leaf_a.png` R 199.6 / G 199.4 / B 199.2, with a maximum absolute R-minus-B of 6 counts. They are grey VALUE textures; every green in the game arrives from `of_lib.PALETTE`, whose five foliage roles sit in a band of HSV saturation 0.519 to 0.551 across hue 85 to 107 degrees. And because `Surfaces.ts` divides `material.color` by the manifest's scalar `albedo_mean`, **raising a card's mean value is a no-op on final brightness BY CONSTRUCTION: the only things that survive that division are the card's spatial VARIANCE and its HUE, and both are currently near zero.** That is where the next foliage pass has the most room, and it is one file. **(8) RN-338 / RN-339, SHADOW AND AMBIENT OCCLUSION AT WALKING DISTANCE, AND BOTH TERMS RUN AT ABOUT A THIRD OF THEIR NOMINAL REACH EXACTLY WHERE THEY MATTER.** Cascade 0 spans 22 m in a square box of 1.44 times that, so on the high tier it is **15.47 mm per shadow texel** with a PCF kernel one texel wide, and the 22 m boundary into cascade 1 is a **3.64x resolution cliff with no blend**. The AO and contact terms are clamped in SCREEN space, `aoMaxScreen` 0.09 and `csMaxScreen` 0.05, and with `uProj[0][0]` at 0.9743 for the shipped 60-degree vertical field of view those clamps **BIND at every pixel closer than 4.87 m and 4.38 m respectively**. The effective world radius collapses to `0.185 * z` for AO and the march length to `0.103 * z` for contact, so the ground under a standing player's own feet at z of 1.5 to 2 m gets an AO radius of **0.28 to 0.37 m against a nominal 0.9 m** and a contact march of **0.15 to 0.21 m against a nominal 0.45 m**. The clamps exist to bound the face-against-a-wall case and their comments say so; what the derivation shows is that they bind in the ORDINARY standing case, which is not what they were written for. Both are fixed-tap terms (36 horizon taps, 8 march steps), so the cost of widening them is texture-cache locality and not arithmetic. **NOT CHANGED THIS PASS, and named as the first thing the next look-dev lane should price.** Load-bearing for any AO retune: `AO_APPLY_FS` is a full-screen MULTIPLY over the final colour and `TerrainShader` sums ambient and direct into one value with no channel to reach into, so **AO attenuates DIRECT SUN on terrain**; `aoStrength` 0.9 and `csStrength` 0.72 are the whole of the compensation and their comments say exactly that. **(9) RN-340, THE MATERIAL-RESPONSE CENSUS, decoded from the shipped PNGs rather than read off the generator.** Effective roughness is `material.roughness * ormG`. **`panel`, which is every machine, plate, steel and suit surface in the game, has a p05..p95 effective roughness band 0.032 wide**, which under a moving sun is indistinguishable from a constant, and that is the plastic read on the manufactured half of the world. **Metalness is a decoration and not a signal: three of the four ORM maps are literally constant 255 in blue**, so the only spatially varying metalness anywhere is `panel`, and 91.1 per cent of that is at identity. **And `coarse`, the family with the most screen area (rock, soil, sand, regolith, coal), has the LEAST relief in the set: mean normal tilt 7.7 degrees and p95 14.8 degrees, against bark's 22.8 and 65.7.** Ore is the one family that behaves like a material (roughness standard deviation 0.174, driven by an explicit glint mask). Five materials draw with Lambert and have no specular term at all, two of them large-area: the ore-patch decal and the near voxel terrain. **The terrain itself is pure Lambert with no specular lobe, no roughness and no metalness**, which is the single largest surface in the frame that cannot respond like a material, and it needs a DW-10 argument rather than a tweak. **NOT CHANGED THIS PASS; the `coarse` normal strength is the cheapest of these and is one constant in `texgen._coarse_masks`.** **(10) CONTROLS AND HYGIENE.** One binary per claim; `npm run sync-assets` before every served comparison; port 4200 never touched; my own port killed by PID and confirmed gone before serving, and **the `--strictPort` trap fired once and was caught** (the new preview refused to start, the OLD server kept answering 200, and the tell was that the frame still had the old floor in it). Freshness proved against HEAD rather than by boot line: served wasm byte-identical to `HEAD:web/wasm/dist/of-core.wasm`, bundle "client expects 21" against `OF_ABI_VERSION = 21`. tsc proven alive with a negative control before it was relied on (`TS2322` by name at `PostDefaults.ts:173`, then reverted byte-identical). Zero em dashes verified in Python per file. Index empty before and after via `git diff --cached --name-status`. **`run.mjs` carried ANOTHER lane's uncommitted `trees` / `treedensity` / `spires` / `forestdetail` whitelist entries, so it was committed as a FILTERED BLOB of HEAD plus my own hunks and their work was left in the working tree for them.** **(11) NOT DONE, NAMED, IN THE ORDER I WOULD DO THEM. (a)** The AO and contact screen clamps in section 8, priced at Forest and Plains. **(b)** The two card-mask defects Admin ruled mine and I did not reach: `of_leaf_a.png`'s bottom row is 22.7 per cent opaque so every leaf strip is cut away at its base, and `_grass_strips` authors 11 blades on a 0.0455 half-pitch at 0.058 to 0.082 half-widths so the roots overlap into a MAT with zero transparent columns. Both are in `texgen.py`, whose entire input closure is itself and which is committed and clean, so regeneration is safe; note that `GRASS_BAND_HALF_U = 0.045` in `props_common.py` is coupled to the blade pitch, so every Grass-bearing asset needs a rebuild if the blade COUNT changes, and that grass coverage measures 0.5949 against a check floor of 0.55, i.e. 0.045 of headroom before narrowing a blade trips the gate. **(c)** Card HUE and within-card value variance, per section 7. **(d)** The `coarse` normal strength. **(e)** The terrain's absent specular lobe. **(f)** A dark scribble artefact on the near ground, plainly visible in every floor frame and attributed in `docs/screenshots/RN347_forestfloor_{notex,norelief}.png`.

No renderer and no lighting, so a geometry pass can run ahead of look development. `--foliage` reports WG-14's bare-trunk ratio off the exported bytes. **Twelve yaws, 256 grid, HEAD against now: Canopy_Pine width cv 0.0539 to 0.1437 / IoU 0.845 to 0.465; Canopy_Broadleaf 0.0789 to 0.0828 / IoU 0.658 to 0.381; Canopy_Fir 0.0125 to 0.0975 / IoU 0.822 to 0.617; TreeConifer 0.0202 to 0.0686 / IoU 0.668 to 0.549; TreeBroadleaf 0.0424 to 0.0888 / IoU 0.607 to 0.501.** IoU 1.000 is the defect. The fir's projected width used to move 1.2 percent over a whole revolution, which is faceting and nothing else. **(3) RN-272 / RN-280 / RN-281 / RN-283, THE GEOMETRY.** Crowns are heavy BOUGHS (new `tree_common.limb`, a tapered tube swept along a polyline, and `tree_common.arc`, a path that rises, flattens and lets its outer end fall) at uneven azimuths and unequal reach, clothed ALONG their length by overlapping foliage clumps, plus a bare or broken limb on every tree. Reach carries TWO harmonics of azimuth: the first leans the crown off the axis (drives IoU), the second makes it elliptical in plan (drives width). Trunks: five rings for a curved taper instead of two for a constant one, per-ring `offsets` for a real sweep (`lean` interpolates ONE displacement and can only make a tilted dowel), a coherent azimuthal RIDGE running the length of the stem in the same direction as RN-100's bark fissures, and a lobed root FLARE. **Ridge, flare and sweep cost ZERO triangles: they reshape rings that already existed.** The conifer also gains three real boughs inside its crown, because RN-69's 121 blades all sprang straight off the trunk. **(4) RN-273, THE STRUCTURAL FINDING: `Parts.fit` INTO A SQUARE BOX NORMALISES AWAY PLAN ANISOTROPY.** It scales X and Y independently to fill `size` exactly, so the first draft rebuilt all three canopy crowns out of asymmetric boughs and still measured a plan aspect of **1.019** on the pine, with width cv 0.023 even though yaw-to-yaw IoU had already collapsed from 0.845 to 0.352. > **RN-96 to RN-99 (2026-07-29): THE FOLIAGE MOVES, AND THE INSTRUMENT THAT PROVES IT HAS AN EXACTLY ZERO FLOOR.** Reid asked for "grass blowing in a gentle breeze and leaves on the tree", and it ships as VERTEX SHADER work, never a mixer (props_common.py:41 already said so in 2026-07). **(1) THE MECHANISM.** One shared `onBeforeCompile` (`web/src/render/instancing/PropWind.ts`) assigned to the eight foliage prop batch materials (`isFoliageMaterial`, the SAME predicate the base bake imports, so a rock can never inherit a breeze) and to `nodes:flat:matte` (the harvest trees' merged leaves; the five node kinds are trees plus four boulder kinds, so `flat` cannot hold a non-plant). Injected after `#include <begin_vertex>` where `transformed` and `batchingMatrix` are both in scope; amplitude is LINEAR IN `transformed.y`, metres above the prop's own base (both normalize() paths bake ground-pivoted geometry), so **displacement is zero at the ground BY CONSTRUCTION** and "grass detaches from the ground plane" is unreachable; reach is `min(h,1) + 0.15*max(h-1,0)`, so a 0.6 m grass tip moves ~4 cm and a 12 m canopy crown ~18 cm, the same order as the authored (and never-read) `Tree_Sway` clip's 17 cm. Trunks are never hooked (Bark is not foliage), which retires "the whole tree slides". Per-instance phase is a dot on the batching matrix TRANSLATION, position not spawn time, so a probe's matched pair survives streaming order; time is `Loop.simSecs` pushed in `Systems.ts` beside `TerrainMaterials.update`, so pausing the sim stops the breeze. **(2) DW-10 BOTH WAYS: 4 ShaderMaterial + 2 live onBeforeCompile with wind on, 4 + 1 with `?wind=0`,** because the flag never assigns the hook and the program set is stock. The RN-52-shape argument: a sway moves vertices so post cannot do it; no existing custom shader draws a foliage triangle; a ShaderMaterial replacement would forfeit three's lighting, shadows, batching and Surfaces bindings to buy nothing. One shared function object means one program cache key: **programs read 37 with wind on AND off.** **(3) THE INSTRUMENT.** `of.framehash` renders synchronously and advances no ticks; `__ofWind.freeze(t)` pins the wind clock; so two captures at two frozen wind times differ by NOTHING except the sway, and the floor is not small, it is zero. `probes/wind.js`, RN-15 camera, 160x90 tiles, freeze pair 1.6 s apart: **6,698 of 14,400 tiles move, 3,196 lighter against 3,502 darker (BOTH WAYS, the silhouette rule), 98.98% inside the props-hidden mask; props hidden, two wind times hash IDENTICAL; `windamp=0`, hash IDENTICAL (the hook alone moves no pixel); `?wind=0`, zero hooks and bit-exact stillness.** Invariants IDENTICAL both ways: 78 calls, 1,001,122 triangles, 37 programs, 52 geometries, 104.2 MB. **Zero draw calls, zero VRAM, zero triangles, zero programs, zero new attributes** (the amplitude coordinate was already on the GPU, the fourth time this lane has cashed that cheque). **(4) MY SKY CONTROL WAS BROKEN THE SAME WAY RN-45's WAS, AND THE REPLACEMENT ASSUMES NO GEOMETRY.** The first probe asserted a fixed top-of-frame "pure sky" band moved zero tiles; it failed with 512 moved, because at this camera the hillside rises and canopy crowns stand in those rows (98.98% of them inside the prop mask, so nothing had escaped; the band had stopped being sky, INSTRUMENTS.md's opening entry). Replaced by the props-hidden identity above. **At the spawn clearing that same control INVERTS BY DESIGN and becomes the harvest-tree measurement:** `propsVisible` does not hide `NodeBatch`, so with the scatter hidden and the arms frozen, **127 tiles still move, 55 up / 72 down, peak 23.9: pure crown sway of `nodes:flat:matte`** with everything else excluded by construction (`trees:true` mode). **(5) STATED LIMITS, NOT OVERSIGHTS:** cast shadows do not sway (the depth material is not hooked; at <=18 cm the static shadow is below notice, and hooking three's depth material would spend real complexity on it); a floating-origin rebase (4 km) re-seeds phases, a re-decorrelation and not a pop; normals are not bent by the sway; screenshot pairs across page loads (RN99_*, RN100_*) sit on the ~0.13% cross-load floor and are illustration, the in-page freeze numbers are the claim. Blade reach varies by nearly 2x inside one whorl and consecutive whorls disagree on their nominal radius on purpose, so the outline is sawtoothed and no two whorls are concentric; each blade kinks twice so the flank has two slope changes instead of one straight cone edge; **the bark trunk is now visible THROUGH the crown** and a green leader runs past the trunk top, which is the strongest conifer cue in the asset and was previously buried inside the tiers. > **RN-64 to RN-67 (2026-07-28): THE PROPS GET A GROUND UNDER THEM, AND THE 3.2x THAT SENT ME LOOKING FOR IT WAS THE FIRST-PERSON ARMS.** **(1) RN-66 IS THE FINDING AND IT IS AN INSTRUMENT ONE.** RN-60 reported the prop band swinging 71.4 counts across a sun sweep where the ground swings 22.4, a 3.2x disagreement, and every conclusion after it rested on that number. The band it called "ground" was defined as the tiles props never touch, at pitch -10. At that pitch those tiles are the sky above the horizon and the ANIMATED FIRST-PERSON ARMS along the bottom, and the arms are drawn in the view-model pass, which has its own sun, its own hemisphere at 1.1 in warm colours and no scattering integral at all, so the control barely responds to the sun BY CONSTRUCTION. **Measured at the same site with the same sun: the band reads 110.7 counts at dawn against 137.7 at its brightest when the camera is pitched -10, and 27.2 against 110.4 when it is pitched -30. Terrain does not brighten fourfold because the camera tilted twenty degrees.** Against real ground the same quantity is **0.10 of normalised response, not 0.44**. `proplight.js` now excludes the arms BY THEIR OWN SIGNATURE rather than by a screen rectangle (a rectangle is a constant that goes stale, which is INSTRUMENTS.md's opening entry): they are the only thing that moves while camera, sun and world are pinned, so two captures one settled frame apart differ exactly where they are. And it asserts the property RN-60 needed: **a sweep that takes the sun to 2.5 degrees removes the direct term, so any surface that sun lights must lose most of its light, and a control band keeping four fifths of its peak at dawn is not that surface.** It **fails BY NAME on RN-60's own configuration (0.8043)** and passes at -30 (0.246). **I WROTE ONE ASSERTION BEFORE THAT AND IT WAS WRONG,** recorded because the mistake is the useful part: "the control sits higher in the frame than the props standing on it" reads like sky contamination and is in fact what happens whenever the camera looks DOWN, since distant ground is at the top and the near understorey at the bottom. A rule whose answer cannot express the failure is the set-versus-order entry with a different subject. Left in as a published field, not as a check. **(2) RN-64, THE GROUND HALF OF THE ENVIRONMENT, AND THE TRACED MECHANISM WAS INVERTED.** The handed-over diagnosis was "sky above and nothing below", so props have an empty lower hemisphere where `TerrainShader` has `ground * (1 - skyView)`. First half right, second half not: **the lower hemisphere is not empty, it holds the sky model MARCHED THROUGH THE PLANET**, which accumulates a real reddish in-scatter worth about **seventeen times** the true ground bounce at the Hills site. Every prop, tree, pebble and machine is lit from below by an integral of atmosphere taken inside the rock. So the fix makes props DARKER on dark ground and BRIGHTER on bright ground, **and the sign flipping with the biome is the assertion rather than the magnitude, because that is what a ground bounce IS and what no tuned constant could do**: same code, same constants, matched pairs at dawn, **Hills (0x6f7346) prop band 17.696 to 13.980; Polar (0xe8eef2, snow) 115.124 to 118.849.** **(3) WHERE THE RADIANCE COMES FROM AND WHY IT IS NOT A TUNED CONSTANT.** Term for term `TerrainShader`'s own `ground`: the albedo is the biome's palette entry from `biomeColorArray`, indexed by the `/core` `biomeAt` classifier under the observer, i.e. `vBiomeColor` and not a tint; the bracket is `uAmbient + skyAmb + sunT * 1.45 * max(dot(up, sunDir), 0)`, computed by the shared `Atmosphere.glsl` model IN THE SHADER and not on the CPU. The three surface constants move into new `TerrainAmbient.ts` and are **shared BY REFERENCE** with both terrain materials on `createAtmosphereUniforms`' precedent; `TerrainShader`'s two `1.45` literals now interpolate the same exported constant and emit the same characters, so the compiled program is unchanged. **The one term not carried over is `shadow`**: a cascade lookup needs a position and this is one radiance for the whole hemisphere, so it is the UNSHADOWED flat ground, and the error errs toward too much bounce inside a shadow where the direct term is already gone. **(4) RN-65, THE WIRING DIAGNOSIS, AND WHY THE FIRST DESIGN WAS THROWN AWAY.** It was a second mesh interposed into the sky scene for one capture, which is the stronger confinement, and it rendered correctly (forced visible it paints the lower hemisphere with the horizon exactly where it belongs). **A FORTY-fold change in its radiance moved the prop band by 0.05 of a count.** A changed input that does not change the output is a wiring diagnosis and never a small effect, so the ground half moved onto the one mesh the capture has always worked from and the graph question disappeared. `?iblgroundamp=` stays as the instrument that made that call: at 0 / 1 / 8 the prop band reads **13.748 / 13.984 / 15.510**. **(5) INVARIANTS, RN-15 camera, ONE binary, `?iblground=0` against default: draw calls 78 to 78, triangles 1,021,918 to 1,021,918, geometries 52 to 52, textures 88 to 88, programs 37 to 37, VRAM est 93.7 to 93.7 MB, ibl rebuild 0.6 to 0.7 ms, `groundBuilds` 0 to 5** (a COUNTER not a flag, on RN-58's `grabs` precedent). **DW-10 UNCHANGED at 4 `ShaderMaterial` + 1 live `onBeforeCompile`**: ground mode is a UNIFORM branch inside the sky shader that already existed, not a define and not a second shader, and **programs reading 37 both ways is what proves the branch did not fork the program**. **(6) WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX, STATED PLAINLY.** Reid's complaint is that props read too dark, and at a dark biome this change makes them darker because it removes light that was never physical. The residual prop-against-ground response gap after the instrument is fixed is 0.10 normalised at Hills and up to 0.25 at a second camera, and **it is NOT the ground bounce**: the ground bounce is multiplied by `1 - skyView`, which is zero for the flat facets that dominate terrain, so it was never what kept the terrain lit at dawn. The remaining suspects, in the order I would take them, are the prop sun being `3.0 * smoothstep(elev, -0.12, 0.15)` with a hand-lerped orange where the terrain sun is `1.45 * ndl * ofAtmoSunTransmittance`, and the env map's sky half being uncalibrated against the terrain's `uSkyAmbient` 0.32. **At Reid's 9-degree candidate site `k` is already 1.0, so the elevation dimmer is not the mechanism there.** Isolation: `?iblground=0 ?iblgroundamp=`, both registered in `run.mjs`. New: `web/src/render/materials/TerrainAmbient.ts`. Screenshots `docs/screenshots/RN64_{hills,polar,rn15cam}_{0,1}.png`. Commit `21fbfc0`.

So beyond ~57 m of spawn there is nothing to accumulate into a treeline: **no silhouette work can ever produce a horizon mass**, because there are no trees out there to form one. That is placement, not asset quality; Admin scoped it to world-gen as a separate lane. **(2) THE NEAR-BLACK BOULDERS ARE NOT A LIGHTING MISMATCH, and I predicted they were.** New probe `probes/proplight.js` sweeps the sun and finds prop pixels BY DIFFERENCE (capture with props shown and hidden; tiles that moved are prop tiles, tiles that moved not at all are pure ground, mixed tiles discarded), so neither band is a hand-picked rectangle. Two controls green: the visibility toggle returns the bit-identical frame, and both surfaces genuinely respond. **Two sites mattered and one would have given a confident wrong answer in either direction.** At high sun the Mountains site reads prop 96.37 against ground 96.13 (agreement to a quarter of a count) while Hills reads 60.97 against 123.41 - the Hills gap is ALBEDO, grass being brighter than rock. Every baseline frame was shot at sunT 0.30 where the two models agree to 0.02 of full range, so the dark boulders are albedo and material (`OF_RockDark` 0x57534C). R8 doing real work on a lighting claim rather than a geometric one. **(3) BUT A REAL SYSTEMIC DISAGREEMENT EXISTS AND IT IS ABOUT THE INDIRECT TERM, NOT THE SUN.** Reproduced at both sites, worst normalised gap 0.42 and 0.48, always at LOW sun; the prop band swings 71.4 counts across the sweep at Mountains where the ground swings 22.4, i.e. **3.2x**. `TerrainShader` gives itself a sky-ambient integral plus RN-30's bounce; props get three's ambient and an IBL and nothing else. **Every prop, tree, pebble and machine crushes toward black at dawn and dusk while the ground stays lit.** Bears directly on Reid's live golden-hour spawn choice: one candidate site sits at 9 degrees maximum sun elevation, which would make that defect permanent. Next commit, reachable via `SkyIbl` and `envMapIntensity` without touching `Systems.ts`. **(4) RN-61: the clone army is gone.** `NodeBatch` never called `setColorAt` at all, so 14 trees were two meshes at a literal scale of 1.0 in one colour, differing only in yaw. Added `NodeBatch.tint` (build-time only) plus one colour PER PLACEMENT applied across that placement's slots - trunk and canopy are separate material batches, so tinting them independently would drift a tree's bark from its own leaves and read as a broken asset. Deliberately NOT a call into `ScatterLook.tintFor`: the flower branch would put a 1.70/1.50/0.38 yellow on a whole conifer, and that value range (0.80-1.18) at tree size reads as a lighting bug. Per-instance tree size 0.86-1.14, bounded because **`art.radiusM` and `art.hitUpM` do not scale with it**, so a big and a small tree are chopped from the same distance; at +/-14% that is under aim tolerance, at +/-40% it would be a gameplay bug wearing an art change's clothes. Verified numerically because the eye would have said "no change": **2.48% of scene pixels (13,514 of 544,000) move by >6 counts, max channel delta 180**. Invariants: draw calls 65 -> 65, triangles 641k -> 641k, VRAM 93.7 -> 93.7 MB. **(5) THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE ROCK SAMENESS, STATED PRECISELY.** Every rock in the game is `harvest_common.lobe()`, a single-valued radial sweep about a vertical axis, **topologically incapable of an overhang, cleft or undercut**; all four ore boulders are the SAME 164 triangles with different material dressing. Canopies are closed solids with zero sky-through. Neither is reachable by a fragment shader, which is the honest converse of the RN-45 strata win (a cliff IS terrain, so one edit reached every face; a boulder is a genuine prop and what is wrong with it is its outline). **DW-10 ledger UNCHANGED at 4 ShaderMaterial + 1 live `onBeforeCompile`, and this pass is not expected to spend a slot.** **(6) THE THIRD ALREADY-UPLOADED ATTRIBUTE NOBODY WAS READING.** `PropGeometry.bakeColour` is gated on `isFoliageMaterial`, so `OF_Rock`, `OF_RockDark`, `OF_Regolith` and `OF_Bark` carry a constant-255 vertex colour with nothing writing it - after RN-50's per-quad UV and the node instance colour, that shape has now paid out three times and is worth a positive entry in `INSTRUMENTS.md`, which is currently all failures. **DEAD WEIGHT, recorded so nobody spends a day on it:** every `_LOD1`, `_LOD2` and `_Stump` in the node files is contract-required and **never rendered** (`NodeBatch` draws LOD0 at every distance), and `bush_scrub.glb`, `water_pool.glb` and `oil_seep.glb` ship, validate and are never loaded. Trees are NOT triangle-constrained: conifer 584 of a 900 budget, broadleaf 452 of 1000, 14 trees = 8,176 triangles in a ~1 M frame. > **RN-50 (2026-07-28): THE DETAIL BUMP SHIPS, ON A COORDINATE THAT WAS ALREADY ON THE GPU, AND THE PER-CHUNK PHASE IS A CAPABILITY WE DID NOT NEED YET.** Admin asked me to MEASURE both the UV route and world-gen's per-chunk phase before committing to either. The UV route wins for this term. WG-56 found that every chunk already carries a per-quad normalised UV, in the wire format, in the batch attributes, written per slot, uploaded and interpolated every frame, and that `TerrainShader.ts` contained the string `uv` **exactly zero times**. It is the well-conditioned coordinate `pM` is not, because it is LOCAL: one uint16 step is 0.883 mm on a depth-14 chunk, a quarter of a ground pixel at 2 m, against `pM`'s quantum of nearly nine pixels there. **MEASURED, one binary, RN-15 camera, 1280x720, props hidden, matched pairs one settled frame apart, noise floor exactly 0.0000: the bump moves 75.4% of the near band at a mean of 6.32 counts, 67.6% of the mid at 5.35, 51.7% of the far at 3.88, and 0.0% of the horizon at 0.0007.** The horizon reading is the one that matters: the term fades itself on the PIXEL FOOTPRINT, so it is gone before a triangle is a few pixels wide, and that is now measured rather than argued. The arcs are gone (`RN50_uvbump.png` against `RN45_iso_bump.png`, same camera, same flags, bump alone). **I WALKED INTO WORLD-GEN'S TRAP AND CAUGHT IT BEFORE MEASURING.** The obvious version keeps the macro field in the bump's height and merely adds a UV octave; that scores 0.00% dead quads, identical to a correct fix, and is still visibly wrong, because a quantised octave ANYWHERE in the sum poisons the derivative of the whole sum. `hArt` now feeds the COLOUR and never the bump, and every octave the derivative sees is on the UV: two, at 14.0 and 5.3 over the quad (4.1 m and 10.9 m at depth 14), neither a power of two because a lattice aligned to the 32-cell grid would draw the grid. **THE HONEST COST, and why this does NOT replace the phase:** the UV normalises over the QUAD, so the detail's world size doubles at every LOD step. Tolerable for THIS term only because it is well conditioned solely within about 20 to 45 m, where the streamer is at max depth, so the step falls outside the band. Any future field needing a derivative at range still wants the phase. **RN-45's ARITHMETIC CORRECTED: the quantum is 0.03125 m, not 0.0625** (I quoted the worst case; a generic point on a 600 km sphere sits one binade lower). Conclusion unchanged, and the corrected figure explains the SHAPE: 8.77x the ground pixel at 2 m and 0.55x at 8 m, which is why it was a near-field band that STOPPED rather than a fade. **TWO ENVIRONMENT DEFECTS, both of which cost a measurement.** (1) `npx vite build` SKIPS `sync-wasm`, which `npm run build` runs as a prebuild step; another lane bumped the client to ABI 19 mid-session, my builds kept a wasm at 18, a binary silently failed to boot, a `--out` screenshot never wrote, and I compared two images that were THE SAME FILE and concluded an amplitude change had done nothing. **Identical output from a changed input is a wiring diagnosis, never a coincidence**, and that rule paid three times tonight. (2) The disk filled to 7.2 MB free of 931 GB from accumulated `dist-*` directories across every lane; I deleted only my own. **`Scatter.ts` is 398 lines and UNDER the 400 cap**, better than the 409 it started the night at, repaying the 3 lines RN-48/49 added. No file was split. **NOT DONE: water polish (surface motion, glint, refraction across the waterline, shoreline) is still untouched, and `WaterSurface.ts` is under `web/src/world/` which is world-gen's, so the surface half needs an ownership ruling; the post-stack half is mine and is the next thing I would take.**

THE REORDER: ITEM 1 AND ITEM 3 OF THE BRIEF ARE THE SAME SHADER EDIT, BECAUSE IN THIS ENGINE A CLIFF IS TERRAIN AND NOT A PROP.** Admin ranked rocks and cliffs first and the terrain material third. Most of that gap is the BIOME props' LOD2, which has been shipping since W4. A control that removes more than the change removed is not a control. **(2) RN-45b, THE TERRAIN SURFACE ART: A MACRO VARIATION FIELD AND ROCK STRATA SHIP; THE DETAIL BUMP IS A MEASURED NEGATIVE RESULT AND IS DEFAULTED TO ZERO.** New `web/src/render/materials/TerrainArt.glsl.ts`, called from the existing terrain `ShaderMaterial`. **The DW-10 ledger is UNCHANGED at 3 `ShaderMaterial` plus 3 `onBeforeCompile`**: this edits a custom shader that already existed and adds no program, no draw call, no texture and no byte of VRAM (69/40/51/93.7 identical with the terms on and off). The noise phase is PLANET-CENTRED METRES and not engine space, because engine space rebases and a field keyed on it would swim across the ground every time the floating origin moved. **TWO INDEPENDENT CONFINEMENTS, and they are not the same reason:** a compile-time `#ifndef OF_SCALED` keeps it out of the far scaled scene where a 12 m octave is far below one pixel (confinement by the call graph, RN-30's rule), and a distance fade completing at 4 km against a ~15 km handover is what prevents a SEAM, since a ridge modulated on one side of the handover and flat on the other is the failure a define cannot catch. **MEASURED, one binary, five states each one settled frame apart through `window.__ofTerrainArt`, props hidden, RN-15 camera, 1280x720, two repetitions bit-identical: the macro field moves 99.6% of the near band, 89.9% of the mid, 81.3% of the far and 54.2% of the horizon, by means of 5.86 / 4.99 / 4.65 / 3.51 counts, and ADDS 0.72 / 1.25 / 3.59 / 2.43 counts of 16x16 block-mean spread against a measured noise floor of 0.0000.** At the Mountains spawn the same term reads block-mean spread gains of x1.42 / x2.07 / x2.27 / x1.32. **THE LEVEL IS THE CONTROL AND IT DID ITS JOB TWICE.** A variation layer must raise the SPREAD and leave the LEVEL where it was, and the first tint pair (0.86,1.00,0.90) against (1.12,1.03,0.84) had a per-channel mean of (0.99, 1.015, 0.87), i.e. a 13% net blue reduction applied to the whole planet, which the probe caught as a 5.03% drop in the mid band's level while its spread rose. The pair is now reciprocal about 1.0. The residual per-band level shift is NOT a bias and that was established rather than argued: it scales LINEARLY with amplitude (mid -2.79% at 1.0 against -1.37% at 0.5, a factor of 2.04 where a tone-curve Jensen term would give 4), the field's own mean is 0.000056 over 200,000 samples computed offline in float64, and **the shift FLIPS SIGN between sites (-2.79% at Hills, +2.63% at the Mountains spawn)**, so it is which lobe of the field that patch of ground is sitting on. That is not a defect, it IS the effect. **I was wrong twice about this mechanism before measuring it, and both wrong explanations were plausible.** **(3) THE DETAIL BUMP DOES NOT WORK ON THIS PLANET, AND THE REASON IS ARITHMETIC.** A Mikkelsen surface-gradient bump from screen derivatives, needing no tangents and no UVs and costing two `dFdx` pairs on a field already evaluated. It produced a field of concentric moire arcs across the ground within about fifteen metres of the eye, **and no number saw it: it moved 35% of the near band with a healthy peak either way. A screenshot caught it (`docs/screenshots/RN45_iso_bump.png`), which is DW-7's rule and RN-15's.** A footprint fade was tried FIRST and did nothing, which is what forced the real diagnosis. `pM` is float32 and about 6e5 at Forge's surface, so one ULP is 2^(19-23) = **0.0625 m**, while at the pinned camera one pixel covers **4.3 mm of ground at 2 m and 21.5 mm at 5 m**: the quantum is 3 to 15 times the pixel footprint, whole runs of adjacent pixels sample the SAME quantised position, `dFdx` of the field is exactly zero across them and steps at the quantisation boundaries, and those boundaries are surfaces of constant range from the eye, which is why the artefact is arcs centred on the player. It is not fadeable: the term is well conditioned only once the footprint clears the quantum (about 20 m) and starts aliasing its own 4.2 m octave once the footprint passes a third of that wavelength (about 45 m), and a 25 m annulus is a band of ground rather than a surface treatment. **Left in the build behind `?bumpamp=1` because the measurement is the deliverable. THE MACRO COLOUR TERM IS UNAFFECTED and ships, because it reads the field's VALUE, where 0.0625 m against an 11.9 m finest octave is 0.5% of a wavelength; only the DERIVATIVE is destroyed.** **DEPENDENCY ON WORLD-GEN, stated rather than faked: sub-metre terrain detail of any kind needs a per-chunk phase reduced modulo the octave period on the CPU in float64 and carried with the integer cell index, so the shader adds a small local offset to a small local coordinate and never forms a 6e5 intermediate. That is a terrain-chunk format change.** **(4) ROCK STRATA, the cliff half, at essentially zero cost.** Beds are quantised from `vRelief` (metres above the datum, already a varying), WARPED by a low-frequency noise so they tilt and thicken instead of reading as a contour map, given a per-bed tone and an iron-versus-grey hue from a hash of the integer bed index, and separated by a dark parting at each contact, which is most of what says "layered" at 100 m after the tonal difference has washed out. (b) The sky control was a band of the shooting frame, which is sky at Hills and is mountains at the 4,668 m spawn, so the probe reported the term had escaped into the sky when the BAND had stopped being sky; it is now taken at pitch +72 over the top 45% of the frame, which is sky at every site and every altitude, and reads **mean 0.0000 and peak 0 over 648,000 px at BOTH sites**. (d) A noise floor was added and the FIRST version of it read EXACTLY equal to the effect it was bounding, to four decimal places, on every band, because the state was not reset before the floor capture. **Two numbers agreeing to the last digit is a wiring diagnosis, never a coincidence.** With it fixed the floor is 0.0000 and every claim is asserted against it rather than against an unreachable zero. **(8) RN-47, THE UNDERWATER VIEW, AND THE APPROVED DW-10 SLOT WAS NOT SPENT.** Admin approved one scene shader slot for water. It was built as a POST pass instead, so the ledger is untouched: RN-10 established post programs cannot be infected by the depth policy (no projection, no depth test, no `gl_FragDepth`), and a post pass also reaches the terrain, the props, the machines and the scatter at once with no per-material edit, using the depth buffer a scene material would have had to recompute. Beer-Lambert per channel with red absorbed roughly 22x harder than blue (Smith and Baker 1981), the water surface treated as a PLANE because curvature over a 22 m pond is under a millimetre, and the exit distance `headUnderM / max(dot(rd, up), eps)` giving the same confined-layer structure the aerial perspective already uses. **Measured, eye 1.346 m under, 921,600 px: red over blue 1.0493 to 0.5813, mean red -44.34 against mean blue +3.36, 81.2% of pixels moved, peak 152.** **The negative controls are BIT-EXACT rather than approximate**, because screenshots cannot reach zero here (sim time advances between captures) so they were taken on `of.framehash()`, which renders and reads back synchronously: dry at 300 m gives the identical hash `3035253034` both ways, and WADING at 1.0 m depth with `headUnderM` -0.62 gives the identical hash `1014643489`, while the same instrument submerged gives two different hashes. The wading control is the sharper one: a pass keyed on "is the player wet" passes the dry control and fails that. Above water the pass is SKIPPED rather than multiplied by one. **Cost: +3 post draw calls and +3 programs when submerged, ZERO when dry, +3.5 MB allocated lazily on the first submerged frame.** It also caught a framebuffer feedback loop the same way RN-10 did: the first shape reported `ran: true`, counted its draws and moved exactly zero pixels while the driver emitted 256 `GL_INVALID_OPERATION` per frame. **NOT DONE, and named: the first-person arms are not attenuated (they are drawn after the interpose point, so it needs a second interpose); the water plane has no lateral bound, so a level ray inside a shallow puddle stays submerged past the bank; a free camera is never tinted because `swim()` needs a capsule; and there is still no surface seen from beneath.** **NOT COMMITTED, DELIBERATELY: `web/src/app/Boot.ts`.** It carries the vessel lane's uncommitted `resumeWorld` call, whose `ResumeBoot.ts` is still UNTRACKED, so a commit of Boot.ts alone would not build. My two hunks there are three lines and will ride with that lane's commit. Every other file is committed path-limited. New: `web/src/render/materials/TerrainArt.glsl.ts`, `web/src/render/post/UnderwaterGlsl.ts`, `web/src/render/post/UnderwaterPass.ts`, `web/tools/smoke/probes/{terrainart,artshot,underwater}.js`. Isolation: `?terrainart=0 ?macrovar=0 ?terrainbump=0 ?strata=0 ?macroamp= ?bumpamp= ?strataamp= ?proplod2=0 ?grassshort=0 ?scatterwet=1 ?underwater=0 ?uwext= ?uwtint= ?uwscatter= ?uwpath=`, all registered in `run.mjs`. Runtime handles `window.__ofTerrainArt.{set,get,reset}` and `window.__ofUnderwater.{set,state,setTune}`. > **RN-30 (2026-07-27): THE GROUND STOPS BEING FLAT, AND THE AERIAL-PERSPECTIVE TERM LANDS ON THE SECOND ATTEMPT BECAUSE THE CONFINEMENT CHANGED RATHER THAN THE TUNING.** Three changes, one binary pair plus a one-binary isolation series, and the headline is that all three sky controls read **exactly 0.0000 mean and 0 peak over 276,480 samples**. RN-15 bought 3.7x the foliage by taking the understorey out of the shadow pass, and the picture paid for it: every grass shadow in the frame went with the 12.3 ms. **(1) SHADOW CONTACT COMES BACK AS TWO COMPLEMENTARY TERMS, NEITHER OF WHICH IS A CASCADE, AND THE REASON IT IS NOT A CASCADE WAS CHECKED IN THREE'S SOURCE RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** `WebGLShadowMap.renderObject` filters casters with `object.layers.test( camera.layers )` at r185 line 511, where `camera` is the VIEW camera passed to `shadowMap.render( shadowsArray, scene, camera )`, **not** the per-light shadow camera, so `light.shadow.camera.layers` is never consulted anywhere in the shadow pass and layers cannot select a cascade. `Object3D.onBeforeShadow` does fire per object per light but at lines 535/549, i.e. AFTER the `castShadow` test, so it cannot veto a draw either; the only supported per-cascade signal is `_frustum.intersectsObject`, and the understorey is ONE `BatchedMesh` whose bound covers the whole ring, so every cascade intersects it. "Understorey in cascade 0 only" needs a fork of three's shadow map. **This also convicts a live comment in my own lane's code: `ShadowRig.ts:59-73` asserts exactly the layer behaviour disproved above and enables `LAYER_PLAYER_BODY`/`LAYER_PROPS` on cascade 0's shadow camera to buy a restriction it does not buy.** The props and the player reach the shadow map because `CameraRig` enables those layers on the NEAR camera. The code is harmless, the comment is false, and the 45-to-27 draw-call measurement recorded beside it was real with another cause. So: **(1a) A BASE-CONTACT GRADIENT BAKED INTO THE FOLIAGE VERTICES, at literally zero cost.** A plant is darker where it meets the ground because the ground and its own neighbours occlude the sky there; that is an ambient-occlusion fact about the ASSET, so it belongs in the asset's vertices. `PropGeometry.bakeColour` writes 0.42 over the bottom 38% of each geometry's own height, smoothstepped, into the per-vertex colour attribute **that already existed and was a constant 255**. No draw call, no triangle, no shader, no uniform, not one extra byte. It survives per-instance tinting because three composes `vColor = 1` then `vColor.rgb *= color` then `vColor *= getBatchingColor(...)`, so the gradient and `PropLibrary.tint` MULTIPLY (`color_vertex.glsl.js`, read rather than assumed). **Measured: near band mean darkening 0.0323, p99 0.3705, 17.9% of pixels moved over 236,195 px; mid band 0.0348 / 0.3861 / 25.4%; 7 batches carry it.** **(1b) SCREEN-SPACE CONTACT SHADOWS, `post/ContactGlsl.ts` plus `post/ContactPass.ts`, two full-screen passes.** A depth-buffer march toward the sun bounded to 0.45 m of WORLD distance, which is what makes it a contact shadow rather than a shadow: it physically cannot see a hill, so it cannot disagree with the cascaded maps about one. It divides from cascade 0 by RANGE exactly as the baked ORM map divides from SSAO by spatial frequency, and cascade 0 at a +/-15.8 m box and 15.5 mm per texel cannot resolve a 3-triangle blade against the soil under it. **Measured: near band mean darkening 0.1012, p99 0.6581, 40.4% of pixels moved over 237,762 px; mid band 0.0521 / 0.3744 / 42.4%.** The sun direction is derived from `shadowCascade0`'s own position minus its target, which is not a second authority because ShadowRig already merged the sun and cascade 0 into one light; when the rig is built disabled the vector is zero and the march skips, so `?shadows=0` also removes contact shadows, which is correct rather than incidental. **(2) THE UNDERSTOREY STOPS READING AS A CROP FIELD, and the durable half of the fix is structural rather than a smaller number.** RN-15 had already retuned the height jitter once for this (1.48 down to 1.30) and it did not hold, because the jitter COMPOUNDS with the distance upscale: `Detail_GrassCardB`'s authored 0.60 m reached 0.60 x 1.3 x 1.30 x 1.32 = **1.34 m**, chest height on a 1.8 m character, and a field of 1.3 m blades has no middle distance in it. The band drops to 0.40 to 0.82 AND `DETAIL_FAR_GROW` is demoted to a HORIZONTAL upscale, so height is no longer a factor in that product at all. **Density-weighted mean understorey height 0.4262 m to 0.2811 m (-34.0%); tallest card in the world 1.34 m to 0.64 m (-52%).** Coverage is held rather than spent: the width band gains 1.18x, and measured screen coverage moves 0.5503 to 0.5456 across three repetitions each, i.e. -0.9%. Capping a product by shrinking one factor has to be repeated every time either factor moves; taking a factor out of the product holds. **(3) AERIAL PERSPECTIVE SHIPS, AND THE ONLY THING THAT CHANGED FROM THE REVERTED ATTEMPT IS THE CONFINEMENT.** The first attempt put the aerosol INSIDE `ofAtmoScatter` and relied on a 400 m scale height to keep it off the sky; that is confinement by HEIGHT, near-horizon sky rays lie inside the layer for tens of kilometres, and it failed its own control (sky saturation 0.494 to 0.410, sky red 81.9 to 97.0). **The seam that works already existed and nobody had named it: every escaping ray in this codebase passes `tMax = 1.0e9` and every terminating ray passes a real metre distance.** So `ofAtmoAerial` is a SEPARATE ENTRY POINT called from exactly one site, `TerrainShader`'s aerial-perspective line, which is the only call with a finite distance to geometry. The sky quad and the terrain's own upward sky-ambient ray both pass 1.0e9 into the other function and cannot reach it. "The sky did not move" stops being a tuning result and becomes a property of the call graph, **and a `#define` keyed on "is this the terrain material" would have got it wrong, because the sky-ambient ray IS a terrain fragment issuing an escaping ray.** Two further things had to be right. The optical depth is ANALYTIC (`L * H / (h1 - h0) * (exp(-h0/H) - exp(-h1/H))`, the closed form for a linear height profile) rather than marched, which is what makes it safe from orbit: a viewer 100 km up collects about H worth of dense air however long the ray is, where a midpoint or Simpson rule weights its samples by the FULL path length and would produce an enormous optical depth for a scaled planet. And the layer sits on the TERRAIN, heights measured from `min(h0, h1)`, not on the datum: measured from the datum the same term is 2x weaker on an 860 m hillside than at sea level and vanishes on a mountain, so one pair of constants would have to be retuned per site. Shipped at sigma 4.5e-4 per metre (Koschmieder 8.7 km), H 400 m, grey tint (0.38, 0.39, 0.43), g 0.35 with a 0.55 isotropic multiple-scattering floor. **The tint is grey because of the first attempt's finding, which is the useful one: a blue-biased coefficient does not haze, it DARKENS** (far-band red 70.2 to 57.0 while saturation moved 0.004), because it extinguishes red hard and refills with saturated blue. The g and floor pair was set to compress the phase function's dynamic range: g 0.55 spans 45:1 between the solar and anti-solar directions, which would make the distance alternately glow and darken as the player turns; g 0.35 with a 0.55 floor spans 2.8:1 and the haze is brighter than the ground it veils in every direction, which is what haze means. **(4) A DEFECT IN MY OWN INSTRUMENT, and it is the reason the first tuning read as doing nothing.** `probes/groundart.js`'s "far band" is frame rows 0.42 to 0.52, and at the pinned Hills camera the horizon sits at about 0.28, so that band is ground **30 to 80 m away**: near enough that no atmosphere on any planet would change it. The term was measured against the wrong range and read 0.3% of pixels moved. A `horizon` band at 0.29 to 0.38 was ADDED rather than the old one moved, so the RN-15 numbers stay comparable. **RESULT AT THE LOCKED RN-15 CAMERA (frozen builds `RN30-before` / `RN30-after` per BT-27, `vite preview`, 1280x720, sandbox, walk, seed 0xbf00d01, lat 12 / lon 150 / yaw 300 / pitch -10, sunT 0.30, RTX 4060 Ti, three repetitions each, interleaved BEFORE/AFTER): horizon saturation drop 0.0254/0.0322/0.0258 to 0.2148/0.2141/0.1994, i.e. mean 0.0278 to 0.2094, a 7.5x; horizon blue shift -0.0551/-0.0475/-0.0548 to +0.1199/+0.1191/+0.1019, i.e. THE SIGN FLIPS (distant ground was redder than ground underfoot and is now bluer); horizon band mean red 118.57 to 132.48 and mean blue 66.22 to 95.13; RN-15's own near-against-far saturation drop -0.185 to -0.139, still negative and correctly so, because that band is 30 to 80 m. Screen coverage 0.5580/0.5582/0.5346 to 0.5449/0.5429/0.5489. Draw calls 67 to 69 of a 150 budget, triangles 1,087,115 to 1,087,719 of a 2.7 M alert, programs 36 to 38, geometries 50 to 50, VRAM 92.8 to 93.7 MB. Props placed 45,854, instances 48,511, `deliveredFraction` 1.0018, pool refusals 0, `cellsCapped` 0, `chunksCapped` 0, all unchanged on both sides. > **RN-15 (2026-07-27): THE GROUND. 3.7x THE FOLIAGE FOR 40% FEWER TRIANGLES AND A THIRD OFF THE FRAME, AND THE THING THAT PAID FOR IT WAS NOT A NEW ASSET, IT WAS TWO STALE RENDER-POLICY DECISIONS.** Reid: "the terrain, trees rocks, ground, etc look like shit still. Im talking satisfactory (the game) level graphics", while being explicitly HAPPY with the rocket and the pad, which is what said the gap was WORLD art and not the renderer. **THE BUDGET WAS FOUND BEFORE ANY OF IT WAS SPENT, and that is the whole shape of this pass.** At a fixed Hills camera (lat 12, lon 150, yaw 300, pitch -10, 1280x720, sandbox, one binary) the isolation flags said: **`?props=0` removes 1,383,872 of the frame's 1,804,969 triangles and 15.0 ms of its 18.0 ms p50; `?shadows=0` removes 1,203,460 triangles and 14.5 ms; `?detail=0` removes 1,003,112 triangles and 12.3 ms for 9,738 understorey cards.** That last is about 103 triangles for a card whose LOD0 is 18 to 42, because **every card was being drawn FOUR times**, once in the near pass and once in each of three shadow cascades.
