## 2.8 THE LOOK AUDIT (RN-1710 to RN-1726, 2026-08-15, `lane/look-audit`). WHAT STILL READS UNFINISHED, RANKED

All seven canonical shots re-captured at current `main` on real Windows D3D11
(ANGLE, RTX 4060 Ti), 1600x900, HUD-free through `of.screenshot()`, `post: true`
asserted by the probe on every frame, in `docs/screenshots/RN1710_audit_*.png`.
This is the queue for the next art waves. It is ranked by **how much a player's
impression moves per unit of work**, which is not the same order as either
severity or area.

**Nothing on this list was both cheap and high impact, and this lane therefore
landed no art change.** The two candidates that looked cheap were measured and
each failed: see R3 and R5 below and the decision rows for RN-1715 and RN-1717.

### QUEUE ORDER, CORRECTED (`lane/audit-corrections`, RN-1727, 2026-08-15)
The list below is still filed as R1 through R7 -- those labels are cited
elsewhere (RN-1730..1814's own allocation rows, `ART-CAMPAIGN-2026-08-13.md`'s
summary table) and are kept stable on purpose -- but **the PRESENTATION order
this audit originally shipped contradicted the metric its own header names.**
The header says the queue is ranked by impression-per-unit-work, explicitly
not by severity or area, and then filed R1 (ground material) first while R1's
own entry concedes it is "ranked first on area alone" and is "the last item
here that could ever be cheap" -- the opposite of what the stated metric would
put first. Found and re-derived by this correction's own fresh-context
verifier, independently of the audit that produced the list.

Re-ordered by the audit's own stated metric, reading each entry's own cost
tier against its own frame share and fix-cost text:
**R3 (MEDIUM, highest impression-per-work of anything that is a bounded
wave), R6 (SMALL-MEDIUM, tiny area but the eye lands there first), R2
(MEDIUM-LARGE, a real budget saving attached), R5 (SMALL-MEDIUM, a harness fix
that unblocks judging the campaign's own climax destination), R4 (MEDIUM,
blocked on a scope ruling rather than on cost), R7 (SMALL but frozen by
Early Decision 1, so it buys nothing until that decision changes), R1 (LARGE,
and the one item that could never be cheap).** This is a re-ordering of how
the seven are PRESENTED, not a renumbering of them, so every existing
cross-reference to "R1" through "R7" by label is unaffected.

**R1 is not dropped, and it is already being worked.** It is last by the
metric this queue names, but Reid's standing directive is that the game
should look close to done, and R1 is the largest single element in five of
the seven canonical shots (§2.1's own frame-share reading, below) -- so area
matters on its own terms even where the work is large, and RN-1730 to
RN-1759 is already allocated to it. Last-by-metric and being-worked are not a
contradiction once both are stated; leaving R1 unstated here is what would
have been the actual error.

### The rectangles, committed (`lane/audit-corrections`, RN-1727)
Every rectangle this section cites beyond the seven shots' own canonical
`box` -- the two untouched-terrain patches on `voxelface`, the peep port and
sight strip on `smelterhero`, the two sky bands on `basedusk` -- is now a
named entry in `artframe.js`'s `SHOTS.<shot>.extra` map, so the next reader of
this section reads them rather than grid-searching the PNGs the way this
correction's own verifier had to. See each shot's own manifest comment for
the exact rectangle and the verification it was checked against.

### The instrument, validated before it was believed
Rectangles that `artframe.js` was not told about at capture time were read off
the committed PNGs with a decoder carrying `statOn`'s arithmetic verbatim
(same luma weights, same `sat`, same percentiles, same `loFrac` at 0.10 and
`hiFrac` at 0.80). It was checked against the probe's own published figures
first and agreed **bit-identically on four rectangles across two shots**
(`forestfloor` box 28.22 / iqr 19.77 / loFrac 0.418; `smelterhero` box 47.42,
`sunface` 71.90, `band` 58.77). Readings below are only used because of that.

### R1. THE GROUND AT WALKING DISTANCE HAS A THIRD OF THE SURFACE VARIATION OF THE MACHINE STANDING ON IT
- **Measurement.** On `voxelface`, eye about 1.5 m off the ground, two
  rectangles of untouched terrain read `iqr` **22.13** and **16.06** (p05 65.55
  and 80.75, `hiFrac` 0) — a smooth blur with no micro-detail. The dug cut face
  in the same frame reads `iqr` 36.78. In the same lighting family the smelter's
  clean plate (`sunface`) reads `iqr` **53.66** and its refractory column
  (`hearthL`) **63.40**.
- **Frame share.** The largest single element in five of the seven shots:
  effectively 100 per cent of `voxelface`, and roughly 45 to 60 per cent of
  `machine` and `forestfloor` below the horizon.
- **Fix and cost.** Per-biome tangent-space normal plus a detail albedo on the
  terrain shader. **LARGE, and already refused once with a reason**: A3 declined
  tangent-frame terrain this campaign (needs world-gen RN-45 per-chunk noise
  phase; float32 ULP is 0.0625 m at the Forge radius). This is a world-gen plus
  rendering wave, not an art wave.
- **CORRECTED, RN-1727: this is the biggest AREA in the frame, not the top of
  the queue's own stated metric.** It is the last item here that could ever be
  cheap, so by impression-per-unit-work (the metric this section's own header
  names) it is ranked LAST, seventh of seven -- see "QUEUE ORDER, CORRECTED"
  above. It is worked anyway, ahead of cheaper items, under RN-1730 to
  RN-1759, because Reid's directive is that the game should look close to
  done and area matters to him even where the work is large.

### R2. THE UNDERSTOREY IS FLAT CARDS, AND THE WHOLE NEAR-SHADOW BUDGET IS SPENT DRAWING THEM AT LOD0
- **Measurement.** `check_shadow_lod.py` put 46 subtrees at the **full 4.0x**
  multiplier at audit time, every cascade still on tier 0. **CORRECTED by
  audit-corrections, RN-1727: one of the 46 was the launch pad, and RN-1690 to
  RN-1696's own form pass (merged after this audit) has since moved the pad to
  2.0x, so the count going forward is 45.** The list is almost entirely
  foliage: all five `detail_cards` tiers, every `bush_scrub` tier, every
  `props_*` grass tuft, `tree_broadleaf` and `tree_conifer` Full/Half/Low.
  `tree_conifer` LOD1 deviates **1250.89 mm** from LOD0 and `tree_broadleaf`
  LOD1 **480.31 mm**, against cascade 1's 56.25 mm texel, so no cascade may draw
  a cruder tier. Only the two `_Stump` tiers (60.50 and 77.87 mm) earn cascade 2.
- **Frame share.** 30 to 45 per cent of the lower half of `forestfloor`,
  `ruin`, `basedusk` and `machine`.
- A5 already took the cards 256 -> 1024 px, so **resolution is not the remaining
  defect; geometry is.** The cards are 2 to 3 triangle spikes with hard alpha
  edges and no thickness, and they read as paper stuck in mud.
- **Fix and cost.** Cross-quad or three-plane cards with a bent normal, plus a
  shadow-safe LOD1 so the cascades stop paying 4.0x. MEDIUM-LARGE: an asset wave
  with a budget consequence attached, and the budget consequence is a saving.

### R3. MASONRY TILES AT 0.6 m AND THE RUIN IS 35.2 m WIDE, SO THE STRUCTURE HIGH-WATER MARK READS AS WALLPAPER
- **Measurement.** `surfaces.json` gives the `stone` family `tile_m` **0.6**;
  `ruin` is 35.2 x 11.4 x 35.2 m, so the cella wall carries about **59 repeats
  across and 19 up**. At the shot's own 34 m standoff the motif is ~15 px in a
  1600 px frame and forms a plainly visible regular lattice.
- **Frame share.** The ruin fills about a quarter of its own frame, and `stone`
  also carries `foundation` (4 m), `launch_pad` (24 m) and every boulder and
  prop rock, so it is on screen in most frames.
- **THE FREE KNOB WAS TESTED AND IS NOT THE FIX, AND THAT IS THE useful half of
  this entry.** `?tile=stone:1.8` (RN-953's own sweep, one multiply, no
  regeneration) visibly converts the wall from knurled wallpaper to stone, and
  the negative controls are perfect: on `smelterhero`, `box` 47.42, `sunface`
  71.90, `firebox` 29.81, `band` 58.77 and `plate` 41.00 are **bit-identical to
  the digit**, only the two stone rectangles move (`hearthL` iqr 63.40 -> 59.76,
  `hearthR` 21.74 -> 24.88), and `voxelface` is bit-identical too, which
  separately proves the dug face is **not** this family. But the family's
  consumers span **0.18 m (`items_atlas`) to 35.2 m (`ruin`), a factor of 195**,
  and at 1.8 a 1.4 m boulder carries **0.78 repeats** — under one, which is
  exactly the failure RN-953 named for `suitplate`. 1.2 was measured as the
  compromise and the crop shows the lattice still plainly there.
- **Fix and cost.** Split a `masonry` family (`tile_m` about 2.0) in
  `texgen.py` and point the ruin's, launch pad's and foundation's `Rock` roles
  at it. MEDIUM, and cheaper than it looks: `FAMILY_TILE_M` has exactly three
  uses in `texgen.py` (a print, the manifest's `tile_m`, and `texels_per_m`) and
  feeds no pixel generation, so a tile-size change alone moves **no texture
  bytes** and the byte-identical determinism gate is not at risk.
- Highest impression-per-unit-work of anything here that is a bounded wave.
- **CLOSED, in two passes (RN-1780 then RN-1835).** RN-1780 took the world
  scale (0.6 m -> 1.8 m, 59 repeats -> 19.6) and its verifier found that the
  wall still read as patterned cut cliff, because the field was still
  `stone`'s isotropic fracture. RN-1835 replaced the field with coursed
  ashlar: level courses, staggered head joints, a chamfered mortar bed at
  every boundary, per-block tone and wear, and rain wash running down from
  each bed. `cella` iqr **23.15 -> 29.20** and shaded `cellaDark`
  **4.93 -> 6.86** on real D3D11, with `sky` and `hill` bit-identical. See
  RN-1835 and RN-1836; the launch pad's share of the trade is stated in the
  latter rather than left for the pad lane to discover.
- **REOPENED AND CLOSED A THIRD TIME (RN-1970), on a finding neither earlier
  pass could see.** RN-1835's verifier measured the family as the MOST
  repetitive of the three architectural ones on the column-averaged
  autocorrelation of the rendered wall, while it measured the LEAST
  low-frequency height contrast: the residual repeat was entirely in the
  per-block ALBEDO tone, where ten independent draws averaged four at a time
  down a column gave the tile a light half and a dark half. The blocks are now
  blended across the face by an exhaustive assignment search, with a
  per-course tone and two within-block bedding terms that are column-neutral
  by construction. Column-averaged luma std **7.13 -> 3.35 counts** and its
  correlation at half a tile **-0.68 -> -0.05** on the shipped map, per-block
  contrast held at 0.247. See RN-1970 to RN-1979.

### R4. THE FIRST-PERSON VIEW MODEL IS IN EVERY GROUND FRAME AND IS THE LOWEST-FIDELITY THING IN IT
- **Measurement.** Present in five of five ground frames at the same place; its
  bounding strip is roughly x 0.26 to 0.82, y 0.86 to 1.00, i.e. about **7.8
  per cent of the frame as an upper bound** (a bounding rectangle, so the
  covered area is less and this is stated as an estimate, not a measurement).
  The bare `OF_Skin` forearm reads as a flat untextured tube in all five.
- **Honest caveat, and it is a scope question rather than a defect.** A7 put the
  player model OUT of the campaign and into the feel workstream, so this is not
  a failure against the campaign's own plan. It is here because it is the one
  asset the player never stops looking at, and because it was rebuilt once
  already (2026-07-27) on exactly that argument from Reid.
- **Fix and cost.** MEDIUM: a Blender rebuild of `player_fp_arms.glb` plus a
  skin and glove map. Needs Reid's ruling on the scope boundary first.

#### R4 WORKED, RN-1875 to RN-1882, 2026-08-16, `lane/view-model`. TWO OF THE THREE CLAIMS ABOVE ARE WRONG, AND THE THING THAT READS UNFINISHED IS THE TOOL
Dispatched anyway against A7, on Reid's standing directive: an unfinished thing
in every frame contradicts "the game should look close to done" more than
anything else on the queue.

- **THE FRAME SHARE IS 3.54 TO 4.51 PER CENT, MEASURED, NOT 7.8.** The estimate
  above is a bounding rectangle around two hands and a diagonal haft, and it is
  roughly 2x the truth. It is now a per-pixel difference: the same shot captured
  twice with `{"hideVm": true}` on the second, differenced at a threshold of 8
  counts. `forestfloor` 50,980 px = **3.54 per cent**, `machine` 63,610 =
  **4.42**, `ruin` 64,939 = **4.51**, `voxelface` 53,340 = **3.70**. The
  instrument's own control: on `voxelface` the mask has **zero** pixels above
  y = 0.75, and on `forestfloor` 156 of 50,980 (0.3 per cent). **Verifier
  re-measurement, independent capture, masks 99.85 and 99.97 per cent clean:
  `forestfloor` 3.81 per cent and `voxelface` 4.63 per cent**, both a bit above
  this lane's own 3.54 and 3.70; the gap is real pose variation between
  captures rather than an instrument fault, and the audit's published 7.8 per
  cent is still roughly 2x either number.
- **THERE IS NO BARE `OF_Skin` FOREARM IN ANY OF THE FIVE FRAMES.** `OF_Skin`
  on `player_fp_arms.glb` is a 604 x 92 x 135 mm pair of wrist bands between the
  cuff and the glove (RN-857), and at the shipped carry every one of them is
  below the frame edge. **What is in the frame, reading as a flat untextured
  tube, is the TOOL HAFT**, which is a different asset (`tool_common.py`) with a
  different owner. An audit that names the wrong object routes the next lane to
  the wrong file.
- **AND THE HAFT'S COLOUR IS NOT THE DEFECT EITHER; THE LIGHT IS.** `forestfloor`,
  real D3D11: the haft's lit face reads **luma 133.69 / warm 78.22 / sat 0.470**
  against a frame at 29.90 / 11.45 / 0.456, and its shaded side reads **iqr
  6.28** against the frame's 27.84. But its rendered chroma-to-luma ratio is
  `Bark`'s **own authored ratio to three decimals (0.585 against 0.585)**, so
  that peach is one palette row lit correctly by a light that is wrong.
- **THE LIGHT, AND THIS IS THE REAL R4.** Render pass 4 has no shadow map
  (`Boot.ts`: `addLighting(scenes.viewModel, sunDir, 3, false)`, `castShadow`
  never set, no `ShadowRig`), so the view model never loses the sun when the
  world does. Model luma against its own frame's luma, four canonical shots,
  each an isolated mask: **`voxelface` 0.55, `ruin` 1.23, `forestfloor` 2.76,
  `machine` 3.36.** A **6.1x spread in a quantity that should be ~1 in every
  frame, and it changes sign**: 2.8x too bright standing in canopy shade, 1.8x
  too DARK standing in a sunlit pit. **Verifier re-measurement on `voxelface`
  and `forestfloor` reproduced the sign change with the world side matching
  almost exactly: 0.56 and 2.53** against this lane's 0.55 and 2.76, which
  moves the spread to 6.0x and the canopy-shade figure to 2.5x too bright; the
  sunlit-pit figure stays 1.8x too dark. In the same `machine` frame the smelter, a
  stock `MeshStandardMaterial` 5.19 m away in the near pass, reads box luma
  19.58 / warm -4.17 while the same class of material at 0.62 m in pass 4 reads
  105.91 / +37.83.
- **SCOPE RULING TAKEN HERE AND STATED UP FRONT: no constant can fix a term
  whose error changes sign, so the fill was NOT retuned.** Dimming
  `VM_HEMI.intensity` would improve `forestfloor` and `machine` and break `ruin`
  and `voxelface`, and `ruin`'s 1.23 is the positive control that proves the
  absolute level is already right where the world is open. **A shadow term for
  render pass 4 is renderer work and is owed** (§2.9). The chroma halving was
  also built, rendered and REVERTED: it moved the whole model's `warm` 29.02 ->
  14.62 against a frame at 11.45, and made the shaft read as bone rather than as
  wood, because taking the hue out of an object still 4.5x too bright leaves a
  pale neutral cylinder. `Haft` therefore ships `Bark`'s colour to the digit.
- **WHAT LANDED, all static, none of it animation.** `timber`, a new texture
  family that is `bark`'s recipe at a tile chosen from the CONSUMER's distance:
  the haft carries **0.080 repeats** of bark across its 48 mm section (measured
  off the shipped UVs, against R3's 0.78 on a boulder) so repeats are the wrong
  instrument for a cylinder this thin, and the right one is the first-person
  texel floor `texgen.FAMILY_SIZE` had already set for `suitfab` (1024) and
  `suitplate` (960) and then left the tool held in that same hand outside at
  **640**. `timber` is 384 px / 0.35 m = **1097 texels/m**, asserted bound in
  the running client at `repeat` 2.8571 by `probes/vmsurface.js`. The haft is 12
  flat-shaded sides on four rings instead of one 8-sided frustum (a facet at
  15 px instead of 22), with a cord **grip wrap** on the 20 cm the fist actually
  closes on, and the head lashing is off `Accent` (FF8A1E, the most saturated
  row in the palette, which RN-645 already removed from this exact frame once)
  onto `Rawhide` -> `suitfab`.
- **Owed to the feel workstream, named with its measurement.** The fingers do
  not close on the haft: the wrap gives them something to be closing on and the
  bind pose still rests the hand on top of the shaft. That is a bind-pose and
  clip change across all twelve `FP_*` clips and it is not an art-pass item.
- **Frames.** `docs/screenshots/RN1875_{before,after}_{forestfloor,machine,voxelface}.png`
  plus the `RN1875_novm_*` and `RN1875_after_novm_*` controls the masks are

  bone shaft) and `RN1875_reject_undercutbutt_forestfloor.png` (the

### R5. THE STATION SHOT IS NOT REPRODUCIBLE, SO THE STORYLINE'S CLIMAX DESTINATION HAS NO JUDGEABLE FRAME
- **Measurement.** Six captures of the identical command. Box luma **21.78,
  3.73, 5.69** at `timeOfDay` 0.35 and **8.76, 10.48** at the shipped 0.60: a
  **5.8x spread at a nominally identical pin**. `elevDot` agrees to three digits
  every time (0.821, 0.822, 0.825 at 0.35) while the subject swings from lit to
  black, which is the signature — the instrument pinning the sun works perfectly
  and is pinned to the wrong body. `pose.lonDeg` differs every run: 149.458,
  149.417, 149.329, 149.214, 148.874, 148.717.
- **Cause, as far as this lane took it.** `setTime` moves the sun and does not
  move the station, and `__ofPost.state().sun` is essentially **constant across
  every phase and every shot** in this lane's twenty-odd reports (its y
  component is exactly 0.3872324843550918 in all of them), which is consistent
  with a world-fixed sun and a rotating body. Under that, a phase pin cannot
  change the light on an orbiting subject at all. This extends §2.6's existing
  trap note ("`__ofPost.state().sun` freezes below the horizon") rather than
  contradicting it.
- **Found on the way, and it is a real doc/code contradiction:** `timeOfDay:
  0.60` ships while the manifest comment three lines above it says the shot
  takes phase 0.35. `git log -S` finds `timeOfDay: 0.60` in A0's own commit
  (3afaea1) and `timeOfDay: 0.35` in **no commit at all**.
- **Frame share.** The whole frame, on the destination the pre-alpha chain ends
  at.
- **Fix and cost.** SMALL-MEDIUM, and it is a harness item rather than an art
  item: the shot needs a deterministic pin on the station's **orbital
  position**, which is a physics or core handle the probe does not currently
  have, or it needs re-siting. Ranked fifth for that reason: it buys a
  judgeable frame, not a better-looking game.

### R6. THE ONLY UNTEXTURED SURFACES LEFT ON A HERO MACHINE ARE ITS TWO BRIGHTEST
- **Measurement.** On `smelterhero` the peep port reads p05 74.22 / p50 190.33 /
  p95 191.98 / **iqr 0.93**, and the sight strip **iqr 4.15**: constant patches.

  salience; this is the one item here whose rank comes from where the eye goes
  rather than from area.

  `texgen.py` and declare it in the manifest. The client slot already exists, so
  no renderer work.
- **CLOSED (RN-1780), WITH TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS ENTRY FROM RN-1838.**
  RN-1780 landed the `ember` family and found the real blocker (the status-chip
  shader branch ADDED a colour instead of reading the map, so the emissive
  multiply landed on zero): peep iqr **0.93 -> 20.66**, strip
  **4.15 -> 52.68**, both still current to the digit.

  **Correction 2: the remaining flat bright slabs on this machine are PAINT,

- **AND THE BRIGHTNESS QUESTION THIS ENTRY OPENED, ANSWERED WITH NUMBERS.**
  After both passes the frame's `iqr` ranking is `hearthL` 63.40, `band` 60.86,
  `sunface` 53.66, **`strip` 52.68**, `firebox` 40.54, `placard` 37.52,

### One process gap, because it cost this audit its baseline
A0's deliverable was "five canonical shots **+ written target grade each**". The
shots exist. The written target grade **does not exist anywhere**: `grep -rn
"target grade" docs/` returns exactly one hit, the plan sentence that
commissioned it. This audit therefore had no per-shot target to check against
and used the recorded readings instead. Whoever runs the next wave should write
the grades, or the same gap recurs at the next audit.

## 2.9 OWED, ROUTED OUT OF R4 (RN-1875, 2026-08-16, `lane/view-model`)

### THE VIEW-MODEL PASS HAS NO SHADOW TERM, AND IT IS THE LARGEST REMAINING LOOK DEFECT ON THE ONE ASSET IN EVERY FRAME
`Frame.ts` renders `scenes.viewModel` as pass 4 with its own camera and depth
range. Its lights are `Boot.ts`'s `addLighting(scenes.viewModel, sunDir, 3,
false)` -- a `DirectionalLight` at the same 3.0 the near sun carries, with
`castShadow` never set and no `ShadowRig` attached -- plus `Headlamp`'s
`vmHemi` and the shared `SkyIbl`. So the arms and the held tool are lit by a
sun **nothing can occlude**, in a frame whose world is shadowed by cascade 0.

**The measurement, four canonical shots, model pixels isolated by the RN-1876
`hideVm` control and differenced per pixel.** Model mean luma divided by the
same frame's own mean luma outside the model:

| shot | world luma | model luma | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| `voxelface` (sunlit pit, dot 0.88) | 98.55 | 54.20 | **0.55** |
| `ruin` (open approach, dot 0.35) | 81.74 | 100.42 | **1.23** |
| `forestfloor` (canopy shade, dot 0.70) | 29.92 | 82.71 | **2.76** |
| `machine` (shaded site, dot 0.45) | 31.48 | 105.91 | **3.36** |

**A 6.1x spread on a quantity that should be near 1 in every frame, and the
error changes sign.** That is what makes it a missing TERM and not a mistuned
constant, and it is why `lane/view-model` deliberately did not touch
`VM_HEMI`: `ruin`'s 1.23 is the control proving the absolute level is already
right wherever the sky is open, so any dimming that helped the two shaded
frames would break the two that are correct.

Second reading of the same fact, in one frame with no cross-shot comparison at
all: on `machine`, the smelter is a stock `MeshStandardMaterial` 5.19 m away in
the near pass and reads box luma **19.58 / warm -4.17**; the view model is the
same class of material 0.62 m away in pass 4 and reads **105.91 / +37.83**.

**What a fix would have to be.** Either cascade 0's shadow map read by a light
in the view-model scene, or the occlusion at the player's eye sampled once per
frame and applied as a scale on the pass-4 sun. The second is much the cheaper
and `Headlamp` already owns the shape of it (`sunScale`, driven from
`skyVis`), but `skyVis` is a ROCK-thickness oracle: it is 1.0 under a tree
canopy, which is exactly the `forestfloor` case. Rendering domain, not an art
wave.

**Also owed, feel workstream (A7):** the hand does not close on the haft.
RN-1880 put a cord grip wrap on the 20 cm the fist occupies, which gives the
fingers something to be closing on, and the bind pose still rests the hand on
top of the shaft rather than around it. Closing it is a bind-pose change plus a
`fp_grip` retune across all twelve `FP_*` clips.

## 2.9a THE VIEW-MODEL PASS NOW HAS A SHADOW TERM, AND IT DOES NOT FIX THE FOUR SHOTS (RN-1990 to RN-1997, 2026-08-16, `lane/vm-light`)

**WHAT LANDED.** `web/src/render/ViewModelLight.ts`. Pass 4's sun is named
`vmSun` in `Boot.ts`, and once per frame -- from inside `Frame.render`, after
the near pass and before the view-model pass, which is the only window in which
the term is this frame's -- it is handed **cascade 0's own shadow map**, bias,
normal bias, radius and map size, with cascade 0's shadow matrix
post-multiplied by a translation of the engine eye. That composition is the
whole trick: `CameraRig.setView` puts `vmCam` at the origin with the near
camera's orientation and `Avatar.placeViewModel` fixes the model there too, so
view-model space is engine space **translated** by the eye, with no rotation and
no scale, and a matrix that maps engine metres to shadow UV maps view-model
metres to the same UV after one translate. Nothing is re-rendered and no second
map is allocated: `vmSun.shadow.autoUpdate` and `needsUpdate` are both false,
which is the documented condition on which three's `WebGLShadowMap.render`
skips a light before it would draw into its map. `Avatar`'s FP rig now loads
with `receiveShadow: true` (it was false, and three's own line is
`receiveShadow ? getShadow(...) : 1.0`, so a wired light with unwired meshes is
a silent identity that reads exactly like the defect).

**COST**, WG-189's interleaved paired method, off phase
`__ofVmLight.receive(false)` -- which is the correct off phase and
`shadow(false)` is not: zeroing the shadow INTENSITY still calls `getShadow` and
still takes its five PCF taps, while clearing `receiveShadow` takes three's
other ternary arm and also skips this file's per-frame traverse. 5 interleaved
pairs of 4 s, real D3D11, RTX 4060 Ti: **median p50 8.30 -> 8.40 ms, delta
+0.10 ms against a 1.4 to 1.5 ms within-arm spread and 0.60 ms of off-arm drift,
not resolvable from zero.** Pass 4 itself 0.30 ms in both arms (spread 0.10).
Draw calls 74, programs 43, unmoved.

### AND NOW THE HONEST HALF: THE FOUR SHOTS DO NOT MOVE, AND THE REASON IS MEASURED RATHER THAN GUESSED

| shot | ratio before | ratio after | model/behind before | after | caster over the player? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `voxelface` | 0.577 | 0.569 | 0.676 | 0.668 | **no** |
| `ruin` | 1.000 | 1.030 | 3.409 | 3.469 | **no** |
| `forestfloor` | 2.320 | 2.323 | 2.696 | 2.647 | **no** |
| `machine` | 2.931 | 2.933 | 2.889 | 2.955 | **no** |
| `basedusk` | 0.950 | 1.005 | 3.348 | 3.598 | **no** |
| `station` | 4.134 | 3.977 | 1.812 | 1.750 | rig off in orbit |

Both arms are one variable apart **inside one page load**
(`__ofVmLight.shadow`), so this is not two scene builds compared. Every movement
above is inside the mask's own noise: the model's pixels are found by
differencing against a view-model-suppressed control, and foliage moving between
the two grabs swings the mask by 10 to 15 per cent, which is worth several
counts. `station` also demonstrates the stale-map guard: in orbit `ShadowRig`
clears `castShadow` on every cascade, and the term correctly reports shadow
intensity 0 in both arms rather than shadowing the arms with the last daylight
frame's trees.

**`casterHere` IS A MEASUREMENT, and it is the finding: the term is correct
and inert on all six canonical shots because none of them stands in a cast
shadow, and cascade 0 itself only ever receives props, never terrain.** This
used to be told in full here; it is now `RN-1993` in section 3, one source of
truth for the shot-set gap rather than two, and it is not this pass's to
close (see `RN-1993`'s own status).

**WHERE IT DOES BITE**, `probes/vmshade.js`, RN-352 forest site, sun dot 0.70,
81 stations scanned by the map and 19 measured with a matched on/off pair at
each: at the stations whose own texel holds a caster nearer the light,
**the model drops 9.87 counts, 19.9 per cent (n = 6)**, and the
model-over-world ratio moves **1.90 -> 1.51**; at the stations whose texel is
clear the same toggle moves it **4.82 counts (n = 13, and one degenerate
near-black station at world luma 4.4 carries 38 of that: the other twelve mean
about 2.0)** and the ratio moves **2.69 -> 1.97**. The clear-station residual is
owed and not a defect: the model spans 0.3 to 0.7 m and its pixels sample a
spread of texels around the eye's, so a leaf over the tip of the haft is a real
occlusion of a real pixel.

### TWO NEGATIVES WORTH MORE THAN THE POSITIVE

**1. THE AMBIENT IS NOT THE TERM, AND NOW THERE IS A NUMBER.** This lane built
the obvious mechanism fix -- derive `VM_HEMI`'s open-sky endpoint from the same
`stockFloor` call the near hemisphere reads, two lines away in `Headlamp.ts`, so
the two cannot drift -- and then sized the term before shipping it and reverted
it. On `forestfloor`, model luma 72.43: `__ofVmLight.ambient(0)` reads
**68.95**, so the whole view-model hemisphere is **3.5 of 72 counts, 4.8 per
cent**; `sun(0)` reads **22.32**, so the direct sun is **50.1 counts, 69 per
cent**; the remaining 17.8 is the shared sky IBL. A term worth 4.8 per cent
cannot move a ratio out by a factor of three. Worse, `stockFloor` returns
intensity 1.0 and carries its level in the COLOUR, so binding the INTENSITY to
it is arithmetically a multiply by one and the change would have read as a
mechanism and shipped as a retune. Recorded beside the constant in
`Headlamp.ts`. Taking the world's COLOUR as well is a real change and a
different one; it costs the arms their warm underground fill and it is worth
3.5 counts.

**2. RN-1875's "the ratio should be about 1" IS THE WRONG BAR, and the
four-shot spread is mostly the DENOMINATOR.** Across the four shots the model's
own luma spans 55.3 to 99.2 (**1.79x**) while the world it is held against
spans 24.1 to 82.8 (**3.43x**). A held tool with a fixed albedo in front of a
world whose albedo and incidence swing 3.4x cannot sit at 1 in all four frames,
and the sign change follows the world, not the model. The remaining defect on
those frames is therefore NOT a missing shadow map; it is that the model's
illumination barely responds to the shot at all, which is a question about the
pass-4 sun's incidence against a camera-locked rig and about the shared IBL, not
about occlusion. That is the next lane's item and it is now stated as a
measurement rather than as a ratio.

### THE INSTRUMENTS, WHICH ARE THE REUSABLE PART
* `artframe.js` `{"vmRatio": true}` and `{"vmArms": [...]}`: the model's own
  pixels by per-pixel difference against a `hideVm` control, three denominators
  published together (whole frame, frame-minus-model, and **the world the model
  occludes**, read out of the control frame at exactly the masked pixels), and
  N arms of `__ofVmLight` state measured in one page load. `ambientAbs` sets an
  ABSOLUTE hemisphere intensity, because a constant multiplier written into an
  invocation would measure a different ambient on every shot and call it one
  control.
* `probes/vmlight.js`: the wiring gate. Wired, receivers non-zero, the eye's
  shadow coordinate inside `getShadow`'s own frustum test, **the compiled
  programs actually carry a `directionalShadowMap` sampler** (read back through
  `onBeforeCompile`, because `castShadow` on the CPU and `USE_SHADOWMAP` in the
  shader are joined only by an ordering), and the map has casters in it.
* `probes/vmshade.js`: the behavioural gate, and its own two scars are the
  lesson. `of.look` takes a DELTA and `of.teleport` re-derives the tangent
  frame, so one correction lands short: the first walk **alternated between two
  yaws on odd and even stations**, which moved the cascade centre 7 m and made
  the eye's texel flip between unrelated cells every step, and the two
  populations it reported were the two yaws, not sun and shade. And measuring
  the model twice, each against its own fresh control, puts the wind clock into
  both halves of the subtraction; one control and one mask per station turned a
  12-count scatter on the negative-control stations into about 1.3.
* `probes/vmcost.js`: WG-189's interleave with `receive` as the off phase.

**A NULL THAT COST THREE MEASUREMENT PASSES, named so it costs none next time.**
With the term wired, receivers at 13 and shadow intensity at 1, all four shots
moved by less than the mask noise. "The arms are not in anybody's shadow here"
and "the lookup never lands" are the same number in a ratio table. Forcing the
shadow bias was tried first and **cannot work**: reversed depth puts the
comparison at `z >= stored`, and an empty texel stores 0, so no bias in `[0, 1]`
can shadow against it, and the forced-bias arm returns "lit" for exactly the
reason the real one does. Only reading the map itself separated them.

## 3. Key design decisions
| # | Decision | Rationale | Status | Date |
|---|----------|-----------|--------|------|
| RN-1835 | **`masonry` STOPS BEING `stone` AT A BIGGER TILE AND BECOMES COURSED ASHLAR. THE RUIN IS LAID STONE NOW, NOT CUT CLIFF** | RN-1780 split `masonry` off `stone` and moved its world scale 0.6 m -> 1.8 m, and its own verifier said what that did not fix: the same lozenge motif still repeated on a visible grid, with no courses and no joints, because a bigger tile cannot turn an ISOTROPIC FRACTURE FIELD into a wall. `_ashlar_height`/`_ashlar_masks`/`_ashlar_albedo` replace `_stone_*` on this family only (`stone` itself is byte-identical, boulders and scree are broken rock and stay broken rock). **The bond:** four courses per 1.8 m tile at hashed heights 0.37 to 0.52 m, two or three blocks per course at hashed lengths with a hashed phase, so a tile holds about ten blocks of eight sizes rather than a 4x2 grid; a 20 mm mortar bed and a 15 mm head joint, each recessed 0.34 relief units with a 26 mm chamfer either side, and the chamfer is what survives minification (at the shot's 34 m the ruin draws ~45 px/m, so a 20 mm groove is under one pixel and the 72 mm joint-plus-draft is three). **Two masks, not one, and conflating them was the first build's defect:** `joint` is the recess (the shape) and `mortar` is the bed alone (the material), and a colour keyed on the recess paints a 98 mm pale band where the wall has a 20 mm one. **The anti-repeat work is where the argument is,** because 19.6 tiles still cross the cella: non-modular courses and blocks, weathering at periods 7 and 11 that share no factor with the bond, per-block tone as a STEP function (an edge reads where a gradient does not), and rain wash running DOWN from each bed joint in per-column streaks, which is the one directional cue an isotropic field can never give. **Measured on real D3D11 through `artframe.js`'s newly committed `ruin.extra`:** `cella` iqr **23.15 -> 29.20** (p05 105.18 -> 103.61, p50 138.03 -> 143.66, p95 161.97 -> 168.87), shaded `cellaDark` iqr **4.93 -> 6.86**, and the two negative controls `sky` and `hill` **bit-identical in every published field on both arms**. | LANDED | 2026-08-16 |
| RN-1836 | **WHICH CONSUMER `masonry` IS OPTIMISED FOR, SAID BEFORE THE CODE RATHER THAN DISCOVERED AFTER IT, BECAUSE RN-953 AND RN-1780 BOTH FAILED THIS WAY** | `masonry` is worn by the ruin (35.2 m), the foundation (4 m) and the launch pad (24 m). **The ruin is the consumer this is authored for:** an 11.4 m cella carries ~25 courses at the mean 0.45 m course height, and 0.6 to 0.9 m blocks are real ashlar block lengths. **The foundation is an improvement and not a compromise:** ~9 courses of dressed block on a player-built stone plinth is what a built foundation is and fractured rock is what it is not. **The launch pad is a TRADE and it is not a fix, stated plainly:** the pad wants poured concrete and has never had it (RN-1815's own pad verifier records the skirt reading as "a repeating dark aggregate rock tile rather than poured concrete"), and under this change it reads as a jointed slab field at 0.45 x 0.6-0.9 m, i.e. heavy paving -- a DIFFERENT wrong thing of the same magnitude, not a regression into one. The shape is at least the right family (a poured deck IS cast in bays, and `build_launch_pad.py` already authors two deck control joints as geometry), and the pad's concrete is owned by the RN-1815 lane. **The alternative was priced and refused:** a separate `ashlar` family with `Ashlar`/`AshlarDark` roles pointed at the ruin alone costs +4.0 MiB of VRAM (512 px RGBA8 with mips, three maps), a `build_ruin.py` change, a Blender rebuild of `ruin.glb` and a four-table role move, to protect a pad surface that is already wrong and is being fixed elsewhere. `probes/pad.js` is green on real D3D11 after the change. | LANDED | 2026-08-16 |
| RN-1837 | **`texgen check` HAS BEEN RED ON `main` SINCE RN-1780 AND NOBODY WAS READING IT. THREE CHANNELS, AND THE TABLE THAT DECLARES THEM NOW ASSERTS ITS OWN VALUE** | `masonry.orm B`, `ember.orm G` and `ember.orm B` all ship CONSTANT and none was declared in `ALLOWED_CONSTANT`, so `python tools/blender/texgen.py check` exited 1 on unmodified `main`. All three constants are deliberate (metalness identity twice, and `ember`'s roughness pinned matte by RN-1780 so no specular can compete with the emissive for which one the eye reads as the hot spot) and none was written down. The declaration used to be a bare reason string with `lo == 255` hard-coded beside it, so an entry could never be wrong about its own value; it is now `(value, reason)` and the check asserts the shipped constant IS that value, which is a **tightening** -- a pinned constant that silently moves now fails instead of passing on a stale declaration. It also admits exactly one non-255 entry (`ember.orm G` at 242), with the argument written in the table header: 255 is identity for a MULTIPLIER, which is the right rule for metalness and not an argument about a channel a family pins as a deliberate absolute. **Zero shipped `ember` bytes changed**, so RN-1780's peep/strip figures stand to the digit. `texgen check` is now `TEXTURES PASS  189 check(s)`. | LANDED | 2026-08-16 |

| RN-1571 | **THE CAUSE IS THAT THREE r185 DOES NOT FLIP THE SHADOW BIAS FOR REVERSED DEPTH ON THE PCF PATH, AND THIS RIG'S BIAS WAS 4.8 WORLD METRES POINTING THE WRONG WAY** | Two independent defects in one literal, `light.shadow.bias = -0.0006`. **(1) THE SIGN.** In `shadowmap_pars_fragment.glsl` the VSM branch (line 161) and the BASIC branch (line 228) both guard with `#ifdef USE_REVERSED_DEPTH_BUFFER shadowCoord.z -= shadowBias; #else += #endif`, and **the `SHADOWMAP_TYPE_PCF` branch at line 122 has no such guard and adds unconditionally**. `Renderer.ts:194` selects `PCFShadowMap` on every tier that is not `shadowSoft`, and the project runs reversed depth wherever the capability exists, so the shipped configuration is exactly the one branch three does not correct. Under reversed depth a larger z is NEARER, so the conventional acne-reducing negative bias is an acne-CREATING one. **(2) THE MAGNITUDE.** `-0.0006` is the number every three.js example carries, sized for a shadow camera tens of metres deep. This one runs `near = 1` to `far = 2 * CASTER_BACKOFF_M` = 7999 m so the light clears planetary relief, and 0.0006 of 7999 m is **4.8 world metres** -- larger than the whole 3.6 m smelter, so every vertical face tested as though it sat behind its own back wall's entry in the map. **MEASURED as a curve, which is what says SIGN and not magnitude: bias -0.0006 box 19.36 / firebox 4.08; -0.0001 box 22.02; 0 box 39.56 / firebox 23.07; +0.0001 box 40.62; +0.0006 box 40.30.** Flat either side, a step across zero. **FIXED by deriving both halves:** `SHADOW_BIAS_M = 0.02` world metres, `shadowBiasSign(reversedDepth, soft)` returning +1 only for reversed-depth PCF, divided by the cascade's own depth range, giving `biasUnits` 2.50e-6. A world-space constant survives a change to the splits, to `CASTER_BACKOFF_M` or to the quality tier, none of which the raw depth-unit number did. `stats().shadow` now publishes `biasM`, `biasSign`, `biasUnits`, `reversedDepth`. **Negative control per standing rule 7, registered in `run.mjs` in the same commit: `?shadowbias=0` restores the raw literal, and it is VERIFIED rather than asserted** -- `?shadowbias=0&sundisc=0` reproduces the pre-lane build to the digit on all seven `smelterhero` rectangles (world 45.13, box 19.52 / warm -4.48 / iqr 19.58 / p95 41.9 / loFrac 0.733, firebox 4.12, plate 30.24, hearthL 21.55, hearthR 22.58). **No acne and no detached contact at 3x zoom on plate, ground and foliage.** | Accepted | 2026-08-13 |

Reported rather than quietly satisfied. **And the low-tier cost, measured because RN-1522's rule demanded it: at a 64 cube the disc is MISSED ENTIRELY** -- max 0.7374 (haze), `atSun` 0.2264, `brightTexels` 0, and a 2x disc boost moves the maximum by a ratio of exactly 1.0000, i.e. the raise never reaches the capture. `iblSize` is 64 on the low tier and 128 on medium, so **on those tiers the sun contributes no specular to the environment at all**; the diffuse cost is the 0.07 per cent above, i.e. nothing. What reaches the eye is (density at the shadow line) times (how much of that air the sight line crosses), and the second factor is 1/cos(emission), which is exactly what puts the glow where the terminator meets the limb. **No amount of retuning a brightness fixes a term with no shape**, and I spent two frames trying before naming it; `RN845_defect_twilight_slab.png` is faults (2) and (3) together, kept as the counter-example. Width and falloff are DERIVED (the ceiling, and 5600 m measured from `_of_atmo_density`); the amplitude is CALIBRATED against the lit disc and says so in the shader, because this material has no radiometric units to derive an amplitude from and giving the whole disc an exposure model is a larger change than this lane should make alone. | **Accepted, shipped, driven-verified** | 2026-08-03 |

The relief term is isolated by SUBTRACTING the amp-0 arm's power spectrum from each rung's, with both frames captured with no await between them so they are pixel-registered by construction. **THE RESULT.** Neither Cinder nor Beach has an interior minimum: both point at the sweep's edge, 64 texels, where dRms is down 70 and 73 per cent, which is the amplitude answer RN-148 already rejected. That is why the moon had only two states. Splitting `SkyOptions.atmosphere` (build the box) from `SkyOptions.scattering` (`uAtmosOn`) gives the third: box present, integral off, so `ofAtmoScatter` returns 0 above the horizon while the ground shell still paints sunlit regolith below it. **`iblGroundOn` deliberately dropped its `scattering` term**, and that omission is the load-bearing line. | RN-842 | **`skyView` was a flat-plane assumption, and a vacuum is where a flat-plane assumption becomes the image; the correction is MEASURED from the body's own height field at boot, never written down** | `0.5 + 0.5*dot(n, up)` is exact for a facet on an infinite tangent plane and wrong on any landscape. | RN-2 | Logarithmic **or cascaded** depth buffer; near camera only | Single-frame coverage of cm→planetary scales. Spike 1: measure reversed-Z float first; cascaded passes preferred over `SV_Depth` log because Nanite can't take a custom per-pixel depth write | **Accepted** (Spike 1) | 2026-06-14 |
| RN-5 | Terrain = **classic streamed meshes (RealtimeMesh), NOT Nanite** | World-gen already does LOD (Nanite's headline feature redundant); Nanite-on-terrain conflicts with the cascaded/`SV_Depth` depth path. Nanite's payoff is later **factory** meshes, not terrain | **Accepted (Spike 1); SUPERSEDED by PMC in practice** (2026-07-05, Admin D-009): RealtimeMesh was never adopted; every shipped mesh path (chunks, voxel near-field, factory visuals) is `UProceduralMeshComponent`, which carried M2.1 to M5.2. | RN-3 | Factory items: GPU-instanced near, texture/decal flow far, none when unobserved | Only way 3D belts survive at scale | **Accepted; render-wall fit CONFIRMED vs factory-sim §6 stream (RC-8, §5), and now NUMERICALLY VALIDATED HEADLESSLY: a render-cost model over the emitted §6 stream quantifies the O(items)→O(lines) collapse (100k entities → 72 draw calls, 180k item-evals vs 12.18M belt items)** | 2026-06-15 |

| RN-7 | **A layer that draws less than it was asked for must say so, and the way to know is to assert the RATIO of delivered to requested rather than a count** | The scatter's per-cell count was `Math.round(expected)`, which is exactly zero for every expected value under 0.5, and DW-19's finer terrain LOD walked it under that line without touching a line of scatter code. No count-based check could have caught it: the chunk-level `want` was right, the density constants were right, the pool was not exhausted, the props existed in the atlas and 159 of them were genuinely on screen. What was false was the RATIO. `deliveredFraction` is placed over requested, over the ground actually drawn on, so it is invariant to terrain, to density and to LOD depth, and it reads 0.0182 against the defect and 0.9971 against the fix. The same argument gave the two truncating caps counters instead of silence, and `chunksCapped` found a 16% shortfall within one run of being added. **The general form, which is RN-6's lesson pointed at a different layer: a stage in a pipeline should publish what it was ASKED for next to what it PRODUCED, because every other instrument in the chain reports the request** | **Accepted, shipped, driven-verified** (screen coverage 0.56% -> 28.87%, same seed, same camera, one binary) | 2026-07-27 |
| RN-15 | **A performance trade is only valid at the scale it was measured, and the failure mode is that nothing announces the scale changed** | `PropLibrary` turned per-instance frustum culling OFF with a recorded measurement (9,340 props, 8.2 ms of near-pass CPU with sorting against 11.1 ms without) and a correct conclusion: for 150-triangle props the walk costs more than the redraw. Raising the understorey to about 45,000 instances inverted it completely, because the scatter is a RING and roughly three quarters of it is behind the camera, so the saving is not a fifth of the triangles, it is three quarters of them. Measured in one binary with `?propcull=0` as the control: triangles 1,916,689 to 1,087,115, p50 22.8 to 11.3 ms, and screen coverage 0.5545 against 0.5563, which is the same picture. **This is the second time a DENSITY change has silently invalidated a constant nobody edited** (RN-7: DW-19's finer terrain LOD walked `Math.round(expected)` under 0.5 and deleted the ground cover). The general form: a comment that says "measured, this is faster" is a claim indexed by a workload, and the index belongs in the comment next to the number so the next lane can see whether it still holds | **Accepted, shipped, measured both ways** | 2026-07-27 |
| RN-16 | **A layer that PRODUCES instances must also REQUEST them, or it blinds the ratio that watches for the opposite failure** | The contact skirt places five understorey cards at the foot of every colliding prop. They are not a density draw, so the first version counted them in `propsPlaced` and not in `wantedProps`, and `probes/grass.js` read `deliveredFraction` 1.5146 against a check that requires 1.00 within 5%. Over-delivery looks harmless and is not: RN-7 built that ratio specifically because every other instrument in the chain reports the REQUEST, and a ratio that can legitimately read 1.5 can no longer be trusted to read 0.98 when the pool is quietly eating a quarter of the placements. The fix is to give the skirt an honest request, exactly `CONTACT_CARDS` per colliding prop placed, which restores 0.9997 and still catches truncation because cards refused by the per-chunk allocation are counted as asked for and not produced. **Worth keeping next to RN-7 rather than inside it: the ratio caught a defect in the code that was ADDED TO SATISFY the ratio's own design** | **Accepted, fixed, probe green** | 2026-07-27 |
| RN-17 | **A shared model gets a new term only if the term can be shown NOT to move the things it was not meant to move, and the check is a control band in the same capture** | Aerial perspective at playable range is a measured gap (near band against far band in ONE frame, so exposure, sun, tone curve and grade are equal by construction: saturation -0.149, the distant ground MORE saturated than the ground underfoot). A boundary-layer aerosol term is the physically right answer and was added to the shared atmosphere rather than as three's own `FogExp2`, correctly, because fog would have been free and would have been a SECOND authority on how distance looks, disagreeing with the terrain integral at every range and seaming exactly where a rock meets the ground behind it (DW-22). It still did not ship. Blue-biased it darkened instead of hazing; grey with a multiple-scattering floor hazed, and then the SKY control moved (saturation 0.494 to 0.410, mean red 81.9 to 97.0), because a 400 m scale height does not confine the term structurally the way the design claimed: near-horizon sky rays lie inside the layer. **The control is what made a clean revert possible instead of a plausible-looking regression in the one file the sky, the near terrain and the far scaled planet all read.** The negative result is the deliverable: the gap is quantified, the mechanism is understood, and the next attempt starts from a known-bad approach rather than from scratch | **Reverted; `Atmosphere.glsl.ts` byte-identical to main. Gap remains open** | 2026-07-27 |
| RN-30 | **Shadow contact is two terms that divide by RANGE, and neither of them is a shadow map** | RN-15 removed the understorey from the shadow pass for 12.3 ms of an 18.0 ms frame and removed every grass shadow with it. Putting it back in cascade 0 alone is not expressible in three r185: `WebGLShadowMap.renderObject` tests `object.layers.test( camera.layers )` against the VIEW camera, not the shadow camera, and `onBeforeShadow` fires after the `castShadow` gate. So the contact comes from (a) a base-contact gradient baked into the foliage geometry's existing per-vertex colour attribute, which costs zero draw calls, zero triangles and zero bytes and grounds the silhouette, and (b) a 0.45 m screen-space march toward the sun, which darkens the ground the card stands on. They divide from the cascades by RANGE the way the baked ORM map divides from SSAO by spatial frequency: a term bounded to half a metre of world distance physically cannot disagree with a cascade about a hill. Measured, one settled frame apart in one binary: near-band mean darkening 0.1012 with p99 0.6581 over 40.4% of pixels for (b), 0.0323 / 0.3705 / 17.9% for (a) | Accepted | 2026-07-27 |
| RN-31 | **A product capped by shrinking one of its factors has to be re-capped every time either factor moves; take the factor out of the product instead** | The understorey's height is card height x width jitter x height jitter x distance upscale. RN-15 found it too tall, retuned the height jitter 1.48 to 1.30, and it was still 1.34 m at the worst instance, because the retune left the product intact. RN-30 lowers the band AND demotes `DETAIL_FAR_GROW` to a horizontal-only upscale, so distance is no longer a factor in height at all: mean understorey height 0.4262 to 0.2811 m, tallest card 1.34 to 0.64 m, and neither number has to be re-derived when the other one is next tuned. The general form is the one this log keeps meeting from the other side (DW-33's "a constant that encodes an assumption is a scale assumption in disguise") | Accepted | 2026-07-27 |
| RN-32 | **Confine a shared model's new term BY PATH, not by height, and the confinement must be a property of the call graph rather than a tuning** | The first aerial-perspective attempt added a boundary-layer aerosol inside `ofAtmoScatter` and relied on a 400 m scale height to keep it off the sky. Near-horizon sky rays lie inside that layer for tens of kilometres, so the ground hazed correctly and the sky moved with it (saturation 0.494 to 0.410), and it was reverted whole. The seam that works already existed and had never been named: every ESCAPING ray in this codebase passes `tMax = 1.0e9` and every TERMINATING ray passes a real metre distance. `ofAtmoAerial` is therefore a separate entry point reachable only from the one call site that has a finite distance to geometry, so "the sky did not move" is structural and the probe measures exactly 0.0000 over 276,480 samples. Note what a plausible alternative would have got wrong: a `#define` on "is this the terrain material" fails, because the terrain's own sky-ambient ray is a terrain fragment issuing an escaping ray. DW-22 is unweakened: still one model, one shared uniform record, one GLSL string | Accepted | 2026-07-27 |
| RN-33 | **An optical depth over a finite path is analytic, never marched, because a quadrature rule weights its samples by the path length and a path can be 500 km long** | The aerosol column uses `L * H / (h1 - h0) * (exp(-h0/H) - exp(-h1/H))`, the closed form for a linear height profile, with the `dh -> 0` limit taken explicitly because a horizontal ray is both the commonest case and the one that zeroes the denominator. It self-limits by construction: a viewer 100 km up collects about H worth of dense air however long the ray is, so the same term that hazes 2 km of hillside costs the scaled far planet exactly sigma x H = 0.18 of optical depth. A midpoint or Simpson rule over the same segment multiplies its samples by the full 500 km and greys the planet out, and it would have done so only in the orbital frame, which is not the frame the term was being tuned in | Accepted | 2026-07-27 |
| RN-34 | **A band named "far" that is 30 m away is an instrument measuring the wrong question, and it fails by reporting that the thing under test does nothing** | `probes/groundart.js` compared a near band at frame rows 0.80 to 0.97 against a "far" band at 0.42 to 0.52. At the pinned camera the horizon is at about 0.28, so the far band is ground 30 to 80 m out, where no atmosphere on any planet changes anything. A correctly working aerosol term measured against it moved 0.3% of pixels and read as broken. A `horizon` band at 0.29 to 0.38 was ADDED and the old one left exactly where it was, so the RN-15 numbers stay comparable rather than being improved by moving the ruler: on the same three runs the horizon saturation drop goes 0.0278 to 0.2094 while the old band's stays negative, which is the right answer for both | Accepted | 2026-07-27 |
| RN-10 | **The post stack is NOT a fifth pass. It brackets the four and interposes at exactly one point: after the NEAR pass and before its `clearDepth()`** | ARCHITECTURE 3.1 composites by CLEAR ORDER, never by depth merge, so the depth attachment holds exactly one pass's depth at any instant. A composer that assumes one scene and one depth buffer (three's own `EffectComposer` among them) would read the VIEW MODEL's depth, the last pass to write, and compute ambient occlusion for the player's forearms against a world no longer in the buffer. The near 1:1 scene is also the CORRECT subject: a planet 600 km away in the far scaled pass has no contact shadow, and the arms are a separate depth range whose occluders are not in the same buffer. Consequence, stated because it is a choice and not an accident: AO never touches the sky, the far scaled planet or the view model, while bloom and the grade see all four passes, which is what makes the sun disc and the engine plume bloom. `EffectComposer` was also unusable without breaking the DW-10 seam, since it takes a concrete `WebGLRenderer` and `Renderer.ts` is the only file allowed to name one; the stack talks to a three-method `PostHost` instead | **Accepted, shipped, driven-verified** (probe asserts occlusion CONTRAST, not that the pass ran) | 2026-07-27 |
| RN-11 | **A post pass may not sample any attachment of the framebuffer it writes to, and the rule earns its own buffer** | The obvious three-pass AO folds the upsample into the multiply: read half-resolution AO plus full-resolution depth, multiply into scene colour. The depth texture is an ATTACHMENT of the scene framebuffer, so that pass is a feedback loop and WebGL says so 256 times a frame. The structural fix, and not a workaround: the depth-aware upsample resolves to its own full-resolution R8 buffer first, and the one pass that touches scene colour samples exactly one texture the scene framebuffer does not own. Cost of the rule is 1.4 MB and one draw call; the thing it buys is that the multiply is a one-tap shader with no depth uniforms at all, which is also why it cannot get the background test wrong. Generalises to any future pass that wants depth AND wants to write colour | **Accepted, shipped** (0 GL errors after; 256/frame before) | 2026-07-27 |
| RN-12 | **A ratio metric needs a floor on its denominator, and a colour grade needs the space its pivot was chosen in** | Two instrument bugs from one night, both of which PASSED. `darkening = 1 - with/without` divides by nothing on an already-black pixel and returns exactly 1.0, so the AO probe reported p99 and max darkening of 1.0000 and passed its own "the 99th percentile moves a lot" check on pixels ambient occlusion had never touched: standing rule 11 inside the instrument rather than inside the code. Percentiles are now taken over pixels above a luminance floor of 12/255 and the lit fraction is published beside them. Separately, a contrast of 1.06 about a pivot of 0.4135 was applied to the ACES output, where mid-grey is 0.18: every value below the pivot was pushed down, hardest at the dark end, and the sky's red channel went 37.9 to 7.9 of 255 while every whole-frame mean stayed unremarkable. The grade now runs after the sRGB encode, where mid-grey really is 0.5. **General form: a metric and a curve both have a domain, and neither announces when it is being evaluated outside it** | **Accepted, both fixed and re-measured** | 2026-07-27 |
| RN-13 | **A before/after pair must re-pin every quantity that a data-dependent wait can move, and the sun is one** | The first before/after pair from this lane showed a warm-to-cool shift across an entire hillside that looked exactly like a colour grade and was entirely SUN ANGLE. The build recipe places machines by trying camera pitches until a ghost is legal, so two runs of the same recipe consume different amounts of sim time, and the sun moves with sim time. Setting the time once at the top of a probe is not enough: it has to be set again after every data-dependent wait and immediately before the frame that is captured. The pair was not wrong by a little, it was wrong in a way that invented a result for the effect under test. Related and worth keeping next to it: I then read a green wash across the ground in the after image and was ALSO wrong, and only measuring the two captures region by region settled it (ground 1.5% darker, its green bias identical in the before). **WG-28 says structural validation cannot replace looking at the thing; this is the converse, and both are true** | **Accepted** (probe re-pins; screenshots retaken) | 2026-07-27 |
| RN-14 | **A baked occlusion map and a screen-space one divide by SPATIAL FREQUENCY, and the way to prove it is to shrink the radius, not to threshold a face** | The material lane's ORM map bakes occlusion INSIDE one surface (panel gaps, bolt recesses, centimetres); this stack computes occlusion BETWEEN separate pieces of geometry (a machine's foot on ground, metres). Multiplying two terms that describe the same thing double-darkens and reads as muddy. The separation is structural rather than tuned: `aoRadiusM` 0.9 m on a half-resolution buffer is physically incapable of resolving a panel gap. **The first attempt to check this was the wrong instrument and is the lesson.** It asserted that a machine face away from contact darkens less than 6%, measured 10.1%, and would have been "fixed" by moving the threshold: the band it sampled is the smelter's own RECESSED PANELS, which are decimetre-scale and are legitimately this term's business, and "how much does this band darken" is not a statement about spatial frequency at all. The check is now: re-run the entire measurement with the radius set to 5 cm, the scale a bolt recess lives at, and require it to produce nothing. If the signal does not exist at that scale, no tuning of the shipped radius can be competing with the baked map | **Accepted, shipped** | 2026-07-27 |
| RN-8 | **A face is lit by the sky it can SEE and by the ground beside it, not by a sky term evaluated along local up** | Task 109's black cut banks. `skyAmb` was traced along `up` for every fragment, so it was a constant, and a near-vertical face with `ndl` clamped to zero kept 2.5 to 5.9 per cent of flat ground's light and rendered black. Neither replacement term is tuned: `skyView = 0.5 + 0.5 * dot(n, up)` is the share of the dome the face sees, and the bounce term's radiance is literally the flat-ground branch the shader already computes at that point, using `vBiomeColor` which IS that ground's albedo there. Two properties follow and both are checked: a flat fragment has `skyView == 1` and is algebraically unchanged (measured 154.8 -> 155.4), and every term goes to zero together at night and under shadow. Isolated with a CIRCULAR pit so that bearing is the only free variable, which is what makes the 155-count azimuthal spread attributable to `dot(N, sunDir)` and nothing else | **Accepted, shipped, driven-verified** (cut face over sunlit floor 0.135 -> 0.313, tolerance 0.18 derived from clear-sky diffuse; headlamp lift 16.99 unchanged) | 2026-07-27 |
| RN-9 | **A batch key must carry every property the batch's MATERIAL expresses, and the moment a material gains a map, the surface family becomes one of those properties** | `NodeBatch` bucketed by `metalness > 0.5`, which was free while every role was a flat colour and stopped being free the instant the bucket got a normal map: Leaf, LeafDeep, LeafDry, LeafLight, Grass, Ice and Oil shared `matte` with Bark and Rock, and the texture pass had recorded a REASON for each of those seven being left bare ("sub-pixel blades at any real viewing distance", "a double-sided card whose normal map fights the flat-shaded silhouette"). A rock normal map on a foliage card is worse than no map. The key is now `(family, metalness)` and the recorded decision survives the batching. Two properties follow and both are asserted against the LIVE materials rather than the table: every `flat` material carries zero maps, and every mapped one carries all four with `aoMap.channel === 0` and `repeat === 1/tile_m`. The cost is exactly one extra batch, measured at +4 draw calls of a 150 budget, which is the main pass plus three shadow cascades and nothing else. **The general form: three copy-pasted `normalize()` functions and two independently-derived bucketing rules is how a shared decision drifts, so the role -> family decision lives in ONE module and is checked against the shipped manifest at runtime** | **Accepted, shipped, driven-verified** (normal map alone moves the ground 2.78 counts mean over 288k px against a sky control of exactly 0.000; UVs 294 copied / 0 synthesised across all three paths) | 2026-07-27 |
| RN-6 | **The near voxel mesh draws ONLY what the heightfield cannot express, and it imports the terrain's COLOUR but not its LIGHT** | Two surfaces exist by construction and are allowed to: /core's 1 m solidity shell and the smooth `surfaceRadius` the chunk draws (DW-26). Any face the near mesh puts on the derived surface is a second drawing of ground the chunk already drew, offset by up to half a cell diagonal, so it pokes through as cube corners. The rule makes the mesh's responsibility a property of the surface rather than of the edit sets, which is what "faces of an edit" got wrong: `levelArea` edits a scatter of cells and their faces are isolated cubes. Colour comes from `BiomePalette` so cut rock and the hillside are one substance; light stays `Headlamp`'s, because the terrain program ignores three's light list and shading the mesh with it silently disabled the headlamp | **Accepted, shipped, driven-verified** (924 exposed -> 20 drawn; pad-vs-ground 33.6% -> 7.6%; lamp lift 3.46x -> 11.5x) | 2026-07-26 |

## 4. Architecture & approach
- **Scaled space transition:** maintain two representations per body, a far proxy (low-poly + baked) rendered by the scaled camera, and near streamed terrain. As the observer enters a body's approach band, cross-fade proxy→terrain; floating-origin keeps near terrain at small coords. The handoff is the "no loading screen" moment.
- **Depth:** log **or cascaded** depth in the near camera only (RN-2); the scaled camera uses plain depth at its own scale; the two are composited, not depth-merged (near always over scaled). Spike 1 measures UE's reversed-Z float first, cascaded preferred over `SV_Depth` (Nanite-compat). See [spike1-rendering §3](../spikes/spike1-rendering.md).
- **Factory LOD ladder (conceptual, not built before Phase 1):** (0) full instanced meshes + animated items near; (1) instanced machines, items as scrolling material far; (2) machines as impostors, no items; (3) not rendered, sim is on-rails anyway ([core-engine](core-engine.md) SimProxy). LOD band ties to the same active/on-rails distance bands. **Nanite's intended home** (RN-5).
- **Atmosphere:** UE5 **Sky Atmosphere** component (Rayleigh/Mie, surface→space fade-to-black out of the box) driven by camera altitude + sun direction + `FAtmosphereProfile` from [world-gen](world-gen.md) (D-006). Custom analytic LUT is a Phase-1 fallback. Forge only; Cinder airless. See [spike1-rendering §4](../spikes/spike1-rendering.md).

## 5. Interfaces & dependencies

### Published this pass (RN-1200): `self.__ofMachineMat`, and one line that is now a CONTRACT

`state()` (enabled / flagPresent / mode / bareOn / bareFlagPresent / bare / baseRoughness /
baseMetalness / baked / roles) and `table()` (the per-ROLE rows `PartMaterial` actually
wrote, plus **`distinct`**, `injections` and `missing`). `distinct` is the discriminating
field and it tells the three states apart with one number: **0** under `?machinemat=0`,
exactly **1** under `?machinemat=flat`, and **17** across the 18 shipped machine roles under
the default. `table()` is also the ONLY reachable read of `partMatState()` on this path,
because `SpiderFlock.partMatStats` needs a flock; without it the anchor-miss failure mode
would have no read-out in a machine frame at all.

**`MachineBatch.makeMaterial`'s `metalness: 0.45, roughness: 0.55` are now an interface, not
an implementation detail.** `tools/blender/render_machines.py:326` regex-reads them as
numeric literals and raises rather than guess. They must stay literals in that constructor;
`MachineMat.assertMachineBase` throws at boot if they and `MachineMat`'s copy disagree.
Changing the machine base is therefore a two-file act with a third-party consumer, and it
needs an Admin-logged decision like any other published interface.

### Published this pass (RN-845): `window.__ofBodies`, the second body's driven surface

`report()` (present / reason / drawn / **refusedId** / texW / texH / bakeMs / oracleSamples /
uvResidual / **eyeM** / simSecs / per-body distanceM, angularDiamDeg, posM, texelM, relief
min-max, and an `optics` record READ BACK OFF THE LIVE UNIFORMS rather than recomputed),
`aim()` (yawDeg / pitchDeg exactly as `of.look` takes them, elevationDeg, angularDiamDeg,
distanceM, aboveHorizon), `planetshine()` (onGround and onBody, both as a fraction of the
sun's irradiance, plus a Rec.709 luma so a lighting lane does not re-derive one),
`facts()`, `airProfile(id)`, `setRelief` / `setDetail` / `setDebug` / `setTimeS`, and
`setFov` (which is `CameraRig.setFov`, present since W1 and never called by anything;
**a zoomed frame has a different shadow-LOD ladder, so no triangle, draw-call or LOD
number may be taken from one**).

Flags, all registered in `run.mjs`'s PAGE_PARAMS in the same commit: `?skybodies=0`
(structural control, nothing is constructed), `?skybodyrelief=`, `?skybodydetail=`,
`?skybodytex=`, `?skybodytime=`.

### Consumed from physics (PH-161), and this is the whole of it

`_of_body_state(bodyId, simTimeS)` -> 6 f64 in the PARENT's frame, and
`_of_body_facts(bodyId)` -> 4 f64 `[radiusM, muM3S2, soiRadiusM, orbitPeriodS]`. Both are
symbol-detected; a client on an older wasm reports what it is missing and draws nothing.
**No number about a body's position or size appears anywhere else in the render tree**, and
if one ever does it is a bug: that is the whole point of `render/CelestialEphemeris.ts`.

**Depends on (inbound), Spike-1 contracts now PINNED (code against these, not the prose):**
- **core-engine** ([spike1-core-engine.md §5](../spikes/spike1-core-engine.md)): `FUniverseCoord`+`FFrameId` & `ToEngine/FromEngine`/`FFloatingOrigin`; `FReferenceFrame`/`IFrameGraph` (`ToUniverse(SimTime)` for body/star positions); `ISimProxy.Position()/Velocity()`; `ISimClock.Alpha()/TickIndex()`. **Events: `OnOriginRebased(DeltaEngine, NewOrigin)`** (re-anchor near scene + atmosphere transform; scaled scene untouched) and **`OnSOIChange(FSOIChangeEvent)`** (re-target approach body). A `UniverseCoord` carries its frame, never a bare `FVector`.
- **world-gen** ([spike1-worldgen.md §4–§5](../spikes/spike1-worldgen.md)): `FTerrainChunk` (center as `FUniverseCoord`, chunk-local positions, skirts, `MaterialId`); `ITerrainProvider::OnChunkReady`/`OnChunkEvicted`/`UpdateStreaming`; `FBodyParams`/`FAtmosphereProfile` (we consume radius/atmosphere, D-006, hardcode nothing). Re-project chunk transforms on `OnOriginRebased` via `CenterUniverse.ToEngine`.
- **physics** (later): entity transforms (interpolated) for vehicles/parts.
- **factory-sim** ([spike3-factory-sim.md §6](../spikes/spike3-factory-sim.md)): the **factory→render stream, PINNED by factory-sim, CONFIRMED here (RC-8), now EMITTED + numerically validated headlessly (factory-sim FS-14: `EmitEntityStates`/`EmitBeltFlowStates`/`GetLineItems`)**. `FFactoryEntityState` (~32B/visible entity: `Id`,`TypeId`,`Position` as `UniverseCoord`,`FQuat16` orient, `VisualState`,`AnimPhase`,`Lod` hint,`Flags`), `FFactoryBeltFlowState` (per visible line: `ItemTypeDominant`,`FlowSpeedQuant`,`Density`,`Compressed`), and on-demand `GetLineItems(LineId)→{itemType,unitOffset}[]`, **the only O(items) call, pulled ONLY at RN-3 LOD-0**. Stream is **delta-only**, drained at render FPS, transforms interpolated via `ISimClock::Alpha()`. Belts emit `FFactoryBeltFlowState` only on flow-state *change* (a steady belt is silent). We evaluate items' world placement via the sim's baked `pathUnitToWorld` (sim never evaluates it; only we do, only for LOD-0 items). **See RC-8 resolution below + §5.4 factory-LOD-ladder mapping.**
**Provides to (outbound):** the rendered frame; camera/observer transform feedback for LOD/AOI; screenshot/observation hooks (useful to [networking](networking.md) AOI tuning).
**Open contract gaps flagged to Admin (Spike 1):**
- `FAtmosphereProfile` has Rayleigh fields but **no Mie params**, request world-gen add `MieScaleHeightM`/`MieScatteringScale`/`MieAnisotropy` (non-breaking; D-006-owned by world-gen). Placeholder Mie used meanwhile.
- UE5 Sky Atmosphere renders **only one atmosphere on screen at once**, fine now (only Forge has one), a constraint for the multi-atmospheric-body future.
**~~Still to negotiate later~~ → NEGOTIATED & CONFIRMED:** the factory→render stream schema (fields, update rate) was pinned by factory-sim Spike 3 §6 and is **confirmed sufficient for RN-3 here (RC-8, below)**, with one *non-breaking* field-add requested (`AABB`/bounds for culling; see RC-8 §4).
